findings.claim: Loss classification of v12's 71 Gold losses: 42 HP races at the limit and 29 queen deaths; losses concentrate against opponents rated >=20, deaths concentrate on seat 1, starting HP and game length do not separate loss types.
findings.numbers: Of 180 games (our csv rows): wins 109 (73 races, 34 kills, 2 opponent removed), losses 71 (42 races, 29 deaths). By opponent ratingAtFetch: <14: S 0.86 (6/7; 0 lost races, 1 death); 14-17: 0.77 (23/30; 1 lost race, 6 deaths); 17-20: 0.68 (58/85; 17 lost races, 10 deaths); 20-23: 0.39 (22/57; 23 lost races, 12 deaths); >=23: 0/1. Seat 0: S 0.67 (54/81), 18 lost races, 9 deaths; seat 1: S 0.56 (55/99), 24 lost races, 20 deaths -> death rate 11% vs 20%, lost-race rate 22% vs 24%. Start HP (trace turn 0, equal for both queens in all 180 games): median 60 in all groups (lost races 60, deaths 60, wins 60); S by bucket <=40: 0.60 (27/45), 41-70: 0.58 (45/78), >70: 0.65 (37/57). Deaths by turn: 5 before t100, 10 in t100-174, 14 in t175-249; median death turn 172 (v11: 134). Opponent trained giants in 35/180 games; S there 0.66 (23/35) vs 0.59 without.
findings.evidence: features-v12-gold.csv (rank, deathTurn, turns), manifests arena-6860036/6860166-games-2026-11-07.json (ratingAtFetch), ours-upload-01/02.txt turn-0 hp; script q1_classify.py.

findings.claim: The 29 deaths are knight deaths next to our own towers, not deaths in the open or to enemy towers: in the last 30 turns 879 of 890 HP lost came from knights; she died within 130 of an own tower in 28 of 29 cases, with 2-6 towers standing; the typical death is a 10-57-turn siege she kites around her towers while losing 1-5 HP per turn.
findings.numbers: Last-30-turn windows of the 29 deaths (870 turns): kd 879, td 9, other 2. Where she died: touching an own tower 16/29, open but nearT<=130 in 12/29, at a non-tower site 1/29 (nearT 208); nearT at death median 108. Own towers at death: T4 9, T3 7, T5 6, T2 4, T6 2, T1 1; ladder complete (T>=6 and B>=2) in only 1/29; barracks B1 in 18/29, B2 10, B0 1. Command classes in the windows: kite 458 turns (523 HP lost), buildwalk 144 (47 HP), topup 120 (164 HP = 1.37 HP/turn), flee 51 (122 HP = 2.4 HP/turn), move 51 (0), newtower 22 (33), mine 19 (0). Consecutive turns with an enemy knight within 250 right before death (kRun): median 10, >=20 in 11/29 (max 57). K250 in the window: mean median 2.4, max median 5 (up to 11). HP 30 turns before death median 23 (>=20 in 18/29, >=30 in 10/29); 10 turns before: median 13. Example 918143669: 11 consecutive BUILD-TOWER top-ups at site 1 (t201-211) with 7-10 knights within 250, losing 4-5 HP per turn (46 HP in 'topup' turns), opponent income 25.
findings.evidence: ours-upload-01/02.txt windows, command classification by counter tracking (tracelib.annotate); q2_deaths.py -> q2_out.txt, deaths.json.

findings.claim: Deaths are economic collapses, not queen-tactics failures: near death the opponent's income is 2-4x ours, our mines are gone (torn down by passing knights or exhausted), we have one barracks and no waves, so the siege never lifts.
findings.numbers: At death (trace, income = max positive gold delta over 8 turns): opponent income median 9, ours 2; opponent >= 2x ours in 23/29, >= 3x in 20/29; our income <= 2 in 18/29. Our mines at death: M1 15/29, M0 6/29, M2 8/29 (<=1 in 21/29); opponent mines median 3 (>=4 in 14/29), towers 4, barracks 2. csv at the last fixed turn before death: opponent income median 8, opponent knights alive median 4. Trainings per death game: ours 6.3 vs opponent 11.6 (gold drops). Mine losses over all 180 games: 552 M-drops (3.1/game); 51% (280/552) happened with an enemy knight within 500 of our queen vs a 36% base rate of such turns (knights touching an enemy mine destroy it, Rules.java line 252). Mines built per game median: ours 4, opponents 6; opponent max income in death games median ~10 vs ours ~5 (csv maxIncome).
findings.evidence: opp-upload-01/02.txt gold deltas and T/M/B, features-v12-gold.csv (inc_t, knights_t, minesBuilt, maxIncome), Rules.java lines 246-263; q2_deaths.py, q5_extra.py. The numbers are solid; the causal reading is medium-confidence because site gold is not in the traces, so exhausted and torn-down mines cannot be separated.

findings.claim: Death mechanisms by criteria: 6 early deaths (<=t106, 5 of them on seat 1), 9 sieges (knight within 250 for >=20 turns to the end; opponent income 6-25 vs ours 0-2; balanced by seat), 8 attrition deaths (<=16 HP already 30 turns before death; 6 of 8 seat 1), 6 mid-game collapses; in 10 of 29 deaths the enemy queen was at <=20 HP when we died (<=30 in 19/29).
findings.evidence: deaths.json, q5_out.txt. Counts are exact; the group boundaries are chosen thresholds.

findings.claim: TRAIN_SYNC starves the army whenever two barracks stand and income is low: 21% of all our turns are spent holding 80-159 gold with two idle-able barracks and no training; the hold lasts 20-90 turns at income <=2; it left gold unspent at the end of 23 of 42 lost races and held waves while the enemy queen stood at <=20 HP in 5 losses.
findings.numbers: Over 38252 turns of 180 games: 8160 turns with gold >= 80, a barracks standing and no training; 8082 of them with B >= 2 and 80 <= gold < 160 (the sync hold) = 21% of all turns and 48% of the 16928 turns with B >= 2 (B >= 2 reached in 132/180 games). Starvation streaks (>= 20 consecutive such turns): 219 (1.22/game, 37 turns/game, 6652 turns = 17% of all); by income at the time: <= 2: 68 streaks, 3-4: 135, >= 5: 16; longest 80 turns (918167057, income 1, lost race by 9), 71, 67, 67, 67, 65 (918159459, death), 55 (918167279, death). Trainings per game: ours 7.3 vs opponents 10.9 (won 7.2 vs 10.8; lost races 8.2 vs 10.9; deaths 6.3 vs 11.6); gold drops are mostly single releases (~74-78 gold), double releases (~156-157) about 1 in 10. Gold at the end of lost races: median 89, >= 80 in 23/42 (won races: median 66, >= 80 in 25/73). Lost races within 9 HP ending with >= 80 gold and B2: 918158655 (gap -1, 83), 918165015 (-1, 162, last training t208), 918169416 (-1, 132, t231), 918145702 (-3, 102), 918146673 (-3, 145, t201), 918149783 (-5, 96), 918148960 (-8, 95), 918158656 (-8, 119, no training after t150 at income 1 with B2), 918143673 (-9, 105), 918152187 (-9, 144). Kill-shot turns (enemy queen <= 20 HP, our gold >= 80, B >= 2, no training that turn): 1281 turns in 37 games; in losses: 918145702 73 turns (lost race by 3), 918167279 55 (death; enemy at 10 HP, our gold 147, 100 turns since the last wave at income 1), 918148596 16 (death; enemy 17 HP, gold 129, 44 turns since the last wave), 918150876 9 (lost race), 918150968 6 (death; enemy 13 HP, gold 104). The enemy queen dropped to <= 20 HP and survived in 37 games: 23 won races, 10 deaths, 4 lost races.
findings.evidence: Gold series in ours-upload-01/02.txt (training = gold drop; income = positive delta), opp-upload hp series, MainBot.train() (TRAIN_SYNC: nothing trains while any barracks trains or gold < 80 x idle barracks), Params.java TRAIN_SYNC comment (on since v06); q3_close.py, q5_extra.py, q6_verify.py, q7_seat_killshot.py. The hold and its size are high-confidence; how much damage a released wave would land is medium (their towers T4-T9 in those games).

findings.claim: Lost races are lost early and by army ineffectiveness: we take 3x the first-wave damage of won races, our knights deal a third of the damage, and when trailing the last 50 turns drift further against us (while the walks out themselves cost almost nothing).
findings.numbers: 42 lost races vs 73 won races, HP lost per game by period (ours): t0-45 10.1 vs 3.2, t46-100 5.6 vs 3.2, t101-200 6.7 vs 5.7, t201-250 4.3 vs 0.8; total 26.8 vs 12.9. By class (lost races): kite 16.5, buildwalk 3.7, topup 3.1, flee 2.0, newtower 1.3; enemy tower damage 1.90/game vs 0.12 in won races. Their HP lost per game: 10.5 in lost races (5.9 of it by t45; only 4.6 over t46-250) vs 31.3 in won races (13.7 by t45). Final gap minus gap at t200: mean -3.6 in lost races (11 games worse, 7 better, 24 unchanged) vs +3.5 in won races (36 better, 7 worse). Late (t>200) walking/building turns: 14.0/game in lost races vs 1.7 in won (LATE_HOLD applies only when ahead), but HP lost during those turns only 0.33/game. First-wave differential (our loss - theirs, t<=45) >= the final gap in 5/42 lost races (918146673 24 vs 0, gap -3; 918152187 15 vs 2, -9; 918145824 28 vs 6, -10; 918143673 8 vs 0, -9; 918158655 30 vs 23, -1). Within 5 HP: 10/42; within 10: 18/42; median gap -13, mean -16.3.
findings.evidence: ours/opp-upload traces per period and class; q3_close.py -> q3_out.txt.

findings.claim: Enemy tower damage is small overall but comes almost entirely from standing at own towers that sit inside an enemy tower's range (top-ups, home walks, flights), and it decided one lost race outright.
findings.numbers: Over 180 games: 192 turns with an enemy tower covering our queen (24 games), 114 HP lost to towers in total (2.7% of the 4156 HP we lost; knights 4038). eTow turns by class: topup 105, buildwalk 31, home 22, kite 13, flee 11, newtower 7, mine 2, barracks 1 -> 138/192 at own towers. Games with td >= 5: 9 (918168604 td 40, lost race by 68: 40 eTow turns t175-235, 24 of them touching site 22; 918146139 td 18, 27 turns topping up site 0; 918160015 td 10 (death); 918150190 td 7 = the whole gap (-7) on seat 0, where equal HP is scored as a player-0 win; 918167279 td 7 (death); 918167057 td 6 (lost race by 9); 918150491, 918158657, 918158658 td 5).
findings.evidence: eTow/td fields of ours-upload traces; docs/rules/inferred.md on equal-score ranking; q4_anomalies.py, q5_extra.py.

findings.claim: Seat asymmetry is a death asymmetry and it is reproduced locally with identical bots: seat 1 dies about twice as often with the same first-wave setup, which points at the referee's processing order (or a coordinate-dependent bot quirk), not at opponent strength.
findings.numbers: Arena v12: deaths 20/99 on seat 1 vs 9/81 on seat 0; lost races 24/99 vs 18/81; v11 (csv): deaths 16/86 vs 9/94; pooled 36/185 (19.5%) vs 18/175 (10.3%), chi-square 5.0, p ~0.025. By death group: early 5/6 seat 1, attrition 6/8, mid collapse 5/6, siege 4/9. Opponent rating medians by seat equal (19.65 vs 19.72). Arena first wave by seat (WaveTrace summary, 176 games): identical contact turn 26, 4 knights within 500 at contact, 2 towers, cover 2, kills 6 in both seats, but our HP lost to knights in 20 turns mean 8.4 (median 4) on seat 1 vs 5.0 (median 3) on seat 0; trace t<=45 loss mean 7.9 vs 4.6. Local eval benches (M/replays/bench/exp-2026-11-07-meet-back/eval, seeds 2001000000+397i, 2000 maps x 2 seats): mirror v12 vs v12: P0 wins 2100, P1 1626, draws 274 (seat-0 S 0.559); deaths P0 150 vs P1 310; direct v12 vs v11: deaths P0 175 vs P1 272, v12 S 0.600 on seat 0 vs 0.543 on seat 1; rival-ctrl: deaths of botA 163 seat 0 vs 255 seat 1; field-cand 59 vs 91.
findings.evidence: q1 tables, features-v11-gold.csv, M/replays/study/gold-v12-2026-11-07/waves/summary.csv, bench eval JSON games[] (aSeat, winner, score<=0 read as death); q6_verify.py, q7_seat_killshot.py. The effect itself is high-confidence (4000 mirror games); its cause is unknown (low confidence on any mechanism).

findings.claim: Trace anomalies: no stalls and almost no target oscillation remain; the queen spends 29% of her turns idly topping up with no knight within 500; towers decay away at 1.4 per game; standing to top up while swarmed costs more per turn than kiting.
findings.numbers: Stalls (>= 3 turns same BUILD, no movement, not touching): 0 in 180 games. Oscillation (A,B,A targets in 3 turns): 4 events in 4 games. Idle pumping (topup, K500 = 0): 11154 of 38252 turns (29%), 62 turns/game (won 68, lost races 72, deaths 24), longest run median 13.5, max 136. Home walks (BUILD to an own tower with no threat): 1256 turns in 118 games. Tower losses (T decreases): 256 events in 112 games (giants trained against us in only 35 games). Ladder complete (T>=6, B>=2) in 88/180 games at median turn 121 (never in 13 lost races and 27 deaths). HP lost while topping up under threat: 496 over 180 games (548 turns, 0.9 HP/turn); in death windows topup 1.37 HP/turn, flee 2.4 HP/turn, kite 1.14 HP/turn.
findings.evidence: q4_anomalies.py -> q4_out.txt, per_game.json; q2_out.txt.

levers.lever: Release knights despite TRAIN_SYNC when the sync wait is hopeless or pointless: (a) cap the hold (if one barracks is idle, gold >= 80 and reaching 80 x idle barracks would take more than N turns at the current income, train from one barracks), (b) release on a kill shot (enemy queen HP <= X and gold >= 80), (c) spend everything from about turn 230 (gold is worthless at 250).
levers.lossMode: HP race last 50 turns; queen death with the enemy queen low; vs strong opponents (their continuous waves vs our 40-90-turn holds)
levers.mechanism: MainBot.train(): with TRAIN_SYNC=1 nothing trains while gold < 80 x idle barracks; with two barracks and income 1-2 the 80->160 wait is 40-80 turns. Evidence: 8082 turns (21% of all) held with 80-159 gold and B>=2; 219 streaks >= 20 turns (68 at income <= 2); gold >= 80 at the end in 23/42 lost races; 1281 kill-shot turns in 37 games, 5 of them losses (918145702 -3, 918167279, 918148596, 918150968 deaths with the enemy at 10-17 HP and 104-147 gold).
levers.estimatedGain: Upper bound 8 of 180 games (5 lost races within 3 HP with >= 80 gold left, 3 close deaths with >= 100 gold and two barracks) = +4.4 pp; realistic 2-4 games (+1-2 pp) because the released 4 knights must pass their towers (T4-T9 in those games). Also a possible general gain from 20-40% more waves per game that cannot be sized from traces.
levers.measurability: Yes: the mirror (91% races; both sides hoard identically, so the candidate's extra waves show as HP), field (income 8, 4 towers at 600: tests whether 4-knight releases survive towers) and rival (kiting). Report trainings per game and gold at the end alongside S. Risk: v06 adopted sync waves as a positive, so variant (a) should keep the 8-knight wave when the wait is short (N ~15-20 turns) and only break it when the wait is long.
levers.effort: flag on existing rule (3 small variants in train(): SYNC_WAIT_MAX, SYNC_KILL_HP, DUMP_FROM)

levers.lever: Explain and then fix the seat-1 death excess: trace local mirror games by seat (DeathTrace/WaveTrace on seat-1 deaths vs seat-0), compare with the referee's processing order (collision order own creeps then queen by players, BUILD parity, creep processing order), then either a seat-aware parameter (e.g., meet the first wave further back or kite earlier on seat 1) or a general fix of whatever the seat-1 queen does differently.
levers.lossMode: queen death (early and attrition deaths: 16 of the 20 seat-1 deaths are early/attrition/mid-collapse) and HP race first wave (seat 1 loses 8.4 vs 5.0 HP to the first wave with an identical setup)
levers.mechanism: Unknown; the effect exists with identical bots (mirror: 310 vs 150 deaths in 4000 games, P0 S 0.559) and on the arena (20/99 vs 9/81 deaths; v11 16/86 vs 9/94). The bot's rules are coordinate-symmetric except rounding, so the referee's order of resolution is the prime suspect; the local Rules port reproduces it, so it can be studied locally without the arena.
levers.estimatedGain: If seat-1 deaths fell to the seat-0 rate (11% -> 11 of 99 instead of 20): up to 9 games of 180 (+5 pp) and ~1 rating point on the arena (v01's seat gap was ~1.1 points); realistic a third to a half of that. Unmeasured upside: any fix also helps the first-wave HP race on seat 1.
levers.measurability: Strong local signal: the eval bench already records aSeat, winner and score per game; a candidate is judged by the mirror's per-seat death count (310 vs 150 is far outside noise) and per-seat S, plus the usual G0-G5. New diagnostics needed first (seat-split DeathTrace of local mirror games).
levers.effort: new analysis (1 study) then flag on existing rules; a rules-order fix in the bot's physics prediction would be a new subsystem

levers.lever: Never top up, flee to or walk home to an own tower that stands inside an enemy tower's range; pick the next own tower or stay.
levers.lossMode: HP race midgame (enemy tower damage) and a few deaths
levers.mechanism: The touch rule (top-up), rule 4 (flee to the nearest own tower) and rule 6 (walk to the home tower) ignore enemy tower coverage of the target; 138 of 192 enemy-tower turns were at own towers (topup 105, home 22, flee 11). Known backlog quirk, now sized.
levers.estimatedGain: Small: 114 HP over 180 games; 1 lost race flips (918150190, td 7 = gap, seat 0 so equal HP wins), 918167057 (-9, td 6) and two deaths (td 7-10) only partially; ~1 game of 180 (+0.5 pp).
levers.measurability: Weak locally: needs opponents whose towers overlap ours (field/rival build 4 towers, some forward); measure td per game in the bench's traces rather than S; a regression test for the quirk is cheap.
levers.effort: flag on existing rules (exclude underEnemyTower targets in the three rules)

levers.lever: Keep the economy alive under siege: deaths are decided by income collapse (M <= 1 in 21/29, our income <= 2 in 18/29, opponent 2-4x), so the upstream lever is a mine rebuild/replace rule that runs in the tower phase when income <= 2 and no knight is within ~500, preferring sites behind our towers, plus not topping up a tower while a free gold site near home is unmined.
levers.lossMode: queen death (sieges and attrition) and HP race vs strong opponents
levers.mechanism: The ladder rebuilds mines only while income < 3 and threat == 0 and it ranks the tower cap ahead of income once 3 is reached; under repeated waves she never gets to rebuild, and 29% of all turns go to idle top-ups. 552 mine losses in 180 games, 51% with knights within 500 of the queen (base 36%). New evidence vs the tried INCOME_LATE: the deaths, not the races, carry the income collapse; INCOME_LATE was judged on S vs mirror/field where deaths are rarer.
levers.estimatedGain: Uncertain; the 9 sieges and 8 attrition deaths (17/180) are the pool, but a mine rebuilt under siege is torn down again unless placed behind towers; 2-5 games plausible, could also cost HP races if the walks expose her.
levers.measurability: Partly: rival (giants, kiting) and field (income 8) exert late pressure; the mirror does not. Judge by deaths per game and income at t150/t200 in addition to S. The panel lacks Gold's strong-economy queens (brief).
levers.effort: new rule (mine rebuild conditions and site preference), moderate

levers.lever: Observation, not a proposal as is: standing to top up while swarmed costs 1.37 HP/turn in death windows (164 HP in 120 turns) vs kiting 1.14; STAND_REACH already failed, so only a tower-cluster-aware flee (move to the point covered by the most own towers rather than the nearest tower) would be new.
levers.lossMode: queen death (sieges)
levers.mechanism: kite() returns null when no step gains >= 5 under cover; the touch rule then tops up; rule 4 flees to the nearest tower in a straight line (flee turns 2.4 HP/turn, 122 HP in death windows). Coverage count at death is not in the DeathTrace, so the size of the cluster effect is unknown.
levers.estimatedGain: Unknown; sieges are 9/180 games and most are lost on economy anyway; likely <= 2 games.
levers.measurability: Mirror and rival produce sieges rarely (91% of mirror games reach t250); would need a death-focused metric (deaths per 1000 games) rather than S.
levers.effort: new rule in kite()/flee (coverage-weighted target); needs a coverage diagnostic first

result.caveats: Sample: 180 arena games, 71 losses, 29 deaths; counts of 5-10 games carry roughly +/-50% uncertainty and the mechanism groups use chosen thresholds (early <= t106, siege kRun >= 20, attrition hp30 <= 16). Command classes come from the DeathTrace alone: own-tower sites are tracked by T/M/B counter changes, so a decayed tower that is rebuilt can misclassify a 'buildwalk' as 'flee/home' (rare); 'topup' is a BUILD TOWER on the touched own tower. Income is estimated from positive gold deltas (max over 8 turns); turns with a training hide the income; the csv inc_t values were used as a cross-check at fixed turns. Opponent ratings are ratingAtFetch, not at game time. Enemy knights alive are only known at the fixed csv turns; K250/K500 are counts around our queen. The seat effect's cause is not established; the local evidence is from the eval bench JSON (deaths read as score <= 0; 4000 mirror games on seeds 2001000000+397i) and the WaveTrace summary (176 games). Equal-HP scoring as a player-0 win is taken from docs/rules/inferred.md. Lever sizes are upper bounds from 'games that would flip if the HP had not been lost/had been dealt', not simulations; whether released knights reach a tower-covered enemy queen is untested. v11 traces were not analysed beyond the csv comparison (deaths 25 vs 29, races 44 vs 42, death turn median 134 vs 172). Tower HP/range, coverage at death and site gold are not in the traces and would need a replay of the recorded games.

findings.evidence: Sums of the DeathTrace kd/td/loss columns over 50-turn windows of ours-upload-0{1,2}.txt and opp-upload-0{1,2}.txt (scratchpad/midgame/analyze.out, section 1); the cumulative gaps -4.64/-8.52/-8.79/-12.69 reproduce the brief's t50/t100/t150/t200 means.

findings.claim: Over turns 50-249 the swing between lost and won races is two thirds 'their queen stops bleeding' and one third 'ours bleeds more'; the extra -4 in P2 and in P4 is each about +2 HP more lost by our queen and 2.8-4.2 HP less taken by theirs.
findings.numbers: Turns 50-249 per game, lost races: our loss 16.17 (kd 14.24, td 1.90), their loss 4.48 (kd 4.21, td 0.26); won races: ours 9.42 (kd 9.30, td 0.12), theirs 17.08 (kd 16.53, td 0.55). Lost minus won: ours +6.75, theirs -12.60. By phase (lost minus won): P2 our kd +2.00, their kd -2.75; P4 our kd +2.08, our td +0.61, their kd -4.20; P5 our kd +2.55, our td +1.00, their kd -3.79.

findings.claim: The opponents who win HP races against v12 are not the economy players but the queen-safe ones: our knights reach their queen about as often but do almost no damage because she stays within 150 of a tower.
findings.numbers: Lost-race opponents vs won-race opponents: maxIncome mean 7.7 vs 8.3, mean income 3.53 vs 4.19, knight trainings 11.0 vs 12.9, giants trained in 8 of 42 vs 19 of 73 games, towers at t200 5.9 vs 5.8, summed tower HP at t200 median 2800 vs 2608. Our knights' contact episodes on their queen (turns 50-249): 163 (3.88/game) vs 337 (4.62/game); kd per episode 1.09 (73% with 0) vs 3.58 (43% with 0); their queen within 150 of an own tower for the whole episode in 76% vs 55%; episodes starting >150 from a tower 11% vs 22%; kd per contact turn by phase P2..P5 0.24/0.43/0.31/0.23 vs 0.45/0.67/0.77/0.92. Knight lifetime (knightTurns/(4*trainK)) equal: ours 11.4 vs 11.3 turns, theirs 11.1 vs 10.9.
findings.evidence: deep.out (contact episodes, waves), deep2.out ('their queen under our knights'), features-v12-gold.csv columns maxIncome/meanIncome/trainK/trainG/towers_200/thp_200 joined in games.json. The observations are direct; the explanation (tower cover and position) is inferred and only medium confidence.

findings.claim: Our extra midgame HP loss comes from enemy waves that catch our queen while she walks the ladder (mostly to rebuild mines); a wave met at her tower costs a third as much.
findings.numbers: Lost races, turns 50-249: 258 contact episodes (K250>0 runs), 153 (59%) began while she walked: walk_mine 79 episodes/266 kd, walk_tower 38/93, walk_barracks 22/80, route_move 13/17, walk_home_tower 1/0; these cost 456 of 598 kd (76%; 10.86 HP/game; 2.98/episode) vs at-tower episodes 79/69 kd (0.87/episode) and building-touch 19/48. Won races: walking 248 of 473 episodes, 420 of 679 kd (62%; 5.75/game; 1.69/episode); at tower 180/141 (0.78/episode). By phase: P2 lost walking 56 eps/140 kd (3.33/game) vs won 108/131 (1.79/game); P4 lost 35/136 (3.24/game) vs won 57/80 (1.10/game) = the whole P2/P4 excess of our kd (+2.00/+2.08). At equal wave size (max K250 in the episode) walking costs more: maxK3 3.45 kd vs 1.22 at tower (lost), 1.96 vs 1.41 (won); maxK4 7.24 vs 6.00, 6.80 vs 1.91; maxK2 0.41 vs 0.07, 0.31 vs 0.14. Per lost race the walking-episode kd: median 7.5, mean 10.86; 24 of 42 games >= 5 HP, 12 with 0. In the 29 queen deaths, 849 of 1306 kd in turns 50-249 came in walking-caught episodes.
findings.evidence: deep2.out (pre-contact activity = the class of the last turn before contact with no knight within 250), deep3.out (kd by max K250), flip.py output; classes from parse.py's own-tower tracking (validated: own-tower BUILD counts match CgStudy's towerTopUps in 315 of 360 game-sides, 213 of 76,504 turn lines differ). Heuristic pre-contact class, 3% of episodes 'unknown': medium-high rather than fully high.

findings.claim: The wave is visible before it reaches the walking queen and her nearest tower is reachable in time, so the exposure is avoidable with the information the bot already reads.
findings.numbers: Walking-caught episodes, lost races (153): turns with a knight within 500 but none within 250 right before contact: median 2, mean 2.6 (distribution 0:2, 1:24, 2:61, 3:42, 4:12, 5:5, 6+:7); nearest own tower on the pre-contact turn median 136; walking 60/turn from the first warning turn reaches touching distance (<=110 from the tower centre) before contact in 141 of 153 episodes (92%) carrying 329 of 456 kd (won races 237 of 248, 335 of 420 kd; deaths 86 of 95, 641 of 849 kd). Yellow-zone turns (knight within 500, none within 250) per game in turns 50-249: 23.5 (lost), 30.8 (won), in 6.9 spells of median 8 turns (11 spells >= 20 turns in 42 lost races); on them she walks 58% (walk_mine 25%, route 12%, walk_tower 11%, walk_barracks 6%, walk_home 4%) or tops up 36%. Wave size at contact is similar for walking and at-tower episodes (K500 at start 3.64 vs 3.28; max K250 2.69 vs 2.23).
findings.evidence: deep3.out (warning time, reachability, yellow zone). Geometric estimate: knights assumed to head straight at her, no simulation.

findings.claim: The mine treadmill drives the walks: enemy waves destroy our mines on their way, the ladder reopens (income < 3), the queen walks out to a site away from her towers, the mine dies again.
findings.numbers: Lost races after t50: 157 mine losses in 42 games (3.74/game; 55% within 5 turns of an enemy contact episode), 124 rebuilt (2.95/game); median turns from a mine build to the next mine loss 18 (won races 47); walk_mine 20.8 turns/game in 7.5 walks (won 13.8 in 4.8); 104 of 124 rebuilt mines were built with the nearest own tower 151-400 away, 17 within 150; walk_mine-caught episodes cost 266 kd = 6.3 HP per lost race (44% of its P2-P5 kd) vs 104 kd = 1.4 per won race. Median own mines at t249: 1 (lost), 0 (won). Our queen's turn budget 50-249 in lost races: pump_idle 39.3, kite 34.7, topup_pass 32.9, route_move 22.9, walk_mine 20.8, walk_tower 16.6, walk_home_tower 8.7, walk_barracks 7.6 (walking 76.6 of 200 turns vs 60.8 in won races). Reference: Legend top-10 (88 games) build 6 mines, 8 upgrades, maxIncome 10 median; v12 4/5/5.
findings.evidence: deep2.out (mine treadmill), deep.out (time budget), analyze.out 4b, features-legend.csv. Mine losses are M-count drops in the trace (any cause: creeps, exhaustion, enemy queen).

findings.claim: Enemy-tower damage to our queen in lost races comes almost entirely from standing at an own tower that lies inside an enemy tower's range (idle pump, top-up, flight), a known quirk whose cost is now quantified.
findings.numbers: td after t50: 80 HP in 8 of 42 lost races (1.9/game), 9 HP in 3 of 73 won, 25 HP in 4 of 29 deaths. Cases: 918146139 18 td on 18 pump_idle/walk_home turns t159-223 at tower 0 with eTow 1 (1 HP/turn, final -23); 918168604 40 td + 23 kd on t197-234 at tower 22 under eTow 1-2 (topup_threat 20 turns, flee_tower 8, walk_mine 6; HP 63 -> 2; gap -9 at t200 -> -68); 918150190 7 td t179-185 (pump_idle 4, walk_home 2, mine_touch 1) under eTow 1, lost by 7 on seat 0; 918167057 6 td topup_pass; 918158658 5 td (pump_idle 3, topup_threat 2). Rules involved: rule 6 idle pump nearest(hx,hy, own tower) and rule 4 flight nearest(qx,qy, own tower) have no enemy-range check, while the touch rule skips a touched site under an enemy tower and falls through to them.
findings.evidence: deep.out ('Enemy tower damage' section and trace excerpts for 918168604 and 918146139); MainBot.java lines 133-136 and 175-176.

findings.claim: Turns 200-249 do not decide the lost races and a LATE_HOLD for the trailing side would save almost nothing: when trailing, the HP goes at her towers, not on walks; comebacks come only from waves catching their queen.
findings.numbers: 115 games at the limit: 44 trailing at t200 (40 stayed lost, 4 flipped), 68 leading (67 won), 3 even. Trailing games: gap at t200 median -9.5, final -12.5; our loss 200-249 mean 3.55 (kd 2.59, td 0.98; median 0; 10 of 44 games lost any HP), of which 7 HP on 598 walking-out turns (0.16/game) and 149 HP at/near her towers (kite 78, topup_threat 42 = 21 kd + 21 td, flee_tower 18); 59 of these in 918168604 alone. Their queen lost 2.68/game (median 0; 11 of 44 games); the 4 comebacks took 38, 33, 16, 8 kd (918166775, 918147437, 918160264, 918161614), 3 of 4 with their queen caught walking (route_move). Our commands when trailing: pump_idle 32%, topup_pass 15%, walk_mine 13%, kite 10%, route_move 8%; our gold held 79 mean (TRAIN_SYNC waits for 160; income ~3 -> one release per ~50 turns); our knights within 250 of their queen 3.3 turns/game (28 of 44 games). Leading side (LATE_HOLD active): our loss 1.15/game, theirs 3.40.
findings.evidence: analyze.out section 5 (per-game table included); deep2.out comebacks list.

findings.claim: Contact frequency is the same in lost and won races; what differs is the cost per episode (ours) and per contact turn (theirs). Our queen kites on 9 of 10 contact turns and still loses 90% of her HP within 150 of a tower.
findings.numbers: Our contact turns per game by phase P1..P5: lost 13.3/13.3/8.9/9.7/7.2 (games with contact 42/41/31/29/22 of 42), won 9.8/13.0/10.3/7.5/4.9; their queen's: lost 9.9/4.7/3.4/3.1/2.7 (42/31/28/29/26), won 12.8/8.7/4.6/6.7/4.8. Episodes per game turns 50-249: ours 6.14 (lost) / 6.48 (won), theirs 3.88 / 4.62. Our kd per contact turn P1..P5 lost 0.80/0.36/0.21/0.43/0.47, won 0.36/0.22/0.35/0.28/0.16; theirs lost 0.61/0.24/0.43/0.31/0.23, won 1.11/0.45/0.67/0.77/0.92. Our loss turns in lost races (538, 12.8/game): 485 within 150 of an own tower (598 of 679 HP), K250 on them 0:47/1:97/2:156/3-4:215/5-8:23 turns; kd per contact turn near a tower K1 0.15 vs 0.09, K2 0.32 vs 0.22, K3 0.59 vs 0.44 (lost vs won). We MOVE on 89-90% of contact turns (mean step 62), they on 67-70% (step 52-56) and stand (<10) on 22-25%; nearest knight touching (<60) on 19% of our contact turns in lost races (13% won) vs 14% (lost) / 31% (won) of theirs.
findings.evidence: analyze.out sections 2b, 3, 6, 6b; deep.out kiting section. The numbers are direct; why we take more per knight in lost races is unexplained.

findings.claim: Opponents' queens walk twice as much as ours and top up about as often; their HP per contact turn is what separates lost from won races on their side.
findings.numbers: Their MOVE share by phase P1..P5, lost races 46.7/50.9/49.9/47.2/48.3% (ours 32.4/39.2/30.5/25.6/19.8%), won 42.6/52.0/45.7/49.3/47.6% (ours 29.5/38.9/31.0/21.3/8.4%); their top-ups per game per phase lost 11.7/14.1/13.0/15.1/15.7 (ours 13.4/12.7/16.5/23.0/22.0), won 12.6/12.8/13.0/12.4/13.0 (ours 14.7/13.3/16.1/24.9/42.4); their walks per game per phase 23-30 (ours 16-23); route_move 88.9 of 200 turns in lost races, 80.1 in won; WAIT 0-5%. On contact turns they kite 67-70%, top up 16-18%, flee 5-9%.
findings.evidence: analyze.out sections 6 and 6b; deep.out time budget.

findings.claim: Margins are thin and seat 1 needs a strict lead: a few HP would flip a quarter of the lost races, and four were lost by exactly 1 HP on seat 1.
findings.numbers: Lost races within 5 HP: 10 of 42; within 10: 18. Lost by exactly 1 HP: 918158655, 918165015, 918165136, 918169416 (all seat 1). Equal-HP finals: 918143672 and 918166983, both seat 0, both won. +2/+4/+6/+10 HP to our final HP flips 4/9/10/17 of the 42 lost races (strict lead). Saving all walking-caught kd flips 11, half of it 2. Won races within 5 HP: 17 of 73 (within 10: 30). Lost races by seat: 24 on seat 1, 18 on seat 0; won: 39/34. Lost races by opponent rating >= 20: 24 of 42 (won: 15 of 73).
findings.evidence: flip.py output; deep2.out equal-HP section; manifests arena-6860036/6860166-games-2026-11-07.json for ratings.

levers.lever: LADDER_CLEAR: pause the ladder walk and return to the nearest own tower while an enemy knight is within ~500 (after the first-wave window or once >= 2 towers stand), with a spell cap
levers.lossMode: HP race midgame (P2 and P4 excess) and queen deaths; also protects the 17 won races within 5 HP
levers.mechanism: MainBot.play rule 5 (the ladder: nextSite + RoutePlanner.plan, and the INCOME_LATE branch) gated by the existing clearOfKnights(s, qx, qy, R) (today used only by LATE_CLEAR); when not clear and an own tower exists, take rule 4's flight (BUILD nearest own tower, a top-up on arrival) instead of the walk. Kiting (rule 2), the defence rule (rule 1) and the touch rule stay at 250. Exempt while firstWaveWindow (WAVE_ANCHOR's tower must be built with the wave visible) or towers < 2; cap the pause per spell like KITE_MAX (11 spells >= 20 turns in 42 lost races). Optional refinement: prefer the own tower away from the knights' centroid over the nearest.
levers.estimatedGain: Walking-caught episodes cost 10.86 HP per lost race (456 of 598 kd in turns 50-249) and 5.75 per won race. Re-costed at the at-tower rate per max-K250 they would have cost ~192 HP less over the 42 lost races (~4.6 HP/game) and ~171 less over 73 won races (~2.3); +4..+6 HP flips 9-10 of 42 lost races (~5-6 of 180 games, ~3 pp) before any effect on the 29 deaths, where 849 of 1306 P2-P5 kd came in walking-caught episodes (641 with the tower reachable). Cost side: 23.5 yellow-zone turns/game (12% of turns 50-249) of ladder delay in ~7 spells of ~8 turns.
levers.measurability: Yes: the mirror (G1; 91% of mirror games are HP races and v12 sends 8-knight waves across the ladder), field (G4; income 8 means more waves) and rival (G5) all produce 'caught walking' episodes. Watch G4: fewer towers/mines from the delay would show there first.
levers.effort: Flag on existing rules (~15 lines: a parameter, a gate before the ladder branch, a cap counter)

levers.lever: Enemy-tower-aware flight and idle pump: never stand at an own tower inside an enemy tower's range when another own tower exists
levers.lossMode: HP race midgame/endgame (enemy-tower drip), a few queen deaths
levers.mechanism: MainBot.play rule 4 (threat flight: nearest(qx,qy, own tower)) and rule 6 (idle pump: nearest(hx,hy, own tower)) exclude own towers for which underEnemyTower(s, site) holds when an alternative exists; when the touched own tower is under an enemy tower (the touch rule already skips it) walk to the nearest own tower outside the range instead of falling through to the same tower.
levers.estimatedGain: 78-80 of the 80 td HP after t50 in 8 of 42 lost races (1.9 HP per lost race; 18 HP in 918146139 at 1/turn while idle-pumping, 40 td + 23 kd in 918168604), 25 HP in 4 of 29 deaths; by itself decides at most 1 game of 180 (918150190, lost by 7 with td 7 on seat 0). Pure waste removal, no strategic cost.
levers.measurability: Weak locally: boss/field/rival rarely place a tower covering our home tower. Treat as a P2 targeted fix (< 10% of maps change) with a regression test on the 918146139 pattern.
levers.effort: Flag on existing rule (small)

levers.lever: Mine rebuilds only under tower cover or until a turn limit (MINE_REBUILD_COVER=R / MINE_REBUILD_UNTIL=T on the mine phase of nextSite)
levers.lossMode: HP race midgame
levers.mechanism: MainBot.nextSite mine phase (income < INCOME_TARGET -> nearest free gold site to the midpoint) restricted to sites within R of an own tower (coveredByOwnTower exists, used by LATE_COVER) or skipped after turn T once the ladder was complete once; the touch rule's MINE branch unchanged.
levers.estimatedGain: walk_mine-caught episodes cost 266 kd = 6.3 HP per lost race (44% of its P2-P5 kd) vs 1.4 per won race; walk_mine 20.8 turns/game; rebuilt mines live a median 18 turns in lost races; 104 of 124 rebuilt mines were built 151-400 from the nearest tower. Trades exposure for income, which Legend has more of (6 mines, 8 upgrades, maxIncome 10 vs ours 4/5/5), so the gain is uncertain and largely subsumed by LADDER_CLEAR.
levers.measurability: Yes: knights destroy mines in all local matchups (mirror, field, rival).
levers.effort: Flag on existing rule

levers.lever: Make waves land on a queen-safe opponent: release timing by the enemy queen's exposure (distance to her nearest tower, whether she walks) or larger merged releases
levers.lossMode: HP race vs the queen-safe opponents who decide the lost races (65% of the P2-P5 swing is their queen not bleeding)
levers.mechanism: MainBot.train release condition (TRAIN_SYNC) extended with the enemy queen's state: she MOVEs on 44-51% of turns and 64% of our contact episodes catch her walking, but within 150 of a tower (nearT median 119); RELEASE_NEAR (proximity to our barracks) already lost, so this needs a new predicate on her tower cover, or holding gold for a 16-knight release. Giants were tried (-21 pp vs rival).
levers.estimatedGain: Ceiling: their queen loses 4.48 HP in turns 50-249 of lost races vs 17.08 in won; each extra 1 kd per episode x 3.88 episodes ~ +4 HP per game. Realistic effect unknown; low confidence.
levers.measurability: Low: field never kites, rival kites but plays giants in 85% of games; neither reproduces Gold's queen-safe tower play, so the arena would have to judge it.
levers.effort: New rule or subsystem

levers.lever: NOT a lever: LATE_HOLD for the trailing side (turns 200-249)
levers.lossMode: HP race last 50 turns
levers.mechanism: Would gate the ladder walk after turn 200 when behind on HP (the mirror of the existing LATE_HOLD).
levers.estimatedGain: None measurable: in the 44 games trailing at t200 our queen lost 7 HP on 598 walking-out turns (0.16/game); the 149 other HP went at her towers (kite 78, topup_threat 42, flee 18), 59 of them in one game; 40 of 44 trailing games were already lost at t200 (median gap -9.5).
levers.measurability: n/a
levers.effort: n/a (do not build)

result.caveats: 1) Command classes come from a heuristic reconstruction of our own-tower set (built sites, HP melt model) over the DeathTrace lines, not from Rules; its own-tower BUILD count matches CgStudy's towerTopUps in 315 of 360 game-sides and 213 of 76,504 turn lines differ, so class shares can be off by well under 1 pp; 'pre-contact activity' is the class on the last turn before contact with no knight within 250 (3% 'unknown'). 2) kd/td are DeathTrace probe splits; kd+td can differ from the turn's loss by a point when removing one source moves the other (lost races P2-P5: loss 16.17 vs kd+td 16.14 per game). 3) The 'met at the tower instead' saving (192 HP over 42 lost races) re-costs walking-caught episodes at the at-tower episodes' kd per max-K250; at-tower waves are not a random sample (they passed the tower's fire first, max K250 2.23 vs 2.69), the reachability check assumes knights head straight at her and ignores sites and collisions, and no game was simulated or played, so it is an estimate of the stake, not a measured effect. 4) Phases use the trace turn index (the loss on line t is turn t's); the csv's hp_t is the HP before turn t, so the phase sums line up with the brief's t50/t100/t150/t200 checkpoints. 5) 42 lost and 73 won races give wide per-phase uncertainty; the walking-episode kd per lost race is skewed (median 7.5, mean 10.9; 7 episodes starting >350 from a tower carry 112 of 456 kd). 6) The opponents' queen classes are the same mechanical labels applied to bots with different rules; 'top-up' for them means BUILD TOWER on a touched own tower, 'walking' any MOVE or BUILD toward a site not touched. 7) The ladder-pause lever's delay cost (towers/mines built later) is not quantified here and must come from the local panel; the first-wave window exemption matters because WAVE_ANCHOR's value depends on building the anchor tower while the wave is visible. 8) The equal-HP tiebreak (player 0 first) is the observed CG behaviour, not an established rule; flip counts use a strict lead except where stated. 9) Confidence labels are constrained to high/medium/low; findings 4-6 are medium-high in substance (see their evidence text).
result.scratchFiles: All under C:/Users/garus/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/bb685f0a5e96cb91/cdd060ad-818d-46d6-8fa6-5d79a4fb541f/scratchpad/midgame/ : parse.py (parses the four DeathTrace files, classifies every queen command, joins features-v12-gold.csv and the two manifests, validates against CgStudy counts, writes games.json); validate.py (class counts vs csv); analyze.py -> analyze.out (sections 1-8: HP by source/phase, loss-turn classes, contact per phase, structure losses, turns 200-249 by HP standing with a per-game table, queen behaviour per phase, gap decomposition, one line per lost race); deep.py -> deep.out (P2-P5 sums, contact episodes, waves and knight lifetime, kiting quality, kd by K250 x tower distance, enemy-tower damage cases with trace excerpts for 918168604 and 918146139, close lost races, time budgets); deep2.py -> deep2.out (pre-contact activity of every episode, walking episodes by walk type, queen depth, mine treadmill, late episodes on their queen, equal-HP finals, episode-level cover for both queens, P2/P4 pre-contact split); deep3.py -> deep3.out (warning time and tower reachability, yellow-zone turns, kd by distance at contact, kd by max K250 for walking vs at-tower episodes, ladder state when caught); flip.py (per lost race: gap, walking-episode kd, P1 kd, seat; flip counts for +X HP; deaths' walking share); games.json (per-turn records with classes for 180 games, both queens).

findings.claim: The seat asymmetry is a rules effect, not a bot-code effect: the live referee resolves collisions in the order [P0 creeps, Q0, P1 creeps, Q1, sites] (docs/rules/inferred.md: the only order matching 35,812 replay turns), and the referee repository's own commit that changed this order (918c375, 2018-04-28, refs/referee-csj) is titled 'Bug in collisions in favor to red queen against blue queen'; red is player 0 (Characters.kt:242 'if (owner.isSecondPlayer) "Bleu" else "Rouge"', Referee.kt:66 players[1].isSecondPlayer = true, player 0 starts at (200,200)). The fix never reached the live game.
findings.evidence: refs/referee-csj git log and Referee.kt:33-34 (commented-out old allEntities with the bug note); docs/rules/inferred.md 'Collision entity order' row (plain-turn unit match 89.69% -> 100% only with the old order); src/main/java/cr/core/Physics.java load() lines 121-128 implements that order.
findings.numbers: Commit 918c375 changes 1 file, 2 insertions, 1 deletion; our simulator matches 97/98 + 137/138 replays only with the pre-fix order.

findings.claim: Mechanism (line-by-line Python port of Physics.collisionCheck/towards/resize and Rules.moveCreep/dealDamage, 5 sub-steps with one collision pass each): when the queen is player 1 her attackers (P0 knights) are resolved among themselves before her, so the pack stays tight and all four knights hit; when she is player 0 each freshly moved enemy knight shoves her (about 4% of overlap + 1 per knight per sub-step) before the pack is resolved, she drifts and sheds half the knights. Direction confirmed in a point-symmetric two-queen setup under the live order.
findings.evidence: Direction high, magnitude in real games medium (toy has no towers). scratchpad/seat/toy_collision.py and toy_sweep.py outputs (toy_collision.txt, toy_sweep.txt).
findings.numbers: Standing queen, 4 knights, 12 turns: as P0 damage 19 (2 per turn once engaged), displaced 188; as P1 damage 36 (4 per turn), displaced 60. 15-turn sweep over 24 scenarios (wait/flee/circle x 1-2 waves x 4 angles): P1/P0 damage ratio 1.09-3.20, typical about 1.5-1.9; fleeing cuts P1 damage 48->26 and P0 25->18. Two-queen symmetric setup: Q0 takes 25, Q1 takes 48 over 15 turns.

findings.claim: The mechanism is visible on the arena in OUR queen (same code on both seats): knight damage per contact turn is about 46% higher on seat 1, the first wave costs 67% more HP on seat 1 with the same number of contact turns, and our queen dies twice as often on seat 1.
findings.evidence: DeathTrace parse (scratchpad/seat/population_seat.py, trace_stand.py) of W/replays/study/gold-v12-2026-11-08/ours-upload-0{1,2}.txt; WaveTrace M/replays/study/gold-v12-2026-11-07/waves/summary.csv and gold-2026-11-07/waves/summary.csv; features-v12-gold.csv.
findings.numbers: v12 ours: kd per contact turn (K250>0) 0.368 = 685/1859 on seat 0 (79 queens) vs 0.539 = 1362/2528 on seat 1 (98 queens); per-game means 0.348 +/- 0.030 vs 0.471 +/- 0.042; turns <=60: 0.411 (413/1004) vs 0.645 (979/1517). First wave (WaveTrace): v12 lossK20 5.01 HP (77 games) vs 8.38 (99 games) with k250Turns20 10.64 vs 11.17; v11 9.46 (87) vs 13.48 (84). Deaths: v12 ours 9/81 on seat 0 vs 20/99 on seat 1; v11 9/94 vs 16/86. Standing while a knight is adjacent (nearK<56) costs 1.85 HP/turn on seat 0 (33 turns) vs 2.73 on seat 1 (70 turns); moving while adjacent 1.20 vs 1.57.

findings.claim: Everyone on the arena shares the tilt, but its size depends on how much a bot lets knights touch queens: opponents' queens in our games also take more per contact turn on seat 1; the cg2 corpus of other players leans to player 0; the Legend top-10 corpus shows the seat-0 HP edge at turns 50-100 but no seat-0 win edge (top bots avoid contact); and our own v07 (free kiting) mirror had almost no seat edge while contact-heavy versions had a large one.
findings.evidence: population_seat.txt (opp-upload traces, features-legend.csv, features-cg2-gold.csv), docs/data/replays-cg2-2026-10-28.json and replays-legend-top-2026-10-28.json ranks, summarize_scan.txt mirrors.

findings.claim: Pooled arena seat effect over all project uploads: seat 1 lowers our win logit by 0.345 +/- 0.099 (z -3.5) after an upload fixed effect and a per-league opponent-rating slope; about -1.0 rating point in Gold units; robust to dropping referee-removed games and ties. Per league: Bronze -0.44, Silver -0.17, Gold -0.36. The opponents' mean rating is the same on both seats, so the split is not a strength confound.
findings.evidence: scratchpad/seat/arena_seat.py over all 31 docs/data/arena-*-games-*.json manifests mapped through docs/data/arena-uploads.json (output arena_seat.txt).
findings.numbers: 2070 games, 30 uploads: seat 0 730/1069 = 0.683, seat 1 614/1001 = 0.613 (gap 6.9 pp, two-proportion z 3.31); P0 share incl. opponents 0.540. Model A gamma -0.345 +/- 0.099 (cluster-robust SE 0.070); in rating points gamma/|beta|: Bronze -0.94 +/- 0.31 (slope scale 2.14), Gold -1.09 +/- 0.71 (scale 3.0), pooled via Gold slope -1.04 +/- 0.36. findings.claim: Bot code review: MainBot/RoutePlanner are point-symmetric. The home corner comes from the cached homeLeft (qx[0] < 960), the kite fan starts at atan2(qy-500, qx-960) and the route fan at the target direction (both map to themselves under point reflection), DEFENCE_FWD uses the signed x offset by side, and nearest() id tie-breaks resolve to mirrored sites because MapGen numbers each pair (2p random, 2p+1 its mirror): P0's min(2p,2q+1) mirrors P1's min(2p+1,2q). Only Math.round half-cases break symmetry (measure zero). Side effect found: the board-centre barracks target (960,500) is exactly equidistant from both sites of the nearest pair, so in a mirror both players target the SAME site (the lower, randomly placed id) and contest it; no seat bias in expectation.

levers.lever: SEAT-aware first-wave posture: when the bot is player 1 (homeLeft == false) apply DEFENCE_FWD=50 with DEFENCE_UNTIL=60 on top of v12's anchor; as player 0 keep v12 as is (the forward defence tower is cheap there because she sheds knights).
levers.lossMode: HP race first wave and queen death on seat 1 (our first-wave loss 8.38 HP vs 5.01 on seat 0; deaths 20/99 vs 9/81).
levers.mechanism: Defence rule (MainBot.play step 1): the nearest free site within 500 may lie toward the enemy; on seat 1 the arriving pack stays tight on her, so a forward tower means more contact turns at full damage. Seat is already known to the bot through homeLeft (seat 0 = top-left = player 0).
levers.estimatedGain: Dev block (500 maps, paired): DEFENCE_FWD adds +3.8 pp on seat-1 games beyond v12 in the mirror pairing (10.9 vs 7.1) and +4.1 pp vs rival, but -3.4 pp vs field; applied on seat 1 only: about +1.9 pp S vs v12-equivalent mirror, +2 pp vs rival, -1.7 pp vs field (G4 borderline). Arena: at most half the seat gap, roughly +0.2-0.3 rating points.
levers.measurability: Yes: direct vs v12 and the mirror on a fresh block, but the report must be split by seat (bench reports carry aSeat; scratchpad/seat/dev_flags_by_seat.py does the paired per-seat delta; tools/bench_pair.py does not). Gates G0-G5 as usual with G4 watched.
levers.effort: Flag on existing rules: a few lines in MainBot.play (effective params chosen by homeLeft); one new Params switch (SEAT_DEFENCE_FWD or similar).

levers.lever: Seat-aware contact rule in kite(): on seat 1 never let the queen stand (BUILD on the touched site or WAIT) while a knight is adjacent (nearK < 56); take the best cover-preserving step even when it gains less than 5. Optionally the same on seat 0 with the normal threshold.
levers.lossMode: HP race first wave / midgame on seat 1 (standing-adjacent turns cost 2.73 HP each on seat 1 vs 1.85 on seat 0).
levers.mechanism: KITE=2 returns null when no heading gains >= 5, so the touch rule tops up while the pack sits on her; the toy shows a moving queen sheds the tight seat-1 pack (48 -> 26 damage) far more than the seat-0 one (25 -> 18). STAND_REACH-155 (forced step whenever a knight is within 155) lost 2.5 pp on seat 1 on the dev block, so the trigger must be adjacency, not range.
levers.estimatedGain: Bounded by 70 standing-adjacent turns x 2.73 HP = 191 HP over 98 seat-1 games (about 2 HP per game, 14% of seat-1 knight damage); with 10 of v12's 42 lost races decided within 5 HP, perhaps 2-4 games of 180. Small but targeted.
levers.measurability: Yes: mirror and direct vs v12 by seat; DeathTrace kd per adjacent turn by stance (scratchpad/seat/trace_stand.py) as the mechanism check.
levers.effort: New rule (small) inside kite(): adjacency test plus a relaxed gain threshold when seat 1 and adjacent.

levers.lever: Seat-aware aggression on seat 0: re-read the existing dev-army and dev-waves reports by seat before any new games; if early/merged waves or a lower BARRACKS_AFTER_TOWERS pay only as player 0, make them seat-conditional.
levers.lossMode: Queen-death wins / HP race midgame vs strong opponents (opponent queens die 18/81 when we are P0 vs 16/99; mirror early kills go 80-89% to P0).
levers.mechanism: As player 0 our knights (P0 creeps) are resolved before the enemy queen, so our waves pack on her; the earlier pooled verdicts ('third/early barracks no help', RELEASE_NEAR loses) averaged a seat where the mechanism helps with one where it hurts.
levers.estimatedGain: Unknown; the seat split of past reports is free and decides whether a candidate exists. Upper bound from the mirror: death games are 11% of maps with a 68% P0 share.
levers.measurability: Yes, from existing reports first (scan_bench.json has per-report seat W/D/L; dev_flags_by_seat.py pairs by seed), then a seat-split direct/mirror run.

levers.lever: Per-seat reporting in P2 tooling: add A's score on each seat, the P0 share and seat-paired deltas to tools/bench_pair.py and the bench JSON summary; optionally score local draws with CG's tie-break (equal HP -> player 0) and let LATE_HOLD treat equal HP as ahead on seat 0 and behind on seat 1.
levers.lossMode: Measurement (all loss modes): the seat shift is 0.2-0.5 logits, larger than most candidate effects, and flags move the two seats differently (DEFENCE_FWD +2 vs +7 pp).

Local draws are 6.5-7.5% of games (identical bots) but CG ranks player 0 first in all 16 known equal-score games; on the arena ties are 0.7% of our games (14/2070), so the bot-side part is worth <= 0.3 pp.

result.caveats: No games were run. The collision toy (scratchpad/seat/toy_collision.py, toy_sweep.py) is a line-by-line Python port of Physics.collisionCheck/towards/resize and Rules.moveCreep/dealDamage for one queen and 4-8 knights without towers, so it isolates the direction and relative size of the order effect; real-game magnitudes are smaller (towers kill knights, queens kite) and the port was not executed against Rules.java at runtime. The direction is independently supported by the referee author's commit message, the arena DeathTraces (same code on both seats) and the mirror's death-game split. The arena logistic model treats games within an upload as independent (cluster-robust SEs are reported and are smaller); the opponent rating is the rating at fetch, not at game time; the per-league rating-point conversions use the fitted slopes (scales 2.14 Bronze, 4.4 Silver, 3.0 Gold), so rating-point figures carry that spread. v12's own 11 pp gap (z 1.5) is noisier than the pooled 6.9 pp; the pooled gamma is the number to use. The Legend (88 games) and cg2 (138) corpora are small; Legend's 0.477 P0 share has SE 0.053. The per-seat flag effects come from one 500-map development block with SEs of 2-3 pp per seat; the DEFENCE_FWD seat difference (+5 to +6 pp) is about 2 SE and several flags were read on the same block, so it needs a fresh block. Opponents' per-contact damage mixes many bots and styles (they stand on 32-37% of contact turns vs our 9-10%). Three of v12's 180 games have no 'ours' trace (177 queens) and 349 opponent trace lines did not parse (non-standard command text); negligible. Seat means CG player index: seat 0 = player 0 = top-left start (200,200) = red; checked in a seat-1 trace header (queen at (1720,800)). The mirror's seat edge varies with version (0.51-0.73), so how much the rules bias any bot depends on its contact exposure; it is therefore not fixed by changing the simulator (which already implements the live order) and cannot be 'removed' on the bot side, only exploited or hedged by seat.

findings.claim: The first-wave residual is carried almost entirely by turns with an enemy knight adjacent to the queen (within 60), not by the wave's size, the merges, or how she kites: lost races have 3.1 more adjacent turns and lose about 1.9 HP per adjacent turn.
findings.numbers: v12 Gold, 115 HP races (42 lost / 73 won, summary.csv + per-game traces): k500AtContact 3.50 vs 3.38 (MW p=0.36), hpK500AtContact 47.4 vs 43.2 (p=0.11), spawned20 3.7 vs 4.1 (p=0.91); lossK20 10.24 vs 3.42 (bootstrap diff +6.8 HP, 95% CI +3.7..+10.3); adjacent turns (nearest knight <=60 in the 20-turn window) 5.17 vs 2.07 (CI +1.6..+4.7); 39/73 won races have 0 adjacent turns vs 8/42 lost; OLS lossK20 = 1.88 x adjTurns, R2 0.89 (115 races); loss per threatened turn 0.75 vs 0.31 HP (CI +0.23..+0.66): the intensity part of the 6.8-HP gap is 5.2 HP, the duration part 0.75. findings.claim: The knights stay adjacent because our towers kill them too slowly at the contact: in lost races the enemy wave arrives about 3 turns earlier, before our second tower is up, so the queen fights it with one tower (and a 196-HP tower built under the wave). Tower damage is set by tower HP (range), one target per tower per turn, so the count alone is not the lever; the second tower's timing relative to the contact is a strong gradient.
findings.numbers: towersAtContact 1.43 vs 1.75 (MW p=0.017; one tower in 22/42 lost vs 25/73 won), towerHpAtContact 887 vs 1070 (CI -341..-32), coverQAtContact 1.40 vs 1.70 (p=0.022); contact turn 24.5 vs 27.3 (p=0.021) while the 2nd tower completes at turn 25 in both groups (25.2 vs 24.9, p=0.73; DeathTrace ours); 2nd tower at/after the contact in 31/42 lost vs 35/73 won. Gradient over 115 races by (2nd tower turn - contact): <=-3: lossK20 1.1, 24% lost (n=21); [-3,0): 2.7, 21% (n=28); [0,3): 6.9, 36% (n=39); >=3: 11.6, 63% (n=27). Over all 176 games with a contact the win rate by the same bands: 21/34 (0.62), 36/47 (0.77), 32/56 (0.57), 16/39 (0.41). Kill-speed proxy ttk = waveHP / sum(3 + hp//200): 6.85 vs 5.38 (p=0.017); lossK20 by ttk band: <4: 1.1 HP (n=37, 0.5 adjacent turns); 4-6: 3.6 (32); 6-8: 6.3 (16); 8-12: 13.8 (22, 7.5 adjacent turns). ttk explains 43% of the variance in adjacent turns and 1.44 of the 3.1-turn adjacency gap. Total tower damage over the window is the same (dmgK20 76 vs 79, killK20 5.55 vs 5.84) but per threatened turn 7.0 vs 9.5 damage and 0.53 vs 0.75 kills; recorded damage per turn in the first 10 turns 5.06 vs 5.59 (p=0.06). Within the one-tower regime (24 lost / 25 won): first tower HP equal (652 vs 672), the new tower completes 3.5 vs 2.2 turns after the contact (p=0.008), walk turns to its site under knights 2.9 vs 1.7 (p=0.009), wave HP 52 vs 45 (p=0.09), adjacent turns 7.9 vs 4.2.

The association is observation (high confidence); the causal reading kill speed -> adjacency -> loss is inference (medium confidence).

findings.claim: The contact turn is the opponent's barracks timing, not our position: early-barracks opponents (first barracks by turn 8) meet our queen at turn 22 with 1.2 towers and we score only 50% against them; late-barracks opponents are the death lens, not the race lens.

findings.claim: Our behaviour during the wave differs only in forward movement and walking to a new tower site under knights; most of the forward-move signal is a symptom of adjacency, and the kite rule's tower pull is not the cause. The net controllable part of the window behaviour is about 1-2 HP of the 6.8-HP gap.
findings.numbers: Forward moves under threat 4.19 vs 1.96 per game (CI +1.2..+3.3; AUC 0.72): forward kite MOVEs 2.93 vs 1.60 (p=0.002), forward walks to a new tower (BUILD on a not-yet-built site) 1.12 vs 0.30 (p<0.001), forward top-up walks 0.14 vs 0.05; backward moves equal (5.6 vs 6.0). Pooled over 176 games, HP lost on the turn after a move by nearest-knight band: knight at 0-60: forward 1.31 (n=275) vs backward 1.18 (n=261) - no direction effect when already adjacent; 121-180: forward 0.44 (n=88) vs back 0.11 (n=284); 181-250: forward 0.51 (n=81) vs back 0.02 (n=369). Forward moves with the knight >120 away: 1.14 vs 0.88 per game (p=0.07), costing 0.74 vs 0.26 HP per game (CI +0.15..+0.81). Forward kite MOVEs that approach her nearest tower: 0.12 vs 0.12 per game (p=0.87) - the pull is not it. Standing with a knight within 155: 0.52 vs 0.18 turns/game (p=0.10; k500=4 stratum 0.83 vs 0.18, p=0.027); stand/BUILD top-up turns with a knight <=100 cost 1.6-3.0 HP next turn (n=5-6 per class). findings.claim: The exchange of first waves (their queen's loss to our knights minus ours to theirs in turns 20-50) is the single best early predictor of the race and accounts for about 45% of the margin difference, but its drivers are the opponent's tower count when our wave lands and whether both our groups are alive together - not our barracks timing, which is identical in lost and won races.

findings.claim: Lost races are against stronger opponents, and the second-tower timing matters most against them.

Local first contacts (meet-back README profiles): mirror turn 24 with 1 tower, field 21 with 1, rival 25 with 1, boss 19 with 1. WAVE_TOWERS=2 / TOPUP_FROM=2 (exp-2026-11-05 README): contact with 2 towers, first-wave loss 7.3-8.2 vs 7.8 (no cut), summed tower HP at t50 1464/1436 vs 1648, queen deaths 36 vs 18 per 400 games.

levers.lever: Second tower up before the enemy's first wave arrives, WITHOUT starving the first tower: pump the first tower only to ~400-500 HP (2-3 turns instead of ~6 to 700) when a wave is coming, walk to the second site, then pump both; optionally triggered or tightened by the visible enemy barracks turn (<= 8 covers 42/180 games where we score 0.50).
levers.lossMode: HP race, first wave (also the vs-strong-opponents mode: within >=20-rated opponents the 2nd tower before the contact wins 11/19 vs 11/39 at/after)
levers.mechanism: Ladder order between the touch rule's top-up (TOWER_HP=700) and the next tower target: a conditional top-up threshold while towers < 2 and the WAVE_ANCHOR window is open (enemy knight barracks or knights visible). Tower damage is 3 + (range - dist)/200 per tower per turn with range from HP (Rules.java:355), so the aim is the summed damage rate at the contact (two towers of 450+700 beat one of 770 plus one of 196), not the count. This is a variant of the rejected WAVE_TOWERS/TOPUP_FROM family: those skipped ALL top-ups, left both towers at 200 HP (local tower HP at t50 1464 vs 1648) and doubled queen deaths; the new evidence is the t2rel gradient (lossK20 1.1 HP and 24% lost with the 2nd tower >=3 turns before the contact vs 11.6 HP and 63% lost >=3 turns after, n=21/27) and the kill-rate chain (ttk explains 43% of adjacent-turn variance).
levers.estimatedGain: Counterfactual on the arena games: 8 of the 24 one-tower lost races flip if their lossK20 fell to the 2-tower mean (9/31 for the 2nd-tower-after-contact subgroup), i.e. up to ~8-9 games of 180 (+4-5 pp) before costs; the symmetric exposure is 6 of 25 won one-tower races. Likely smaller in practice: the first tower's range at 450 HP is ~380 instead of ~500, and the old flags' failure shows deaths are the risk.
levers.measurability: Yes: mirror (contact turn 24, 1 tower), field (21, 1 tower) and rival (25, 1 tower) all meet the first wave in the one-tower regime; LocalProfile/WaveTrace can record the second tower turn minus the contact, the first-wave loss, summed tower HP at t50 and queen deaths per 1000 as tripwires (the 2026-11-05 flags doubled deaths against field).
levers.effort: flag on existing rule (conditional top-up threshold / ladder order); 1-2 parameters

levers.lever: Do not start a walk to a not-yet-built tower site while the wave is on her unless the site is within ~2 turns; instead hold at the existing tower and kite until the group is dead, then resume the ladder (a time-to-arrive/distance condition on the defence rule and ladder, not DEFENCE_FWD's half-plane).
levers.lossMode: HP race, first wave
levers.mechanism: The defence rule (threat with <2 towers within 500) and the ladder send the queen to the nearest free site; in lost races she walks 1.12 forward BUILD-new turns per game under knights (vs 0.30) at 1.7 HP per turn, and in the one-tower regime spends 2.9 walk turns to the 2nd site under knights (vs 1.7), the tower completing 3.5 vs 2.2 turns after the contact. The study's costliest traces (918150876, 918158655, 918146673, 918158658) show the walk through the knights and the stand at the 196-HP tower afterwards.
levers.estimatedGain: About 1-2 HP of the 6.8-HP gap (OLS: fwd BUILD-new 0.8 extra moves x ~1.7 HP; standing +1.0 HP); flips at most 2-5 of the 42 lost races on the uniform-gain table (+2 HP flips 5, +3 flips 6). Risk: THREAT_RADIUS=350 (fewer defence towers) lost 10 pp vs rival, so the tower must still be built, only later.
levers.measurability: Yes against mirror and field (both produce the defence walk at the contact); DEFENCE_FWD's failure (field -3 pp) is the reference; WaveTrace's walkTurnsToT2 / forward BUILD-new counts are the local metric.
levers.effort: flag on existing rule (defence rule / ladder gate by distance or turns to the site while a knight is within 250)

levers.lever: Record, do not pursue: standing within reach (STAND_REACH) and forward kiting penalties.
levers.lossMode: HP race, first wave
levers.mechanism: Standing turns with a knight within 155 are 0.52 vs 0.18 per game (~1 HP of the gap); forward moves while a knight is already adjacent cost the same as backward ones (1.31 vs 1.18 HP), and the kite's tower pull does not produce forward steps (0.12 vs 0.12 per game). STAND_REACH=155 and KITE_PULL=200 were already neutral locally.
levers.estimatedGain: <= 1 HP per lost race; 0-2 games of 180
levers.measurability: Already measured (STAND_REACH removes the standing turns without lowering the loss, mirror 7.9 vs 7.8)
levers.effort: none (closed)

levers.lever: The exchange of first waves is mostly the opponent's to decide (their tower count when our wave lands: 43 HP with 0 towers, 19 with 1, 9 with 2); the only our-side factor is whether both knight groups are alive together (8 knights vs 1 tower 23 HP, 4 knights 10 HP), which a single barracks cannot time (groups 5 turns apart). Not a cheap first-wave lever; hand to the army/midgame lens.
levers.lossMode: HP race, midgame (the 0-50 exchange is 45% of the margin gap but its drivers are theirs)
levers.mechanism: TRAIN timing with one barracks (first TRAIN at 80 gold at the barracks turn 9); our barracks timing is identical in lost and won races (9.17 vs 8.97), so no timing lever appears in the data.
levers.estimatedGain: unknown; the association (their loss 6.0 vs 14.2 HP) is driven by their builds
levers.measurability: field/rival build 1-2 towers early like Gold; the mirror's exchange is symmetric by construction
levers.effort: new rule at best; not recommended from this evidence

result.caveats: All counterfactual flip counts hold the rest of the game fixed (a smaller first-wave loss would also change the opponent's later play and our top-up budget); the symmetric exposure (20/73 won races at the lost mean) shows the first wave is noisy both ways. Lost races are against stronger opponents (20.05 vs 18.39), who also build barracks earlier (corr of the 2nd-tower-minus-contact with rating 0.21), so part of the timing effect may be opponent quality; the within-rating strata are small (19 vs 39 games above 20). The kill-speed proxy sum(3 + hp//200) ignores range and the one-target rule (corr 0.68 with the recorded damage per turn; the recorded first-10-turn damage differs only 5.06 vs 5.59, p=0.06), so 'kill rate' is a mechanism inferred from the formula and the adjacency chain, not measured directly. The traces carry no knight positions: 'forward' means toward the enemy's edge, not toward the knights, and 'adjacent' uses the nearest-knight distance <= 60. Mann-Whitney p-values are normal approximations with tie correction over dozens of metrics; treat p between 0.02 and 0.10 as suggestive only; bootstrap CIs are percentile with 10000 resamples. summary.csv's spawned20 counts any enemy spawn in the window and is not the study's merged-wave definition; my merge definitions (net of kills: 17/42 vs 18/73; simple: 12/42 vs 12/73) bracket the README's 12 of 42. 176 of 180 games have a wave summary (the 2 referee-removed games and 2 kills lack a contact); the DeathTrace files cover all 180. Ties at equal HP were counted as a win on seat 0 and a loss on seat 1 (CG ranks player 0 first). The rating conversion (+0.7 points for 10 games) is a back-of-envelope logistic estimate with Gold's scale 3.04, not a measurement. Lever 1 is a variant of a twice-rejected family (WAVE_TOWERS/TOPUP_FROM); it is proposed only because the mechanism (tower HP -> damage rate -> adjacency) and the t2rel gradient are new, and its local test needs the death-rate tripwire. Confidence notes folded into the evidence fields: finding 2's association is high, its causal chain medium; finding 5 and finding 9 are medium-high; finding 7's rating conversion is low. No games were run; everything is from the recorded Gold replays' derived files.

levers.lever: Stop pumping a capped tower: idle-queen rule (MainBot ladder-complete branch, lines 176-179) tops up the own tower with the LOWEST HP (or any below ~550) instead of the nearest-home tower, and never BUILDs on a tower >= 700 without a threat; freed turns go to the lowest tower or a mine (INCOME_LATE site).

levers.mechanism: v12 wastes 39-52 turns per game (mean; 57 in lost races, 24.7% of turns alive) on consecutive BUILDs beyond the 3rd on the same tower, which add ~4 effective HP each at the 800 cap; strong Gold 20.5, Legend 10.6. Despite 92.5 vs 69.5 top-ups in lost races our summed tower HP at t200 is 2378 (6 towers, 396 each) vs 2800 (5 towers, 560 each): the non-home towers melt. Maintaining 6 towers evenly costs 1 build per ~4 turns (24 HP/turn melt), far below our 92 top-ups, so the budget exists.

Direction high confidence (pure waste), size low confidence.

Differs from the rejected 'income target 5' and 'mines before towers' by timing (after the first wave and towers 3-4, when the queen is already walking the ladder) and by pairing with the freed pump turns (lever 1) rather than taking turns from towers.
levers.estimatedGain: Plausibly 20-30 of the 71 losses (economy deaths 17, races with lower income 20, overlapping); the arena shows opponents with maxIncome >= 12 winning 20/36 vs v12 while mid-income 7-12 opponents lose 52/71, so the gain depends on converting income into waves, not income alone. Medium-low confidence; the panel undervalued economy before.
levers.measurability: Partly: G1 mirror will under-reward it (HP races), field/rival (economy opponents, we score 0.92/0.75) are the relevant gates; arena placement is the real test. Add an arena-like check: opponents' income >= 7 games in the Gold corpus cannot be replayed, so only P1 decides.
levers.effort: new rule in nextSite / touch rule (ladder order), parameters existing (INCOME_TARGET, MINES_FIRST)

levers.lever: Wave cadence after the first wave: TRAIN_SYNC=0 (or sync only until turn 50), training 4 knights whenever 80 gold is banked, matching the strong players' 86-gold waves every 14 turns.
levers.lossMode: HP race midgame (42 lost races: our knights deal 1.24 HP/100g vs their 2.67; our contact episodes 7.3 vs their 5.1 per game vs strong)
levers.mechanism: Strong Gold opponents run 11.9 TRAIN events per game (gap 14 turns) vs our 7.3 (gap 20) with near-equal damage per gold overall (2.98 vs 2.83 HP/100g vs strong); more frequent waves reach the enemy queen more often (episode starts at t100-199: theirs at our queen 1.64/1.46 per 50 turns, ours at theirs 0.85/0.65). Legend winners train every 5 turns from 2-3 barracks. Sync was adopted in v06 against the local panel; the arena cadence evidence is new.
levers.estimatedGain: Touches the 42 lost races; direction uncertain because 8-knight waves may be what makes our 4.86 HP/100g in won games; low-medium confidence, could also lose vs 6-tower turtles if small waves die on towers.
levers.measurability: Yes: mirror, field, rival all respond to wave cadence; bench traces give kd per episode and episodes per game.
levers.effort: flag on existing rule (TRAIN_SYNC with a turn gate)

levers.lever: Keep building to the end when not ahead: let the ladder restart after losses (rebuild lost towers/mines, towers_200 and mines) and keep LATE_HOLD only when ahead; the strong players' last new structure is at median turn 232 vs ours 183.

levers.mechanism: Strong Gold add 1.0-1.17 towers and 0.86-1.57 mines per 50 turns at t100-249 and rebuild 4.4 lost mines (minesBuilt 6.7); v12 adds 0.28-0.73 towers and 0.32-0.93 mines and rebuilds ~2 of 3.1 lost mines because MINE is only rebuilt while income < 3 and towers only while < 6. In lost races v12 does keep walking (lastNew 236) but spends 100 top-ups and reaches only 5 mines built.

levers.lever: Different balance (not a rule): the Legend economy style - 3 mines by turn ~32 and income 7-9 by t50-100, 4-5 towers held at ~500 HP, 2-3 knight barracks with near-continuous training, forward barracks, HP traded for kills.

result.caveats: All opponent/Legend numbers are observational and style-correlated with rating; subgroups are small (strong: 22 won / 24 lost race / 12 died). Groups by ratingAtFetch (>=20: 58, 17-20: 85, <17: 37 games). The Legend corpus (88 games, 176 rows; 168 rows traced) is dominated by NotVerySmart (79 rows) and mixes economy players with two tower turtles, so Legend medians are not one style. TRAIN events, wave gold and knights (~spent/80) are inferred from gold drops in the DeathTrace (a drop = one event; giants/archers would inflate 'knights'); top-ups in traces are BUILDs on a site already seen as an own tower (csv towerTopUps agrees: v12 91 vs trace 92.5 median); the 'wasted pump' measure beyond the 3rd consecutive build assumes the tower started >= 500 (beyond the 5th: 39 vs 7 vs 3.4 is the conservative figure); knight efficiency = queen damage / gold on units ignores structure damage and tower kills. Fixed-turn csv values are empty for games that ended earlier and were excluded at that turn. The cg2 Gold corpus (84 rows, 2026-10-28) resembles Gold mid and was used only as context. Levers 1-3 overlap in which losses they touch; the counts of losses 'touched' are plausibility bounds, not effect estimates. No games were run.

findings.claim: Enemy-tower damage is almost eliminated in Gold v12, and 88 % of what remains comes from the two code paths that choose an own tower without the enemy-range check: the flight (MainBot.java:133-137, nearest own TOWER with no !underEnemyTower) and the idle pump (MainBot.java:175-176), while the touch rule is guarded (MainBot.java:117). ROUTE's straight fallback through ranges (RoutePlanner.java:91-92 and :128 return the BUILD when the straight walk is unsafe; from inside a range every fan plan breaks at its first step, :108, because ApproachPlanner.safeSegment :140-150 fails at the start point) is no longer a measurable cost after SAFE_LADDER.
findings.numbers: Total td (HP from enemy towers) 114 over 180 games = 0.63/game (won games 0.08, lost 1.48). Top-ups while standing inside an enemy range: 110 turns in 15 games, 71 HP (68 turns with td>0, 11 games); walks to such an own tower: 33 turns in 8 games, 29 HP. Ladder walks through ranges: walk_new_M 9 HP, walk_new_B 3 HP, upgrade 2 HP. Games with td>=5: 9 (8 lost, 3 of them deaths; largest 40 HP in 918168604, lost 2:70, and 18 HP in 918146139, lost 39:62). Lost races with td >= margin: 1 of 42 (918150190, 21:28, td 7).

findings.claim: Under knights, 66 % of all knight damage is taken during kite steps themselves and 15 % of contact turns are spent standing or walking in reach at 2.5-2.7 HP/turn, 2.6x the in-reach kite step. The kite rule (MainBot.java:242-284) predicts one sites-only step (Physics.queenStep ignores units, :267), scores knights where they stand (:273-274), demands cover at the end point (:271) and a +5 gain (:258); it never shakes knights (speed 100 vs 60).
findings.numbers: Contact turns (enemy knight within 250): 8615 = 47.9/game = 23 % of our 38252 turns. By our command: kite MOVE 7325 turns (85 %), 2679 HP, 0.37/turn (0.97/turn in the 2749 turns with the nearest knight <=120); standing top-up 572 turns, 444 HP, 0.78/turn (2.63/turn in reach, 162 turns); defence walk to a new tower 394 turns, 396 HP, 1.01/turn; defence build 147 turns, 185 HP, 1.26/turn; flight to the nearest own tower 177 turns, 334 HP, 1.89/turn (2.55 in reach, 129 turns). In-reach stand+flee: 291 turns, 755 HP = 4.2 HP/game. After a kite step a knight is still within 250 next turn in 5754/7292 (79 %); kite runs 2020, mean 3.6 turns, 626 runs >=5, max 21. In-reach kite steps take 0 hits in 622/2749, 1 in 1668, 2+ in 459. Knight damage total 4038 HP = 22.4/game.
findings.evidence: trace_quirks.out section D; trace_levers.out sections 1 and 7; code lines read from MainBot.java.

findings.claim: The knight-damage budget separates lost races from won ones mainly through kiting duration/cost, then the defence rule, then in-reach standing; tower damage is marginal. Upper bounds on flippable lost races per lever are small but non-zero.

Per game: lost races kite 16.5 HP, defence walk+build 4.7, stand/flee in reach 3.5, td 1.9; won races (73): 9.4 / 1.8 / 1.5 / 0.1; deaths (29): 33.8 / 5.7 / 14.8 / 0.9. Lost races where a lever's whole HP >= the margin (not additive): kite 22, half the kite HP 8, defence 6, stand/flee in reach 3, stand+defence 8, td 1. Deaths' last 10 turns: 182 of 290 turns are kite moves, kd 397 (13.7 HP per death).

With no knight within 500: 7058 turns while T<6 (39.2/game, 179 games), 4304 while T>=6 (23.9/game overall; 48 per game in the 89 games whose ladder completed, median completion turn 121), plus 1061 turns walking home to pump (5.9/game) and 2434 standing at a tower with knights 250-500 away (13.5/game). Passing top-up episodes (diversion from a walk, T<6): 474 in 151 games, 1086 turns = 6.0/game. Gold at idle top-ups mean 80, 2 % >=160. Won games 69 idle top-ups/game (33 % of turns), lost 53 (25 %). Her command when a tower fell: topup 124, kite 47, move 24.

findings.claim: The defence rule (MainBot.java:97-110) spends about 3 HP per game walking to and building a 200-HP tower under knights; it never exceeds the tower cap in practice. A 200-HP tower's range is only ~262-277 (sqrt((200*1000+pi*r^2)/pi), Rules.java:361) and it needs ~7 turns to kill one 25-HP knight (3-4 damage/turn, Const.java:16,48), so its value within a wave is small; the Gold study already found the walk-and-build not causal (+1.4 HP, CI through 0).

findings.claim: The threat definition (MainBot.java:87-88: enemy KNIGHTs within THREAT_RANGE only) costs no direct HP: archers damage only creeps (Rules.java:318-323) and giants only towers (:325-331). Its cost is indirect (cover loss to giants) and the missing early warning: most contact episodes begin while the queen is walking to a new site, but the HP difference against episodes begun at a tower is small.

Contact episodes 1743: begun while walking to a new site 1167 (kd 2.58/episode, 3.5 towers at contact), at a tower 330 (2.09, 3.8 towers), other 246 (1.38). Opponents trained giants in 35/180 games.
