findings.claim: A 1-ply + short rollout over cr.core.Rules for the queen's command under knights fits the 50 ms turn: the per-turn cost is dominated by the five collision passes over all entities, and the typical entity count is small.
findings.numbers: Rules.resolve per simulated turn: processCreeps (Rules.java:233-265) runs 5 sub-steps, each moveCreep for n creeps plus fixCollisions(s,1) = one collisionCheck (Physics.java:76-109) over E = creeps + 2 queens + nSites entities with E(E-1) pair tests, each a sqrt; then n dealDamage, n*24 closestSite tear-down tests, towers*n targeting, mines, rounding. Creeps alive (both players, cgStudy csv): t25 median 12 max 16; t50-200 median 2-4, p90 8-11, max 20 (Legend max 29). So E ~ 30-40 typical, <= 56 worst: 5*E(E-1) = 4.4k-7.8k sqrt-pairs typical, 15.4k worst; at ~10-20 ns per pair (JIT-compiled) ~0.05-0.15 ms typical, <=0.3 ms worst per simulated turn (estimate from loop counts; no benchmark). Free budget ~30 ms (50 - 7.7 current max - 10 margin) -> ~200-600 simulated turns typical, ~100 worst. 27 candidates (24 headings + stand/top-up + BUILD nearest own tower + defence site) x horizon 4-6 = 108-162 turns: fits typical crowds; the worst case needs 12 headings or a local sub-state (entities within ~600 of the queen, E ~ 15 -> ~1k pairs/turn). Allocation: preallocate ~30 GameStates (copyFrom, GameState.java:108-141) instead of copy(); Rules.build allocates only a tiny String[].
findings.evidence: Rules.java, Physics.java, GameState.java read in full; features_seat_cost.out (creeps alive); brief (7.7 ms max turn).

findings.claim: What the rollout needs is already in the local view except the seat and the enemy queen's intent, and the knights' motion is deterministic given our queen's path: enemy knights walk at 100/turn (5 sub-steps of 20) toward our queen with a 3-unit offset (Rules.java:296-309), hit when within 20+30+5 of her centre for 1 HP each (Rules.java:314-317, Const KNIGHT_DAMAGE 1, CREEP_HP 25); our knights walk to their queen; towers fire deterministically at the closest enemy creep else the queen (Rules.java:347-363); barracks spawns in progress are known exactly (InputReader.java:81-84 sets barrProgress from p1), so spawns within the horizon are predicted; enemy gold matters only for new TRAINs that would spawn >=5 turns later (CREEP_BUILD_TIME 5). The seat is inferable at turn 0 from the start corner (MapGen.java:65-66: player 0 at (200,200), player 1 at (1720,800); all 180 traces agree), which settles the PLAN.md prerequisite (build-conflict parity, Rules.java:61-70); the parity never fired in these games.
findings.numbers: Start corners: 81 seat-0 games top-left, 99 seat-1 games bottom-right (180/180). Build conflicts (both queens BUILD the same touched site on one turn): 0 in 180 games. Remaining seat-dependence of Rules with us as player 0: the entity order in collisions (player 0's units first, Physics.java:121-128) and tower target ties, sub-unit effects; swap players when seat==1 for exactness. CGRunner.warmUp (CGRunner.java:92-127) never runs Rules, so the rollout code would meet the JIT in a 50 ms turn unless the warm-up is extended.
findings.evidence: trace_quirks.out (corner and conflict counts); MapGen.java; Rules.java; InputReader.java; CGRunner.java.

findings.claim: The evaluation a rollout would use and the rules it would replace: minimise our HP lost over the horizon, reward enemy knight HP removed by our towers (the only way a contact ends), keep a terminal cover term (end under an own tower's range, as KITE=2 demands) and an enemy-range penalty, tie-break by the current rule's choice. It replaces, in order, kite (MainBot.java:111/242-284), the under-threat touch/flight block (:117-137: stand-and-top-up vs flee), then the defence rule (:97-110) in a second phase because the new tower's value outlives the horizon; the ladder, TRAIN and the economy stay rule-based.
findings.numbers: Addressable HP (180 games): kite 2679, in-reach stand/flee 755, defence 581; excess of in-reach standing/fleeing over in-reach kite steps (2.63-0.97)*162 + (2.55-0.97)*129 = 473 HP = 2.6 HP/game; half of the kite HP would flip <= 8 of 42 lost races.
findings.evidence: trace_quirks.out section D; trace_levers.out section 1; code structure of MainBot.play.

findings.claim: Seat asymmetry: the bot's own code is symmetric under the 180-degree map rotation (kite fan starts at the centre-to-queen direction, MainBot.java:256; the ROUTE fan starts at the queen-to-target direction with +15 degrees first, RoutePlanner.java:97-101; nearest() ties by lowest id, :51-60; Math.round on positions, Rules.java:102-104 and Physics.java:166-167, breaks symmetry only at exact .5). The rules' asymmetries are the tie (CG ranks player 0 first in all 16 known equal-score games) and the build parity (0 occurrences). In Gold the observed seat gap is weak and the tie rule accounts for a large part of it; strong players show no seat-0 edge. LATE_HOLD compares strictly (hp[0] > hp[1], MainBot.java:95), so at equal HP our seat-0 queen, who would win the tie, keeps walking.
findings.numbers: v12: seat 0 won 54/81 (0.667), seat 1 55/99 (0.556), deaths 9 vs 20; v11: 59/94 (0.628) vs 52/86 (0.605). Pooled v11+v12: 113/175 vs 107/185, diff 0.067, SE 0.051, z 1.3. Equal-score games: v12 2 (both as player 0, counted as wins), v11 3 (2 won as player 0, 1 lost as player 1) -> 5 of 360 games decided by the tie rule, 4 favouring our seat 0, i.e. about 40 % of the pooled seat gap of ~12 games. Legend top-10 corpus: seat 0 ranked first 42/88 (0.477 +- 0.053); cg2 Gold others 24/42 (0.571 +- 0.077). Turns >=200 with equal queen HP: 129 in 7 of 180 games. Close races (margin <=5): 27, seat 0 won 8 of 10, seat 1 9 of 17.
findings.evidence: features_seat_cost.out; tower_loss_split.out (pooled z); trace_levers.out sections 6 and 8; docs/rules/inferred.md lines 43-57; MapGen.java; code read.

levers.lever: Rollout-based threat response with cr.core.Rules (new flag, e.g. KITE=3): each turn with an enemy knight within ~300-400, simulate 24 headings + stand/top-up + BUILD nearest own tower (+ the defence site) for 4-6 turns with the enemy knights walking to our queen, our knights to theirs, towers firing and visible spawns; pick by HP lost, enemy knight HP removed, terminal cover and enemy-range penalty. Replaces kite, the under-threat stand/flee block first; the defence rule in phase 2.
levers.lossMode: queen death (29/180; 48.6 HP of their contact loss is kiting + in-reach standing) and HP races (kite 16.5 HP/game in lost races vs 9.4 in won; vs strong opponents 28.5 kd/game)
levers.mechanism: MainBot.java:111/242-284 (kite: one sites-only step, static knights, +5 gain, cover required), :117-137 (top-up/flee under knights at 2.5-2.7 HP/turn in reach), :97-110 (defence walk/build 1.0-1.3 HP/turn); Rules.resolve gives exact knight motion, hits and tower kills within the horizon
levers.estimatedGain: 3-5 HP/game: 2.6 HP/game from the in-reach excess alone (473 HP/180) plus 10-20 % of the kite's 2679 HP; upper bound <= 8 of 42 lost races flipped (half the kite HP >= margin) plus some of the 29 deaths; realistic 1-3 pp of arena score; arena-undemonstrated
levers.measurability: yes on the whole panel (mirror, field and rival all send knight waves; rival adds giants); G0 is the risk: needs the warm-up extended to Rules (CGRunner.warmUp) and procCheck on both seats; LegScan/LocalProfile for max play() time
levers.effort: new subsystem (sim adapter from the local view, candidate generation, evaluation, warm-up, tests; ~0.05-0.3 ms per simulated turn, 108-162 turns per real turn)

levers.lever: Targeted-fix bundle (each < 10 % of maps): (a) add !underEnemyTower to the flight's and the idle pump's nearest-own-tower predicates (MainBot.java:134, :175), falling back to the nearest own tower outside enemy ranges; (b) hysteresis on the ladder target (keep the previous target unless the new one saves >= 1 turn, nextSite/:149); (c) seat-aware LATE_HOLD: hold at equal HP on seat 0 (MainBot.java:95) with the seat stored in InputReader from the start corner (also the prerequisite of lever 1). (d) ROUTE's straight fallback: nothing measurable left (12 HP/180 games).
levers.lossMode: (a) HP race / deaths via tower fire: 100 HP/180 games in 15-23 games, 1 lost race flippable; (b) 1-2.4 turns/game of walking (about 0.01 S per turn by the ROUTE calibration); (c) HP race last 50 turns: 7 of 180 games had equal HP after turn 200
levers.mechanism: guards missing on two code paths; target recomputed every turn from the moving midpoint; strict comparison ignoring CG's player-0 tie rule
levers.estimatedGain: small and near-certain: <= 0.6 HP/game (a), <= 2.4 turns/game (b), <= 1-2 games/180 (c)
levers.measurability: (a) by td in local games (field and rival build towers) and a regression test; (b) by LegScan turns and switch counts; (c) only by replaying recorded equal-HP positions; all as P2 targeted fixes (G0, S >= 0.500, boss >= -1 pp)
levers.effort: small code edits + unit tests on captured positions

levers.lever: Tower maintenance walk: when no knight is within 500 and the ladder is complete (or while standing idle), walk to the own tower with the lowest HP or the one nearest the enemy's approach instead of pumping the home tower forever (MainBot.java:175-176), staying on own-tower sites only (no new sites, unlike INCOME_LATE).
levers.lossMode: queen death and HP race midgame through cover loss (256 towers lost in 112 games; 134 in the 35 giant games, 42 melt-outs before turn 200 in the 145 others; opponents >=20 hold 2788 summed tower HP vs our 2380 at t200)
levers.mechanism: 63 turns/game at a tower with no knight within 500 (7058 + 4304 turns) plus 1061 walking-home turns are the queen's largest unused capacity; KITE=2 needs cover at every step (MainBot.java:271), so lost towers convert kiting into standing
levers.estimatedGain: unquantified; bounded by the 35 giant games (we lose cover at 3.8 towers/game there) and the 24 idle turns/game; INCOME_LATE's failure (deaths on walks to new sites) does not apply to covered own sites, but walks under approaching waves remain a risk
levers.measurability: yes: rival (giants from turn 80) and field; towers lost and summed tower HP from LocalProfile/cgStudy; G1 mirror
levers.effort: flag on an existing rule (new target choice after the ladder, reuse of walkTo/ROUTE)

levers.lever: Defence gating by the rollout (phase 2 of lever 1): build the 200-HP defence tower only when the simulation shows it kills or deters knights within the horizon; otherwise kite or stand at the existing tower.
levers.lossMode: HP race first wave (defence walk+build 4.7 HP/game in lost races vs 1.8 in won; 581 HP/180 total)
levers.mechanism: MainBot.java:97-110 walks through knights to the nearest free site within 500 and spends a build turn standing (1.26 HP/turn); the new tower's range ~262-277 and ~7 turns per knight kill
levers.estimatedGain: <= 6 of 42 lost races by HP; the Gold study found the walk-and-build not causal (+1.4 HP, CI through 0), so the realistic gain is small and the tower's later value must be modelled
levers.measurability: mirror and field (first wave at turn ~24); WaveTrace metrics (lossK20, towersAtContact)
levers.effort: part of the new subsystem; not worth a standalone rule

levers.lever: TRAIN_SYNC relaxation (new mechanism, not RELEASE_NEAR): release one barracks when the two-barracks hold exceeds N turns, or when our knights are absent from the board and the enemy queen is far from her towers; keep the 8-knight wave otherwise.
levers.lossMode: vs strong opponents (HP races where their pressure exceeds ours: they train 11-12 waves vs our 9; their kd on our queen 27 vs ours 22 per game)
levers.mechanism: MainBot.java:211-216: with two barracks 48 % of turns hold 80-159 gold (45 turns/game), each double release waits a median 22 turns, gold float 81 vs the opponents' 60
levers.estimatedGain: unknown direction: v06 adopted the sync against v05 (0.548 with the army flags), never against Gold-strength opponents; 4-knight waves die to towers faster
levers.measurability: rival and field (knights vs towers dynamics), but the panel undervalued army changes before (v08, v12); arena decides
levers.effort: flag on an existing rule

levers.lever: Second barracks site/timing: take a nearer free site when the central site (BARRACKS_FORWARD=50, MainBot.java:425-430) is more than N walking turns away, or start it from the 3rd tower.
levers.lossMode: vs strong opponents / HP race midgame (fewer waves: second barracks at median turn 95 after the 4th tower at 65; never built in 27 of 159 games; 7.3 turns/game walking to it)
levers.mechanism: nextSite's forward-barracks branch picks the free site nearest the board centre regardless of distance; the walk is unprotected and competes with the first waves (26.8 % of the gap turns are kiting)
levers.estimatedGain: unknown; v10's centre choice gave +3 pp vs rival locally, so a distance cap should keep that where the walk is short
levers.measurability: rival (waves and giants), field; LegScan for walking turns
levers.effort: flag on an existing rule

levers.lever: Pre-contact positioning (early warning from knights within 400-500 or an enemy barracks about to spawn): finish the current build only if it completes before contact, else move to the nearest covered tower.
levers.lossMode: HP race first wave / midgame (1167 of 1743 contact episodes begin while walking to a new site)
levers.mechanism: threat is binary at 250 (MainBot.java:87-88); knightWaveComing/firstWaveWindow exist (:388, :445) but only steer WAVE_ANCHOR/WAVE_TOWERS; ROUTE's quietStep (ApproachPlanner.java:117-131) already refuses landings near knights
levers.estimatedGain: small: episodes begun walking cost 2.58 HP vs 2.09 at a tower (self-selected); prior KITE_RANGE 500 (v07 rule) lost 12 pp to field, THREAT_RADIUS 350 nothing
levers.measurability: mirror and field first wave; WaveTrace coverQAtContact
levers.effort: new rule; low priority unless folded into lever 1's trigger (start the search at 400)

result.caveats: All trace numbers are from v12's 180 recorded Gold games (two uploads) replayed by DeathTrace; own structures are inferred from a touched BUILD whose count rises next turn, so a tower destroyed and rebuilt on the same site, or a build lost to a conflict (0 observed), can be misclassified; 'kd' and 'td' are probe losses (enemy tower ranges zeroed / enemy knights removed) and the in-reach bucket (nearest knight <= 120) approximates a hit next turn. Per-lever HP totals are upper bounds: the counterfactual command also costs HP, and the flippable-race counts are not additive. The Rules cost model is derived from loop counts only (benchmarks were forbidden); the nanoseconds-per-pair figure and CG's single-CPU JIT behaviour could move it by about 3x either way, and the first-turn warm-up must cover Rules. The seat analysis is observational (pooled z 1.3) and the tie-rule share of the gap is arithmetic on 5 games. The levers' arena effects are undemonstrated; the local panel's known biases (it undervalued v08 and v12, overvalued v07; the mirror over-weights HP races; rival over-plays giants) apply to every measurability claim. Enemy gold and the enemy queen's intent are unknown to any rollout; within 4-6 turns this only matters through builds she might start.

findings.claim: The panel undervalued the two changes that place the queen relative to enemy knights and own towers in the first-wave window (v08 bound kiting, v12 first-wave anchor) and the two macro opening changes (v03, v05); it overvalued free kiting (v07) and the forward second barracks (v10). The common thread of the undervalued class: the local opponents' first waves are about 60 % as costly as Gold's, so a rule that protects the queen in that window shows a smaller local effect than its arena effect.

findings.claim: P2's machine cost per candidate is about 10 minutes for a screen or a final evaluation at v03-era bot speeds, dominated by the two boss process series, plus 2-thread repeats when host slow turns appear, plus a development sweep of 7-22 arms; the arena adds two placements of 11-24 minutes each.
findings.numbers: Measured 2026-11-01 (eval-run.log): direct 2000 maps (4000 games, 8 threads) 21:20:06-21:20:26 = 20 s; mirror 18 s; boss-cand 500 maps (1000 games, 3 threads, 200 ms) 186 s; boss-ctrl 208 s; legScan 2000 maps 26 s and 16 s; whole eval 7 min 54 s. The current screen.sh/eval.sh run 6 in-process series (direct, mirror, field cand/ctrl, rival cand/ctrl, 2000 maps each) and 2 boss series (500 maps) -> about 2-3 min in-process + 6-7 min boss if per-game cost stays near v03's (mean turn 0.05-0.08 ms for v09-v12 per the DEVLOG). G0 repeats at 2 threads were needed on 5 of the last 8 screens/evals (late-hold, income, waves, waves-eval, safe-ladder) on the hybrid-core laptop (2 performance + 10 efficiency cores). Development sweep: per arm 3 series x 500 maps (1000 games, roughly 10 s each) + 3 controls; arms tried per experiment: income 22, giants 7, waves 7, meet-back 7 + 10 + 2 probes, first-wave 4, safety 12+, army 12+. Artifact step: ./gradlew test ~30 s, submit, two 100-map procCheck runs (not timed in the logs). Arena: Gold placements completed 22-24 min after the agent's creation (v12), Silver 17-19 min, Bronze 11-16 min; tools/arena.py follow automates snapshot, fetch and cgAttribute. Total per candidate excluding coding: roughly 1-2 hours.

levers.lever: Add a giant-free strong-opponent variant to the panel (spec `rival?GIANTS=0`, or report G5 split by giants) so that G5 measures strength/economy rather than the giant answer.
levers.lossMode: vs strong opponents; HP race midgame
levers.mechanism: R0 trains giants in 85 % of its games against Gold's 17-19 % (30/180, 35/180), so every candidate that interacts with giants (GIANT_GUARD -1.8..-3.3 pp, ARCHERS +3.05 pp on dev seeds) is scored mostly through a mechanism five times rarer on the arena; v09 scores 0.76 vs R0 without giants against 0.70 with them, and the strongest Silver players trained 1-2 giants in 36 of 55 games (Gold top players: 85 % none).
levers.estimatedGain: Process lever: removes a +-2-3 pp distortion of G5 for giant-sensitive candidates; no direct arena points.
levers.measurability: Zero-code: `./gradlew bench -Pbot2=rival?GIANTS=0` in-process, 2000 maps about 20-40 s; the ledger and local-screen.md record the variant.
levers.effort: Policy text only (a user decision under PV5).

levers.lever: Give FieldBot a first-wave knob that reproduces Gold's wave cost (e.g., FIRST_WAVE_GOLD=160: hold the first knight TRAIN until 160 gold, or BARRACKS=2 with a sync), then calibrate so the local 20-turn first-wave loss against v12 matches the Gold reference (v12 on the arena: 6.9 HP mean, 10.2 in lost races, 45 merged waves of 176).
levers.lossMode: HP race first wave
levers.mechanism: The panel's first wave costs 7.3-7.8 HP (mirror/field/rival, 200 maps) against Gold's 11.4 (v11, 171 games); the class of changes that the arena rewarded most (v08 +2.46, v12 +3.28) acts in exactly this window and was undervalued locally by a factor 2.7-3.7, while the first-wave defence flags (WAVE_TOWERS/TOPUP_FROM) were rejected on local evidence that may not transfer (local one-tower loss 5-7 HP vs Silver 12).
levers.estimatedGain: Better ranking of first-wave candidates, the class with the largest realised arena steps; upper bound of the loss pool: lost v12 races lose 10.6 HP to knights in turns 0-50 vs 3.5 in won ones (42 vs 73 games).
levers.measurability: LocalProfile already prints contact distance, 20-turn loss and merged waves; gold_reference.py gives the Gold numbers; a calibration sweep of ~10 variants x 500 maps is about 5 minutes; the v05-v12 ladder against the variant checks the arena order.
levers.effort: New rule in FieldBot.train (about 20-40 lines) plus a calibration experiment; no bot change.

levers.lever: Partial-kiting knob for FieldBot (kite only with >= N knights within range, or a MOVE-share cap) to approximate the strongest players' 14 % MOVE under knights instead of R0's 66 % or field's 0 %.
levers.lossMode: vs strong opponents
levers.mechanism: R0's full v08-style kiting drives 74-76 % of its games to the limit (Gold 59-64 %) and made R0 reward v07's free kiting (+0.17 logit) where the arena showed -0.71; the strongest Silver players kited on 14 % of contact turns and lost 1.07 HP per contact turn (R0 0.5).
levers.estimatedGain: Unknown; the acceptance test is that the v05-v12 ladder against the variant reproduces the arena order including v07 <= v06.
levers.measurability: 8 series x 500 maps (about 2 minutes) for the ladder check; in-process.
levers.effort: Small (a guard in FieldBot.kite); a calibration run; policy text if adopted as a gate.

levers.lever: Pre-screen every candidate flag on v12's 180 Gold replays with cgAttribute (the arena_diff.py method used for SAFE_LADDER) before spending a P2 block: count the games and turns where the rule's decision differs from the recorded one, split by outcome class (42 lost races, 29 deaths, 109 wins).
levers.lossMode: any (the pre-screen tells which)
levers.mechanism: The local panel cannot produce Gold's field, but the recorded games can show whether a rule fires in the games we lose: SAFE_LADDER changed a decision in 20 of v10's 52 losses vs 11 of 108 wins before its upload; a rule that never fires in the 42 lost races or 29 deaths cannot fix them.
levers.estimatedGain: Saves screen blocks and about 10 minutes per rejected arm; gives an upper bound on the games a rule can touch (as the TRAIN_SYNC estimate of 8/180 in the next-step study).
levers.measurability: Counts only, no counterfactual outcome; the tool exists (`./gradlew cgAttribute -Pbot=current?FLAG=1 -Preplays=... -Pagent=...` plus a 50-line diff script); minutes per candidate.
levers.effort: Existing tools; a generic version of arena_diff.py.

levers.lever: Count changed maps against every panel opponent (not only the control's mirror) for the targeted-fix classification, and report it in bench_pair.
levers.lossMode: process (policy integrity)
levers.mechanism: A rule that acts only on an opponent's units passes as targeted however much it changes against that opponent: ARCHERS changed 0 of 2000 maps vs the mirror and 1740 of 2000 vs R0 and was adopted by the letter until the user refused.
levers.estimatedGain: Prevents a repeat of the archers case; no arena points.
levers.measurability: bench_pair.py already computes changed maps per pair; the rule needs the mirror-equivalent control series for field and rival (already run in every screen).
levers.effort: Small tool change + a line in local-screen.md (user decision; the gap is recorded since 2026-11-06).

levers.lever: Rebalance the screen's time: shorten or drop G2 (boss) and spend the minutes on a second strong-opponent variant or on the pre-screen above.
levers.lossMode: process (throughput)
levers.mechanism: boss deltas were 0.0000 in the last six screens/evals (v11/v12 win 999-1000 of 1000, games end by turn 50) while the two boss series take about 6-7 of the ~10 minutes of a screen and caused the only invalid series (48 of 500 maps lost to boss timeouts in the income screen; 6 in the late-hold screen).
levers.estimatedGain: About 60 % of the screen's wall time; more candidates per session.
levers.measurability: Immediate from the run logs.
levers.effort: Policy text (user decision); G2 could stay as a 100-map smoke check.

levers.lever: Replace the single S >= 0.60 upload recommendation by a two-part signal: a mechanism check against the Gold reference metrics (first-wave loss, contact distance, merged waves, HP-race margins) and the sign/size of the rival delta, with the mirror kept as a no-regression gate.
levers.lossMode: process (which candidates reach the arena)
levers.mechanism: The head-to-head S ordered the arena gains at rho 0.31 (n=10): v12 (S 0.57) and v08 (S 0.67) gave +3.28 and +2.46, v07 (S 0.68) gave -0.71; the user already overrode the 0.60 rule for 5 of 10 uploads. R0's sign agreed with the arena on the v06, v08 and v12 steps and disagreed only on v07 (3-4 steps, a small sample); the Gold reference metrics moved on the arena as the local profiles predicted for v12 (contact 411 -> 287, loss 11.4 -> 6.9).
levers.estimatedGain: Fewer wasted placements (each 22-24 min in Gold and one of the two per candidate); no direct points.
levers.measurability: Retrospective: apply the rule to the 10 uploaded candidates (table in finding 1); prospective: each upload adds a data point.
levers.effort: Policy text and a small summary script; a user decision (P2 is the user's policy).

levers.lever: Size the next step to the arena's resolution: aim for a change of the queen-under-knights/first-wave class (realised +2.5 and +3.3) or a bundle of several small fixes in one artifact, since a gain below about 2.5 points is invisible with two placements per side and small fixes paid two placements each (v11 +0.92, v04 +0.07, v02 +0.05 all within noise).
levers.lossMode: HP race first wave; queen death
levers.mechanism: SE of the difference of two 2-placement means is 1.23 points at SD 1.23 (M 2.46; Gold's own pooled SD 1.27); a 1-point gain needs ~13 placements per side at 2 SE. The gap to the top of Gold is 6.2 points = 2.5 M, i.e. two or three steps of v12's size.
levers.estimatedGain: A visible step is >= 2.5 points; the two largest realised steps came from this class.
levers.measurability: P1 as it stands (two placements, arena_compare.py).
levers.effort: Planning only.

levers.lever: Treat the economy class as arena-untested rather than refuted: if an economy candidate passes G0, loses at most 2 pp to any opponent and shows a mechanism in the Gold replays (income at t150 2.5 vs 5 in lost games), let one exception upload judge it, because the panel has killed every economy arm and PV3/PV5 record the late pressure of strong economies as unrepresented.
levers.lossMode: queen death (economic collapse, 29/180 deaths with opponent income 2x ours in 23 of 29); HP race midgame
levers.mechanism: All four economy arms lost or tied locally for a recorded structural reason (our half's sites are towers at ladder completion; late mines are far; +5-8 % gold = one wave), but the arena has never seen one; the mirror (91 % at the limit) punishes any trade of early safety for late income, and field over-earns (income 8) so it does not reward out-earning it either.
levers.estimatedGain: Unknown; risk of a placement at or below v12's mean (rollback only below 17.90 on the mean and 2 SE on the rating).
levers.measurability: Only the arena (P1), after G0 and the -2 pp gates; the local panel cannot measure it (recorded in PV3/PV5).
levers.effort: Policy exception (user decision) + the two placements (~1 hour).

result.caveats:
DO-NOT-REPEAT (candidate; flags; local result; arena result if uploaded; recorded mechanism). Dev = development seeds (500 maps, both seats; 10000-10499 before 2026-11-05, 1+397k since); S = map score vs the control named.
1. INCOME_TARGET=5 (mines before towers): 0.290 vs v04 (dev); with INCOME_LATE=6,LATE_CLEAR=1000: target 4 0.481 / target 5 0.402 vs v09, -0.1/-3.9 pp vs R0. Mechanism: the income phase delays the tower line; early knights pin the queen. (INCOME_TARGET=8 was v01: 0.525 vs v02 for early towers; 4 -> 0.670; 3+MAX_TOWERS=8 -> 0.782, adopted v03; 2+MAX_TOWERS=6 0.797.)
2. INCOME_LATE 4/5/6/8 (income after the ladder): 0.505/0.513/0.508/0.485 vs v06, -9/-12 pp vs field (6/8); vs v09 0.485/0.482/0.478/0.479 and +1.3/+1.7/+1.8/+1.9 pp vs R0, ~0 vs field; with LATE_COVER/LATE_HALF/LATE_CLEAR 600/1000 0.483-0.498 vs v09; screened MAX_TOWERS=5,INCOME_LATE=6,LATE_CLEAR=1000 (block screen-pv3 1): S 0.5016 (CI 0.4898-0.5135) G1 FAIL, rival +1.79 pp, field +0.31. Mechanism: our half's sites are towers at ladder completion; late mines are far; the walks kill the queen (63 vs 47 deaths/1000 mirror games); +5-8 % gold = one wave. Never uploaded.
3. UPGRADE=1 (walk to upgrade own mines): within +-0.005 of off in every pair (the touch rule already fills a new mine).
4. MINES_FIRST=3: 0.673 vs v04 (2 mines 0.760, adopted v05); +3 pp vs field but games 87 turns (the field queen dies early). MINES_FIRST=1: 0.684.
5. TOWER_HP (top-up threshold) 400/500/600/800: 400 -> 0.293 vs v04 (0.492 with MINES_FIRST=1); 600 -> 0.616 (vs 0.684 at 700); 800 -> 0.474; 500 -> -7 pp vs field; INCOME_LATE 6 with 600/500 -> 0.428/0.368 vs v06. Mechanism: tower damage and range rise with HP (3 at 200 HP, 4 at 700); thinner towers lose to knight waves.
6. MAX_TOWERS 4/5/10/12: 4 -> 0.399 vs v04 (0.646 with MF=1), -6 pp vs field; 5 alone -> 0.471 vs v09, -4.0 pp vs R0; 10/12 within +-0.02 of 8; 6 adopted with the army flags (v06).
7. Own giants GIANTS=1,GIANT_TURN=80,GIANTS_MAX=2: 0.379 vs v09, -21.6 pp vs R0, -9.5 pp vs field (with the late income 0.395/-20.6/-9.4). Mechanism: 280 gold of a ~750 budget; the knights wait while the barracks saves.
8. GIANT_GUARD 150/300/500 (top up the tower a giant attacks): -1.8/-3.3/-2.5 pp vs R0; saves towers (2.7 vs 3.8 lost per game) but loses games; cause not traced.
9. ARCHERS=1 with ARCHER_RANGE 0/600/1000: dev +3.05/+1.75/+3.05 pp vs R0 (7 arms, tie-break set after the tie); screen block 2: +0.36 pp (CI -0.88..+1.60) vs R0, -0.99 pp vs field?GIANTS=1, 0 of 2000 maps changed vs the mirror. Not adopted (user, against P2's letter). Mechanism: archers cost one knight wave and kills of the enemy queen; the dev gain was the pick's luck.
10. WAVE_TOWERS 2/3 and TOPUP_FROM 2 (second tower before the first wave): vs v08 0.4675/0.3135/0.4620 and -3.7/-9.4/-3.4 pp vs field (2026-11-05); retried over v11: 0.4515/0.4470, rival -5.9/-7.3 pp, field -3.0/-2.5 pp (2026-11-07). Mechanism: two towers do meet the wave but the mean loss does not fall (7.3/8.2 vs 7.8), the first tower stays at 200 HP and melts, the line is weaker at t50 (1,464 vs 1,648 HP) and the queen dies twice as often (36 vs 18 per 400). The arena premise was the opponent's timing (medians misled: towers at contact 1.6 vs 1.7 mean in lost vs won Gold races).
11. THREAT_RANGE 350/450 alone: 0.471/0.409 vs v05 (reacting earlier stops mines and walks); 200/350/450 with THREAT_TOWERS_NEAR=2 within noise. THREAT_TOWERS_NEAR=3: 0.57-0.59 vs 0.62-0.63 for 2; =1 no effect (6 maps); =0 (defence off) -9 pp vs field. THREAT_RADIUS 600 within noise of 500; THREAT_RADIUS=350 probe over v11: 0.3925, -10.3 pp rival, -3.3 field (the forward second tower is worth keeping).
12. KITE=1 free kiting (v07): local S 0.6803 vs v06, +3.5 pp field; ARENA -0.71 (25.53 vs 26.24). Mechanism: the queen leaves tower cover (34 % of contact turns near a tower vs 90 %), knights chase 50-130 turns without dying, top-ups halve (36 vs 73), kills fall 68 -> 56. KITE_RANGE 400/500 with KITE=1: 500 -> -12 pp vs field (leaves the ladder to the faster earner), not retried with KITE=2; KITE_COVER=0 within noise.
13. KITE_PULL 30/50/200, KITE_MAX 8 (with KITE=2): pull 30/50 0.739/0.737 vs v06 against 0.785 at 100; 200 ~ 100 (0.790; probe over v11 0.5035, -0.8 pp rival, no first-wave change); the cap adds nothing.
14. STAND_REACH=155 (never stand with a knight within 155): 0.4895 vs v11, -1.95 pp rival, +0.1 field; removes the standing turns, first-wave loss unchanged (7.9 vs 7.8).
15. DEFENCE_FWD 50/150 (+DEFENCE_UNTIL 60/100): mirror S 0.548/0.515 (0.5385/0.5430 with an end), field -3.15/-2.0 pp (-3.5/-3.15 with an end); with the anchor 0.5845 vs v11 but field -2.8. Dropped; never arena-tested. Mechanism: the cost is decided in the first wave against field.
16. WAVE_ANCHOR variants: A=50 UNTIL=50 (0.5115, field -5.6, rival -3.2), UNTIL=40 (0.544, field -2.3), UNTIL=0 whole game (0.489, field -4.9), UNTIL=35 (0.552, field -1.35), UNTIL=25 (0.5575, field +0.3); A=100 (0.505, rival -5.75, field -5.15); A=25 (0.5285, field -5.05); A=75/UNTIL 35 (0.5515, field -0.85). Adopted A=50,UNTIL=30 (v12). Mechanism: towers placed deep after the first wave cost the midgame against strong economies.
17. Rejected at design (not coded): WAVE_FRONT/WAVE_BACK, WAVE_STAY, WAVE_AWAY, KITE_FWD (kiting is already net backward). Untested from the Gold study: hysteresis on the defence radius (candidate C).
18. BARRACKS=2 with BARRACKS_AFTER_TOWERS 0/2/3/5/6/8: 0.315-0.357 / 0.401-0.492 / 0.511-0.508 / 0.489 / 0.468-0.469 / 0.477-0.488 vs v05; only gate 4 + TRAIN_SYNC=1 (0.548) + MAX_TOWERS=6 (0.574/0.542 on two blocks) gained -> adopted in v06. BARRACKS=3: 0.455. Mechanism: at income 3 the gold bounds the waves (80 per wave), a second barracks adds only concentration.
19. BARRACKS_FORWARD 30/35/50/70: vs v05 0.531 / - / 0.541 & 0.486 (two blocks) / 0.517 (unsettled, dropped 2026-11-03); vs v09 35 -> 0.503 (+4.5 pp R0), 50 -> 0.5425 (+5.35 pp) -> screen 0.5426, +3.09 pp R0 -> v10; ARENA -0.20 vs v08 (inside noise; v10 beat the top: 10 of 15 vs >=21-rated).
20. RELEASE_NEAR 600/800/1000 with RELEASE_HOLD 15/30 (hold waves for the enemy queen): 0.254-0.377 vs v09, -6.9..-19.8 pp vs R0, -2.65..-10.95 field. Mechanism: the enemy queen is outside her towers' ranges on 0.2-0.9 % of turns; a hold costs one wave in ten and halves the damage per training (0.8 vs 1.5 HP).
21. LATE_HOLD 100/150/225: 0.483 (stops rebuilding too early) / 0.531 (+2.25 field) / 0.511 vs v08; 200 adopted (v09; screen S 0.5269, field +1.46 pp), never uploaded alone. Nothing exists for the trailing side (behind at t200 in 41 of 44 lost v11 races).
22. APPROACH=1 (same-site final approach): S 0.5245 (CI 0.5111-0.5379) vs v03 on screen block 2 (+0.0245 S for 2.05 walking turns); superseded by ROUTE; adoption deferred.
23. ROUTE iteration 1 (own towers/mines as diverting sites, no slide trigger): 0.5315 vs iteration 2's 0.5825 (adopted v04, eval S 0.5856 -> ARENA +0.07); the codex branch's ROUTE on block 3: S 0.5179. ROUTE steps 2-4 (unit-aware last step, target by walking turns, own towers on the route) are open; the branch's exchange rate is ~0.01-0.014 S per saved walking turn and 1-2 walking turns per game are left.
24. UNSTICK variants (MIN_STEP, detour depth): adopted as the targeted fix v02 (S 0.5046, stalls 739 -> 53 turns per 4000 games; ARENA +0.05, played as v01 in 114 of 120 games). Left: slides under 5 as stalls (13.6 % maps changed, S 0.507 dev), knight-blocked stalls (3 of 4000 games).
25. SAFE_LADDER=2 (never target the enemy half): 0.5075 vs v10, 219 of 500 maps changed, rival +0.95, field +0.85 pp: a strategy change with no clear gain; =1 adopted (v11; ARENA +0.92 within noise, tower damage 5.1 -> 0.6 HP/game).
26. The safety flag alone (THREAT_TOWERS_NEAR=2,THREAT_RADIUS=500): 0.635/0.605 on two dev blocks, not screened; with the army flags 0.680/0.629 -> screened 0.642, eval 0.6519 -> v06 (ARENA +0.85).
27. Economy as a whole (items 1-3, 6-7): four independent failures with one mechanism; a fifth attempt needs a different balance of sites (towers vs mines), not a flag on the ladder (recorded 2026-11-03 and 2026-11-06).
28. Panel/opponent variants already calibrated (not bot candidates): field?GIANTS=1 (loses 94 % vs v08; -20 pp for the field itself), field TOWER_HP 450/800, TOWERS 3/5, INCOME 10/12, MINES 2/4, THREAT_RADIUS 700; R0's neighbours (TOWERS 3/5/6, INCOME 6/10, GIANT_TURN 60/100, GIANTS_MAX 1/3/4, no giants, no kiting, TOWER_HP 800, KITE_PULL 200, KITE_RANGE 350) all leave v09 at 0.70-0.88.
GENERAL CAVEATS. (a) Arena gains are means of two placements against the selected version's mean within one league; a 2.5-point difference is at the noise margin, so only v03, v05, v08 and v12 are clearly positive and v07's negative sign is inside noise. (b) The local-vs-arena correlation (rho 0.31) rests on 10 points with three leagues and three logistic scales; Bronze predictions use scale 1.33 although later Bronze fits were 1.9-2.1. (c) Head-to-head S against one opponent and a field rating differ by construction; the ratio arena/h2h ranged from -0.7 to 3.7. (d) P2 wall times are from one logged run of 2026-11-01 (v03-era bots) plus policy statements; the current bots' series were not timed in any kept log. (e) The Gold boss has never been met in 360 Gold games; the gap to the top of Gold (6.2 points) is to the top player row, not to the boss. (f) Mechanism explanations (why the panel undervalues first-wave rules: local first-wave loss 7.3-7.8 vs Gold 11.4) are inferences from recorded profiles, not tested by changing the panel. (g) The seat asymmetry (v12 0.667 on seat 0 vs 0.556 on seat 1) is attributed to the engine by the next-step study's code reader, unverified here. (h) `old` (G3) is still absent, so every verdict since 2026-10-30 skipped G3.

primary.step: Add LADDER_CLEAR: after the first-wave window (turn >= LADDER_CLEAR_FROM, ~50, and >= 2 own towers), while an enemy knight is within LADDER_CLEAR (~500) of the queen but none within THREAT_RANGE 250, the ladder walk to a new site is paused and she walks to / tops up her nearest own tower instead, for at most LADDER_CLEAR_MAX (~15) consecutive turns per spell; kiting, the defence rule, the touch rule and the first wave are untouched.
primary.mechanism: MainBot.play rule 5, the ladder branch at line 149 (`int target = hold ? -1 : nextSite(...)`), which today ignores knights entirely (only LATE_HOLD gates it). New gate: `pause = p.LADDER_CLEAR > 0 && s.turn >= p.LADDER_CLEAR_FROM && towers >= 2 && !firstWaveWindow(s, p) && !clearOfKnights(s, qx, qy, p.LADDER_CLEAR) && (p.LADDER_CLEAR_MAX == 0 || pauseRun < p.LADDER_CLEAR_MAX)`; when it holds, take the flight's command of lines 133-136 (BUILD TOWER on `nearest(s, qx, qy, own tower)`, adding the missing `!underEnemyTower` guard there) instead of the nextSite walk, increment `pauseRun`, reset it when `clearOfKnights` is true again. `clearOfKnights` (line 380) already exists for LATE_CLEAR; `firstWaveWindow` (line 445) is WAVE_ANCHOR's window, so the anchor tower is still built with the wave visible. Three new Params fields: LADDER_CLEAR (radius, 0 = off, as v12), LADDER_CLEAR_FROM (turn), LADDER_CLEAR_MAX (spell cap, 0 = none). Optional sweep variant LADDER_CLEAR_MINES=1: pause only when nextSite's target is a mine (the income phase).
primary.evidence: Midgame reader (DeathTrace of v12's 180 Gold games, turns 50-249, deep2.out/deep3.out): in the 42 lost races 153 of 258 enemy-contact episodes (59 %) began while our queen walked the ladder (walk_mine 79, walk_tower 38, walk_barracks 22, route_move 13) and they cost 456 of 598 knight HP (76 %; 10.86 HP per lost race, 2.98 per episode) against 0.87 per episode for the 79 episodes met at a tower; in the 73 won races 248 of 473 episodes, 420 of 679 kd (5.75/game, 1.69/episode). At equal wave size the walking episode costs more (max K250 = 3: 3.45 vs 1.22 kd lost races, 1.96 vs 1.41 won; K250 = 4: 7.24 vs 6.00, 6.80 vs 1.91). The wave was visible: on the pre-contact turn a knight was within 500 in 151 of 153 walking episodes, with a median 2 warning turns (mean 2.6), the nearest own tower a median 136 away, and a 60/turn walk reaches touching distance before contact in 141 of 153 episodes (92 %) carrying 329 of 456 kd (won races 237/248, 335/420; the 29 deaths 86/95 episodes, 641 of 849 kd). The P2/P4 phase excess of our kd in lost vs won races (+2.00/+2.08 HP per game) equals the walking-episode excess (3.33 vs 1.79 and 3.24 vs 1.10 HP/game). The pause's cost side: yellow-zone turns (knight within 500, none within 250) 23.5 per lost race and 30.8 per won race in turns 50-249, in 6.9-8.5 spells of median 7-8 turns (11-12 spells >= 20 turns per 42/73 games); on them she walks 58 % (lost) / 42 % (won). Losses reader: 42 lost races have margins median -13, 10 within 5 HP, 18 within 10; +2/+4/+6/+10 HP to our final HP flips 4/9/10/17 of them (flip.py, strict lead). Code reader: contact episodes begun walking 1167 of 1743 over all 180 games at 2.58 kd/episode vs 2.09 at a tower.
primary.lossMode: HP race midgame (P2 t50-99 and P4 t150-199 carry -3.9 HP each of the lost races' -16.3 mean gap; walking-caught episodes are the whole excess) and queen death (849 of 1306 P2-P5 knight HP in the 29 deaths came in walking-caught episodes, 641 with the tower reachable); also protects the 17 of 73 won races within 5 HP.
primary.expectedGain: Re-costing the walking-caught episodes at the at-tower rate per wave size saves ~192 HP over the 42 lost races (~4.6 HP/game) and ~171 over the 73 won; +4..+6 HP flips 9-10 of 42 lost races = 5-6 of 180 games (~+3 pp S) before deaths; a third of the reachable death-episode kd (641) would be ~7 HP per death game and could turn 2-3 of the 17 siege/attrition deaths into races. Realistic 4-8 games of 180 (+2-4 pp) after the selection bias of the at-tower sample. By the Gold head-to-head conversion (scale 3.04) that is +0.6-1.3 arena points; this class (queen placement relative to knights and own towers) realised 2.7-3.7x its local S on the arena (v08 S 0.667 -> +2.46, v12 S 0.572 -> +3.28), so a step at or above the noise margin M = 2.46 is plausible but not assured.
primary.effort: Flag on existing rules: 3 Params fields, ~20 lines in MainBot.play (gate + pause counter + the flight target), a unit test on a captured position; ~0.5 day to code, ~1 day for the arena pre-screen, development sweep, screen, evaluation, submit + two procChecks and the records (P2 machine time ~10 min per screen/eval, dominated by the boss process series).
primary.p2Plan: (0) Pre-screen without games (history reader's lever 4): cgAttribute over replays/arena/v12/gold/upload-01+02/games with -Pbot=current?LADDER_CLEAR=500,LADDER_CLEAR_FROM=50,LADDER_CLEAR_MAX=15 and the arena_diff.py method; count games and turns where the decision changes, split by the 42 lost races / 29 deaths / 109 wins; expect it to fire in most lost races (yellow-zone walks ~14 turns/game) and record the upper bound. (1) Development sweep on seeds 1 + 397k (-PseedBase=1 -PseedStride=397 -Pmaps=500, both seats, -Pthreads=8 -PturnMs=50), each arm vs the v12 mirror, field and rival, plus the three controls (v12 vs the same): arms LADDER_CLEAR 400/500/600 x LADDER_CLEAR_MAX 0/15 at FROM=50, FROM=30 for the best radius, LADDER_CLEAR_MINES=1 (mines-only pause) as the low-cost fallback; ~9 arms x 3 series ~ 5 min. Choose by mirror S with field Delta >= -1 pp and rival Delta >= 0; report per seat (bench JSON aSeat) since seat 1 carries 20 of the 29 arena deaths. (2) Screen on the fresh block screen-pv3 k=6: seeds 1006000000 + 397 i, i < 2000 (-PseedBase=1006000000 -PseedStride=397; boss the first 500 maps with -Pthreads=3 -PturnMs=200): G0 zero candidate failures (repeat at -Pthreads=2 if host slow turns appear), G1 mirror S lower 95 % CI > 0.50 (needs S >= ~0.525 at 2000 maps), G2 boss Delta >= -2 pp (expected 0.000), G4 field Delta >= -2 pp (the binding gate: field's income-8 stream of 4-knight waves maximises yellow-zone turns, so the ladder delay shows there first), G5 rival Delta >= -2 pp (expected positive: its continuous waves and giants catch the walking queen as Gold's do). If more than one arm is screened on block 6, replicate the pick on block 7 (1007000000 + 397 i). (3) Mechanism tripwires alongside S: contact episodes begun walking and their kd per game (DeathTrace-style parse of local replays) down >= 30 % vs control; LegScan's ladder-completion turn delayed <= 10 turns and towers/mines built by t150 within 0.3 of control; mirror deaths per 1000 games not above control; LocalProfile first-wave loss and contact distance unchanged (the window is exempt). (4) Pass = G0-G5 met with the tripwires satisfied; then evaluation-pv3 k=2 (2002000000 + 397 i) once vs v12, submit, procCheck -Popp=v01 -Pgames=100 -PseedBase=5000 and -Popp=boss -PseedBase=6000, then tools/arena.py follow for two Gold placements (P1: rollback only below v12's mean 20.36 by > M). An eval S of 0.53-0.58 with the tripwires moving should be put to the user as an upload recommendation with the class's arena/local ratio stated, even though it is below the 0.60 letter.
primary.risks: History: every earlier widening of the reaction radius lost locally: THREAT_RANGE 350/450 alone 0.471/0.409 vs v05 ('reacting earlier stops mines and walks'), KITE_RANGE 500 with KITE=1 -12 pp vs field ('leaves the ladder to the faster earner'), THREAT_RADIUS=350 over v11 -10.3 pp vs rival. Those changed the whole threat response (defence tower, flight, touch rule, kiting) from turn 0; LADDER_CLEAR changes only the ladder walk, after the first wave, with a spell cap, and sends her to a tower (a top-up) rather than away, but it is the same trade of ladder tempo for HP, and the field gate (G4, -2 pp) is exactly where v12 already sits at -1.2..-1.5 pp vs v11, so the delay can fail G4; the mines-only variant is the fallback. The saving estimate re-costs walking episodes at the at-tower rate, which is a selected sample (waves that passed tower fire first, max K250 2.23 vs 2.69), and assumes knights head straight at her, so the true saving is smaller than 192 HP. Locally the caught-walking cost is lower than Gold's (the panel's first wave costs 7.3-7.8 HP vs Gold 11.4), so a true +1.5 pp effect could fail G1's lower-CI rule (SE ~1.2 pp at 2000 maps); the arena undervaluation of this class (v08, v12) cuts both ways. Delayed mine rebuilds cost income, but in lost races rebuilt mines live a median 18 turns and 104 of 124 were built 151-400 from the nearest tower, so the forgone income is small; delayed towers/barracks against strong economies are the real cost (longer WAVE_UNTIL windows cost the midgame for the same reason). Fewer walks should lower deaths (the opposite of INCOME_LATE's 63 vs 47 per 1000), but the pause parks her at the tower nearest her, which may be a forward one; the underEnemyTower guard on that target is required. The first wave must stay exempt (FROM >= 30 or firstWaveWindow), or v12's anchor gain is at risk.

runnerUp.step: Bound the TRAIN_SYNC hold in MainBot.train(): release knights from an idle barracks when (a) the enemy queen is at or below SYNC_KILL_HP (~20) and gold >= 80, (b) from turn DUMP_FROM (~230) whenever 80 gold is banked, and (c) when the wait to 80 x idle barracks at the current income would exceed SYNC_WAIT_MAX turns (~30); otherwise keep the 8-knight synchronous wave.
runnerUp.mechanism: MainBot.train() line 216: `if (p.TRAIN_SYNC == 1 && (idle <= 0 || gold < cost)) return ...` holds every release while any barracks trains or the gold does not cover all idle barracks (160 with two). New: before that line, `boolean release = idle >= 1 && gold >= Const.CREEP_COST[KNIGHT] && ((p.SYNC_KILL_HP > 0 && s.hp[1] <= p.SYNC_KILL_HP) || (p.DUMP_FROM > 0 && s.turn >= p.DUMP_FROM) || (p.SYNC_WAIT_MAX > 0 && gold < cost && (cost - gold) > p.SYNC_WAIT_MAX * Math.max(1, income)))`; when it holds, skip the sync return and let the existing loop (lines 223-230) train the barracks the gold covers in id order. The income total already computed in play() (line 75) is stored in a field for train(). Three new Params fields (SYNC_KILL_HP, DUMP_FROM, SYNC_WAIT_MAX; 0 = off, as v12). RELEASE_NEAR/RELEASE_HOLD (hold longer for proximity) stay off; this is the opposite direction, a bounded hold.
runnerUp.evidence: Losses reader (gold series of ours-upload-01/02.txt; q5_out, q6_out, q7_out): over 38252 turns of 180 games, 8082 turns (21 % of all, 48 % of the 16928 turns with two barracks; B >= 2 reached in 132 of 180 games) hold 80-159 gold with an idle barracks and no training; 219 starvation streaks >= 20 turns (1.22/game, 6652 turns = 17 % of all; 68 at income <= 2, 135 at 3-4, 16 at >= 5; longest 80 turns in 918167057 at income 1, a race lost by 9). Code reader: the 80-gold-to-release wait with two barracks is median 22 turns, mean 24.9 (n = 263 double releases vs 1055 single ones); our gold float 81 at B2 vs the opponents' 60. Trainings per game 7.3 vs the opponents' 10.9 (deaths 6.3 vs 11.6; strong >= 20 opponents 11.9 events at 14-turn gaps, 86 gold each, with equal damage per gold vs us: 2.98 vs 2.83 HP per 100 gold, opponents reader). Gold left at the end of the 42 lost races: median 89, >= 80 in 23 of 42 (won races 25 of 73); the 10 races lost within 9 HP that ended with >= 83 gold and two barracks: 918158655 (-1, 83), 918165015 (-1, 162, last training t208), 918169416 (-1, 132), 918145702 (-3, 102), 918146673 (-3, 145, t201), 918149783 (-5, 96), 918148960 (-8, 95), 918158656 (-8, 119, no training after t150 at income 1), 918143673 (-9, 105), 918152187 (-9, 144). Kill-shot turns (enemy queen <= 20 HP, our gold >= 80, B >= 2, no training): 1281 turns in 37 games; in 5 losses: 918145702 73 turns (lost by 3), 918167279 55 (death; enemy at 10 HP, our gold 147, 100 turns since the last wave at income 1), 918148596 16 (death; enemy 17 HP, gold 129), 918150876 9 (lost race), 918150968 6 (death; enemy 13 HP, gold 104); the enemy queen reached <= 20 HP and survived in 37 games (23 won races, 10 deaths, 4 lost races). Midgame reader: when trailing after t200 our gold held 79 mean, one release per ~50 turns at income ~3, our knights within 250 of their queen only 3.3 turns/game.
runnerUp.lossMode: HP race last 50 turns (gold worthless at turn 250 left unspent in 23 of 42 lost races, 6 of them within 5 HP), queen death with the enemy queen low (3 deaths with the enemy at 10-17 HP and 104-147 gold banked), and vs strong opponents (their 11.9 waves at 14-turn gaps vs our 7.3 at 20).
runnerUp.expectedGain: Upper bound 8 of 180 games (+4.4 pp): the 5 lost races within 5 HP with >= 83 gold left plus the 3 close deaths with >= 100 gold and two barracks; realistic 2-4 games (+1-2 pp) because the released 4 knights must pass T4-T9 enemy towers and a kiting queen (our knights' kd per contact episode on queen-safe opponents is 1.09, 73 % of episodes with 0). That is +0.3-0.6 Gold points by the head-to-head conversion, below the arena's resolution with two placements (M = 2.46), so alone it is a tooling-measurable but arena-invisible step; its value is as a second flag in the primary's artifact (one upload) or as a gain across all games from ~20-40 % more waves that the traces cannot size.
runnerUp.effort: Flags on an existing rule: 3 Params fields, ~12 lines in train() plus passing the income total from play(); ~0.5 day to code with a unit test on a captured state, ~1 day of P2 (sweep, screen, eval, procChecks, records).
runnerUp.p2Plan: (1) Development sweep on 1 + 397k (500 maps, both seats, -Pthreads=8 -PturnMs=50) vs the v12 mirror, field and rival with controls: arms DUMP_FROM=230 alone; SYNC_KILL_HP=20 alone; SYNC_WAIT_MAX=20/30/40 alone; the best of each combined. Report trainings per game, gold at t250, enemy queen HP at the end, our deaths per 1000, kd dealt per training (bench traces) beside S; split by seat. Expected signs: DUMP_FROM and SYNC_KILL_HP >= 0 everywhere (they spend otherwise-dead gold); SYNC_WAIT_MAX is the risky arm and is dropped if field or rival lose >= 1 pp. (2) Screen on the next fresh block after the primary's (screen-pv3 k=7: 1007000000 + 397 i, i < 2000; boss the first 500): G0, G1 mirror lower CI > 0.50 (the mirror is 91 % HP races and both sides hoard identically at B2, so extra releases show directly as HP; expect S 0.51-0.54, so G1 may miss on a true small gain), G2 boss >= -2 pp, G4 field >= -2 pp (4 towers at 600 kill 4-knight releases: the tripwire for SYNC_WAIT_MAX), G5 rival >= -2 pp (its kiting queen under 4 towers tests whether late releases ever land). (3) Pass = G0-G5 with trainings per game up, end gold down and deaths per 1000 not up; then either bundle with the primary for one evaluation on evaluation-pv3 k=2 (2002000000 + 397 i) and one upload under P1, or, if the primary fails, evaluate alone and hand the user the decision with the arena-invisibility caveat stated.
runnerUp.risks: TRAIN_SYNC was adopted in v06 for a reason: the second barracks at gate 4 scored 0.548 vs v05 only with the sync (gates 3/5 without it 0.51/0.49), and the physics favour concentration: with towers killing at a roughly fixed rate per turn, knight-turns alive scale with the square of the wave size (8 knights ~ 2x the knight-turns of two 4-knight waves), so SYNC_WAIT_MAX with a short N would lose; N must sit above the median hold (22 turns) so that only the income <= 2 holds (68 of 219 streaks) break. RELEASE_NEAR/RELEASE_HOLD (0.25-0.38 vs v09, -7..-20 pp vs R0) shows that touching the release rule can lose a lot, though in the opposite direction. The opponents' equal damage per gold with smaller waves is observational and style-confounded (they also have 1.7-2x our income). The panel undervalued army/economy classes before and the arena never confirmed one (v06 +0.85, v10 -0.20 within noise), so even a local pass predicts little; the mirror cannot show the kill-shot value (both queens kite under six towers; mirror deaths are rare), only rival can. The endgame dump is free of strategic cost but a 4-knight wave spawned at t235 reaches a covered queen for at most 5-10 turns, so its effect lives in the 1-HP races (4 of 42 lost by exactly 1, all on seat 1) and may not register in 2000 maps.

result.whyNotOthers: Enemy-tower-aware flight and idle pump (losses lever 3, midgame lever 2, code lever 2a): correct and near-certain, but it is worth 114 HP over 180 games (2.7 % of the 4156 HP we lost; 138 of 192 enemy-tower turns at own towers) and flips at most one lost race (918150190, td 7 = the gap), so about +0.5 pp, invisible under P1 and weakly measurable (field/rival rarely cover our home tower); it belongs in the primary's artifact as the `!underEnemyTower` guard on the pause/flight target plus a regression test, not as a step. Stop pumping a capped tower / maintenance walk to the lowest tower (opponents lever 1, code lever 3): the waste is clear (52 turns per game beyond the third consecutive build on one tower, 24.7 % of turns alive; summed tower HP at t200 in lost races 2378 over 6 towers vs the opponents' 2800 over 5 despite 92.5 vs 69.5 top-ups) but the link to outcomes is low-confidence, it moves the idle queen between towers in the midgame (INCOME_LATE's walks raised mirror deaths 63 vs 47 per 1000, UPGRADE walks changed nothing), and it needs a new target choice rather than a gate; a good second-wave candidate once LADDER_CLEAR has shown whether walks under visible waves can be made safe. Seat-aware DEFENCE_FWD on seat 1 (seat lever 1): the cause is established (collision order; seat 1 loses 8.38 vs 5.01 HP to the first wave and dies 20/99 vs 9/81) and the bot knows its seat, but the dev-block effect is +1.9 pp S with field -1.7 pp on one 500-map block (2 SE), worth +0.2-0.3 Gold points, and P2's tooling does not yet report per seat; it is a refinement to fold into a later first-wave step, not a step. The second tower before the wave without starving the first (firstwave lever 1) is a variant of the twice-rejected WAVE_TOWERS/TOPUP_FROM family that doubled queen deaths (36 vs 18 per 400 games); its new mechanism (tower-HP kill rate -> adjacency) is inferred from the damage formula, not measured, and it acts inside the window where v12's whole gain lives, the worst place to gamble under a low-risk lens. The economy levers (midgame mine interleave, Legend balance, income after the ladder) cannot be judged by the panel (PV3/PV5 record the strong-economy pressure as unrepresented; four local economy arms failed for one structural reason) and would need an exception upload to be judged at all. The rollout-based threat response (code lever 1) is a new subsystem with G0 risk (JIT warm-up, 50 ms) and days of work. LATE_HOLD for the trailing side is not a lever: in the 44 games trailing at t200 our queen lost 7 HP on 598 walking-out turns, 149 at her towers. Mine rebuilds only under cover (midgame lever 3) is a strict subset of LADDER_CLEAR's mines-only arm, so it is covered by the sweep rather than proposed separately.

primary.step: Add a first-wave top-up cap: while fewer than 2 own towers stand and an enemy knight wave is visible (knightWaveComing), top up the touched first tower only while its HP is below WAVE_TOWER_HP (sweep 400/500/600 instead of TOWER_HP=700), so the queen leaves for the second (WAVE_ANCHOR) site 2-3 turns earlier and meets the enemy's first wave with two towers standing, then pumps both to 700 as today.
primary.mechanism: MainBot.play touch rule, MainBot.java:121 (`s.stType[t]==TOWER && owner 0 && s.towerHp[t] < p.TOWER_HP && topUp`): new Params int WAVE_TOWER_HP (0 = off); the effective threshold becomes (WAVE_TOWER_HP > 0 && towers < 2 && knightWaveComing(s)) ? WAVE_TOWER_HP : TOWER_HP (a second sweep arm uses `towers < 2` alone or firstWaveWindow(s,p) as the trigger). Nothing else moves: the defence rule (:97-110), KITE=2, WAVE_ANCHOR's target choice (nextSite :432-435) and the 700 threshold once two towers stand are v12's. Chain: tower 1 is built at ~t14 and pumped 5 times to 700 (first tower HP at contact 652 vs 672 in the one-tower regime), the walk to site 2 takes 3-4 turns and tower 2 completes at t25.2 (lost races) / 24.9 (won) while the contact comes at 24.5 vs 27.3; 2-3 fewer pumps put tower 2 up before the contact, so (a) the defence rule no longer fires at contact (2 towers within THREAT_RADIUS 500) and the 2.9-turn walk-and-build under knights (1.7 HP/turn, 4.7 HP per lost race vs 1.8 per won) disappears, and (b) two towers (~450 and 200→700) fire on the knights adjacent to her instead of one 196-HP tower, raising the kill rate that governs adjacent turns (Rules.java:355: damage 3 + (range − dist)/200 per tower, one target each). Why it is not the rejected WAVE_TOWERS=2/TOPUP_FROM=2: those set `topUp = !wave` / `towers >= TOPUP_FROM`, i.e. zero top-ups before the second tower, leaving both towers at ~200 HP (range ~260), the first melted out (summed tower HP at t50 1648 → 1464/1436), the line was weaker and deaths doubled (18 → 36 per 400); at 450 HP the first tower keeps range ~380 (vs ~480 at 700) and 60 turns of melt before 200. Global TOWER_HP 400/500 also lost (0.293 vs v04, −7 pp field), so the cap is conditional on the pre-second-tower wave window only.
primary.evidence: First-wave reader (v12's 115 Gold HP races, summary.csv + traces): lossK20 10.24 (42 lost) vs 3.42 (73 won), bootstrap diff +6.8 HP (CI +3.7..+10.3); adjacent turns (knight ≤ 60) 5.17 vs 2.07; OLS lossK20 = 1.88 × adjTurns, R² 0.89; kiting metrics identical (moves20 10.1 vs 10.3, meanNearTower20 120 vs 118). Towers at contact 1.43 vs 1.75 (MW p=0.017; one tower in 22/42 lost vs 25/73 won), coverQ 1.40 vs 1.70, contact 24.5 vs 27.3 (p=0.021), 2nd tower completes at 25.2 vs 24.9 (p=0.73), 2nd tower at/after contact in 31/42 lost vs 35/73 won. Gradient over the 176 games with a contact (q8-v12.txt): t2rel [−99,−3) n=34 won 21 (0.62) lossK20 3.5; [−3,0) n=47 won 36 (0.77) 3.4; [0,3) n=56 won 32 (0.57) 7.7; [3,99) n=39 won 16 (0.41) 12.9. Against ≥20-rated opponents: 2nd tower before contact won 11/19 (0.58), lossK20 4.3; at/after won 11/39 (0.28), lossK20 12.0 (opponents <20: 46/62 = 0.74 vs 37/56 = 0.66). Kill-speed proxy ttk = waveHP / Σ(3 + hp//200): bands 0-4 lossK20 1.1 (n=37, towers 2.16), 4-6 3.6 (32), 6-8 6.3 (16), 8-12 13.8 (22, towers 1.00); ttk explains 43% of the adjacent-turn variance. One-tower regime (24 lost / 25 won): first tower HP equal (652 vs 672), new tower completes 3.5 vs 2.2 turns after contact (p=0.008), walk turns to its site under knights 2.9 vs 1.7 (p=0.009), adjacent turns 7.9 vs 4.2. Early-barracks opponents (first barracks ≤ 8): 42/180 games, won 21 (0.50), contact 22.5, towers at contact 1.24; corr(contact, opponent firstBarracks) 0.77 — the timing is theirs, the second tower's is ours. Counterfactuals (q5/q8): lost races with the 2nd tower at/after contact → before-contact mean lossK20 2.0: 9/31 flip; one-tower lost races → two-tower mean: 8/24; lossK20 → won mean: 10/42. Code reader: defence walk+build 581 HP over 180 games (4.7 per lost race, 1.8 per won, 5.7 per death). Local reference (docs/data/exp-2026-11-05-first-wave/README.md, 200 maps vs v08): v08 meets the first wave at t24 with 1 tower; WAVE_TOWERS=2/TOPUP_FROM=2 met it at t23 with 2 towers but mean 20-turn loss 7.3/8.2 vs 7.8, tower HP at t50 1464/1436 vs 1648, deaths 36/36 vs 18 per 400; the panel (mirror t24/1 tower, field 21/1, rival 25/1) exercises exactly this regime.
primary.lossMode: HP race, first wave, against strong opponents: the 24 lost races vs ≥20-rated opponents (within ≥20 lossK20 9.7 lost vs 3.3 won; 39 of our 58 games vs ≥20 had the second tower at/after contact and we won 11 of them). Secondarily the 6 early queen deaths (≤ t106; lossK20 mean 9.4 in death games) and the defence-rule HP.
primary.expectedGain: Upper bound from the recorded games, rest of the game fixed: 8-9 of 180 flip (+4.5-5 pp) when the at/after lost races take the before-contact lossK20 (9/31) or the one-tower lost races the two-tower mean (8/24). In the task's lens: moving the 39 at/after games vs ≥20 (won 11, 0.28) to the before-contact rate 0.58 would be +11-12 games of 58; halving for confounding by opponent strength (corr(t2rel, rating) 0.21) gives +6 of 58, i.e. S vs ≥20 from 0.39 to ~0.45-0.49. Realistic after costs (first tower at ~450 instead of ~700 at contact, symmetric exposure 6/25 won one-tower races): +3-5 games of 180 (+2-3 pp), concentrated on ≥20 opponents (at/after bucket 39/58 of them vs 56/118 of the <20). Arena conversion: +2-3 pp against a fixed field is only +0.3-0.4 rating points at Gold's logistic scale 3.04 (dP/dR 0.078/pt at p 0.61), but both uploads of this queen-placement/first-wave class realised 2.7-3.7x their local head-to-head prediction (v12: local S 0.5716 → +3.28 placement points; v08: 0.667 → +2.46), and this step acts in the same window on the same opponents as v12, so a step at or above M = 2.46 is plausible but not assured; below ~2.5 points two placements per side cannot see it.
primary.effort: Flag on an existing rule: one Params int, one conditional in the touch rule, a unit test on a captured one-tower position (plus a small 'second tower turn minus contact' column in LocalProfile/WaveTrace). About 0.5 day code, 1 day sweep + screen + eval, 1-2 hours tests/submit/two procChecks, ~25 min arena follow per placement; 2-3 days end to end.
primary.p2Plan: Step 0 (minutes, no games): arena_diff-style replay of v12's 180 Gold games with the flag (cgAttribute -Pbot=current?WAVE_TOWER_HP=500) to count the games and turns where the first decision changes (expected: nearly all, at t16-19) and confirm it precedes the contact in the 31 at/after lost races. Development sweep on 1+397k (500 maps, both seats, in-process, -Pthreads=8): WAVE_TOWER_HP ∈ {400, 500, 600} × trigger {knightWaveComing, towers<2 alone} = 6 arms vs ctrl-v12 mirror, field and rival (3 control series); LocalProfile tripwires per arm: first contact turn and own towers at contact (expect 2 in a majority), HP lost in the 20 turns from contact, summed own tower HP at t50 (baseline ~1648; the rejected flags 1464/1436), queen deaths per 400 (baseline 18; rejected 36), defence BUILDs ahead under knights (FW_DEF_AHEAD/FW_DEF_LOSS). Choose the arm with the best S vs mirror and rival whose field Δ ≥ −2 pp and deaths ≤ control. Screen on block screen-pv3 k=6 (seeds 1006000000 + 397·i, i < 2000; boss on the first 500, -Pthreads=3 -PturnMs=200): G0 (0 candidate failures; repeat at -Pthreads=2 on host slow turns), G1 mirror lower 95% CI > 0.50, G2 boss Δ ≥ −2 pp, G4 field Δ ≥ −2 pp, G5 rival Δ ≥ −2 pp; G3 skipped (no `old`), recorded. Final evaluation once on evaluation-pv3 k=2 (2002000000 + 397·i) against v12. What a pass looks like: S 0.52-0.56 vs v12 (the panel's first waves cost 7.3-7.8 HP vs Gold's 10.2 in lost races, so the local effect is damped as for v12), field within −2 pp (its t21 contact is the early-barracks regime where we score 0.50 on the arena), rival ≥ 0, deaths not above control, 20-turn loss down ≥ 1 HP, towers at contact 2 in most games; field shows the effect first, the mirror decides G1. The S ≥ 0.60 recommendation will probably not be met (v12 had 0.5716); the upload is the user's decision. After upload: cgStudy/WaveTrace on the new agent's games must show the share with the 2nd tower before contact above 81/176 = 46% and lossK20 in lost races below 10.2, deaths not above 29/180.
primary.risks: (1) A third point in a twice-rejected family (WAVE_TOWERS/TOPUP_FROM: 2026-11-05 vs v08 S 0.4675/0.4620, field −3.7/−3.4 pp; 2026-11-07 vs v11 0.4515/0.4470, rival −5.9/−7.3, field −3.0/−2.5). The recorded failure (first tower at 200 melts, line weaker at t50, deaths ×2) is exactly what the 400-600 cap avoids, and the sweep's tripwires detect a repeat; but it may turn out the second tower's timing was standing in for the opponent's timing, as the 2026-11-05 README concluded for Silver. (2) The gradient is partly opponent quality (early barracks = stronger: corr(t2rel, rating) 0.21, corr(contact, rating) −0.22); all flip counts hold the rest of the game fixed; the symmetric exposure is 6/25 won one-tower races. (3) The first tower at ~450 covers ~380 instead of ~480: if the anchor site is far she can be caught between two weak towers; TOWER_HP 400/500 as global thresholds lost badly, so the cap must stay conditional and the 600 arm is the safe fallback. (4) The panel's waves are smaller than Gold's (local one-tower 20-turn loss 5-7 HP vs 10-12 on the arena), so a true gain may show locally as S 0.52-0.55 and fail the 0.60 recommendation; conversely G4 was nearly binding for v12 (−1.49 pp) and could reject a true gain. (5) Arena resolution: M = 2.46 with two placements hides steps under ~2.5 points; a 1-point step needs ~13 placements per side.

runnerUp.step: Gate the midgame ladder walk by knight proximity (LADDER_CLEAR): once two towers stand and the first-wave window is over, when an enemy knight is within LADDER_CLEAR (sweep 400/500) of the queen and an own tower exists, replace the ladder's walk to a new site by the rule-4 flight to the nearest own tower (BUILD TOWER there, a top-up on arrival) for at most LADDER_CLEAR_MAX consecutive turns per spell, then resume the ladder.
runnerUp.mechanism: MainBot.play rule 5 (`cmd == null` → nextSite + RoutePlanner.plan, MainBot.java:148-164, and the INCOME_LATE branch :165-175): new Params ints LADDER_CLEAR (radius, 0 = off) and LADDER_CLEAR_MAX (spell cap); gate `towers >= 2 && !firstWaveWindow(s,p) && !clearOfKnights(s, qx, qy, p.LADDER_CLEAR) && spell < LADDER_CLEAR_MAX` → `nearest(s, qx, qy, own TOWER)` BUILD (the flight of rule 4, :133-136), counter reset when clear. clearOfKnights (:380) exists and is used today only by LATE_CLEAR; firstWaveWindow (:445) is v12's. THREAT_RANGE 250, the defence rule, KITE=2 and the touch rule are untouched, so contacts are fought as today; only the decision to start or continue a walk to a new site while a wave is 250-500 away changes. Optional second arm: the own tower farthest from the knights' centroid instead of the nearest. primary.evidence: Where the HP goes (code reader, trace_levers section 1, trace_quirks D-E; 180 Gold games): 8615 contact turns of 38252 (47.9/game, 23%); knight damage 4038 of the 4156 HP lost; kite steps 2679 HP (7325 turns, 0.37/turn, 0.97/turn when the nearest knight is <= 120), standing/fleeing in reach 755 HP (291 turns at 2.55-2.63/turn), defence walk+build 581 HP (541 turns at 1.0-1.3/turn). Lost races vs won: kite 16.5 vs 9.4 HP/game, defence 4.7 vs 1.8, in-reach stand/flee 3.5 vs 1.5; deaths 33.8 / 5.7 / 14.8; margins median 13 (10 of 42 within 5); per game, half the kite HP >= the margin in 8 of 42 lost races, stand+defence in 8 of 42, kite whole in 22 of 42. After a kite step a knight is still within 250 next turn in 5754/7292 (79%): the step itself sheds nothing (knights 100 vs queen 60), the fight is decided by tower kill speed and pack tightness. First wave (firstwave reader q7/q8, 115 races): lossK20 = 1.88 x adjacent turns (R2 0.89); adjacent turns 5.17 vs 2.07; damage rate at contact median 6 vs 10; ttk explains 43% of adjacency variance; towers hit one creep per turn, so the fight's position relative to the towers (damage 3 at the edge, up to 5-6 near a 700-HP tower's centre) and the number of covering towers set the kill rate; the static rule has no such term. Collision order matters (seat reader toy port of Physics/Rules: a standing queen takes 19 HP as P0 vs 36 as P1 over 12 turns from 4 knights; fleeing cuts 48 -> 26 and 25 -> 18): kite() cannot see it, Rules reproduces it. Cost model (code reader): 5 collision passes x E(E-1) sqrt pairs, E = creeps + 2 + nSites (<= 24); creeps alive median 12 at t25 (max 16), 2-4 at t50-200 (p90 8-11, max 20) -> 4.4k-7.8k pairs per simulated turn typical, 15k worst, estimated 0.05-0.3 ms (unbenchmarked); 27 x 5 = 135 turns per real turn -> 7-40 ms worst, against a free budget of about 30 ms (50 - 7.7 measured max - 10 margin) -> the work budget or a local sub-state (entities within 600) must be sized by the benchmark. Everything the horizon needs is in the local view except enemy gold and the enemy queen's intent: barracks progress (InputReader lines 81-84), tower HP/range, creep HP; spawns within 5 turns are exact. History (history reader): the two largest arena steps were queen-under-knights changes undervalued locally (v08 KITE=2 S 0.667 -> +2.46; v12 anchor 0.5716 -> +3.28); the one that left cover (v07 KITE=1, S 0.680) gave -0.71.

primary.risks: (1) G0 and tail latency: CG runs one CPU with an unknown JIT state, and Rules has never run inside the artifact's warm-up, so a cold rollout at the first contact (turn ~24) could exceed 50 ms; mitigations are the warm-up extension, the deadline cut, LegScan tail times and procCheck on both seats. (2) Model mismatch: the enemy queen WAITs in the sim (she MOVEs on 44-51% of turns; within 5 turns only her top-ups matter), enemy TRAINs are unknown (they spawn >= 5 turns later), and the stdin order of creeps may differ from the referee's internal order used in collision resolution; the prediction test decides, and a biased simulator would be worse than the static rule. (3) Horizon myopia: one 700-HP tower needs about 24 turns to kill a 4-knight pack (one target per turn), so 5 turns see only damage dealt; a large SIM_KILL can make her stand to farm tower damage and bleed, the v07-type artefact the stand-still local opponents reward; keep the cover constraint hard and the kill weight small in phase 1. (4) Panel bias: field never kites and rewards any mobility, rival kites and plays giants in 85% of its games, the mirror over-weights races; the panel predicted +1.0 for v07 and the arena gave -0.71, so after an upload the arena mechanism metrics (share of contact turns at own towers, 90% for v12; HP per contact turn 0.47) must be checked, not only the placement. (5) Reproducibility: a time-budgeted search makes repeated bench runs produce different games; hence the fixed work budget with the deadline as a counted safety cut. (6) The history of per-step tweaks is flat (STAND_REACH 155 neutral, KITE_PULL 200 neutral, KITE_MAX nothing): the rollout's new content is exact knight motion, collision pushes, tower damage rates and the stand-versus-step trade; if the development sweep shows <= 2 HP/game of saving, the subsystem still pays as the platform for phases 2-3, but that is a decision for the user after day 1's prediction test and benchmark, before the controller is written. (7) Effort creep: phase 1 stays in-contact only; pre-contact triggers and the defence rule are later phases.

runnerUp.step: Add an open-loop wave model, knightEta(s): the turn when the enemy's knights (the ones alive, at 100 per turn, and the ones a visible enemy knight barracks will spawn in 5 - progress turns) reach our queen or the tower she would hold, and gate two existing decisions on it: (a) in the first-wave window, walk to the second tower site only if its build completes >= ETA_MARGIN (2-3) turns before the ETA, otherwise pump the first tower (ETA_PUMP_TO=500 instead of 700) and hold at it; (b) after the window, abort a ladder, mine or barracks walk and return to the nearest own tower that covers her when the ETA is shorter than the turns to finish the walk plus one build plus the return, resuming when no knight is within 500 (clearOfKnights). This is the structural alternative when the rollout subsystem is not affordable: the same prediction, done as arithmetic instead of simulation and search.
runnerUp.mechanism: New rule (about 80 lines) in MainBot.play before the ladder (rule 5, lines 148-163) and in the touch rule's top-up threshold (line 121, TOWER_HP replaced by ETA_PUMP_TO while towers < 2 and a wave is coming): knightEta over s.cx/cy with Const.CREEP_SPEED[KNIGHT] = 100 and the enemy knight barracks' barrProgress/barrTraining (InputReader lines 81-84 set them from p1; CREEP_BUILD_TIME 5), the walk time from the existing MainBot.walkTurns / Physics.queenStep or RoutePlanner's plan length; flags WAVE_ETA=1, ETA_MARGIN, ETA_PUMP_TO, ETA_RETREAT=1, ETA_SPELL_MAX (a cap per spell like KITE_MAX). It differs from the rejected WAVE_TOWERS/TOPUP_FROM (static tower counts that skipped all top-ups, so both towers sat at 200 HP and the first one melted, summed tower HP at t50 1464 vs 1648, deaths doubled) by the time criterion and by keeping the first tower's HP; it differs from LADDER_CLEAR or KITE_RANGE 500 (distance triggers; v07's 500 lost 12 pp against field by leaving the ladder) by acting only when the wave arrives before the walk can finish, on the 2-3 turns of warning the traces show. No collision simulation and no candidate search; phase 3 of the primary would replace it with simulated candidates, so nothing is wasted if both are built.
