Screen the single best arm on screen-pv3 k=6 (seeds 1006000000 + 397 i, i < 2000; k=7 if the primary took 6): G0; G1 mirror lower CI > 0.50 (first contact at turn 24 with one tower: the regime the rule targets); G4 field >= -2 pp (contact at 21 with one tower; the binding gate: the static flags lost 3-9 pp here and v12 itself -1.49 pp); G5 rival >= -2 pp (contact at 25; kiting and giants); G2 boss as a formality (0.0000 deltas in the last six screens). A pass looks like: S lower CI > 0.50 with t2rel shifted negative by >= 2 turns in the mirror, lossK20 down from 4.3 to <= 3, summed tower HP at t50 within 100 of v12's, deaths per 1000 not up against field, field delta >= -2 pp; report per seat (the rules' tilt costs seat 1 the first wave: 8.38 vs 5.01 HP, and flags have moved the seats by 5-6 pp differently). Final evaluation on evaluation-pv3 k=2 (2002000000 + 397 i) against v12 before any upload. Pre-screen first: the arena-replay diff over v12's 180 Gold games, counting in how many of the 42 lost races and 29 deaths the ETA gate would have changed a command.
runnerUp.risks: The family was rejected twice (2026-11-05 against v08, 2026-11-07 against v11) with a recorded mechanism: two towers met the wave but the mean loss did not fall (7.3/8.2 vs 7.8), the first tower stayed at 200 HP and melted, deaths doubled; the ETA gate's fallback is v12's play (pump and wait), so the regression is bounded to the games where the ETA says 'in time' and is wrong, but the local one-tower loss (5-7 HP) is smaller than Gold's (10.2 in lost races), so the screen may show S 0.52-0.55 for a change the arena rewards, as v12 did (0.5716 -> +3.28). The ETA ignores collisions and sites (knights slowed by obstacles, the queen's own blocked path), so the margin must absorb +-1-2 turns. Part of the t2rel gradient is opponent quality (strong players build early; within >= 20-rated opponents the cell is 19 vs 39 games) and the kill-speed -> adjacency -> loss chain is inferred (the recorded first-10-turn tower damage differs only 5.06 vs 5.59, p=0.06). The retreat (b) delays the ladder (23.5 yellow-zone turns per lost race, 12% of turns 50-249) and the mirror punishes lost tempo; cap the spell and exempt the first-wave window, where WAVE_ANCHOR's tower must be built with the wave visible. The per-game re-costing shows (b) does not flip the close lost races (2-3 of 42), so its gain rests on the deaths, where survival also needs the economy; G4 is the gate most likely to fail, as for v12.

result.whyNotOthers: TRAIN_SYNC relaxation (SYNC_WAIT_MAX, kill-shot release, DUMP_FROM 230): the strongest cheap army flag by evidence (8082 of 38252 turns, 21%, held with 80-159 gold and two barracks; gold >= 80 at the end of 23 of 42 lost races; 1281 kill-shot turns in 37 games), but its realistic gain is 2-4 games of 180 (+1-2 pp) because the released 4 knights must cross 4-9 enemy towers, v06 adopted the sync for a measured reason (0.548 vs 0.49 without it), and the panel has never ordered army changes with the arena (v10 -0.20); it is not a structural step and belongs as a bundled companion flag in the same artifact as either proposal, where a bundle is what the arena's resolution (M 2.46 at two placements) can see. Post-ladder economy and tower maintenance (pump the lowest tower, never at the 800 cap; mine interleave; a Legend-style balance): the waste is real (52.4 pump turns per game beyond the third on one tower, 24.7% of turns alive, against 20.5 for strong Gold and 10.6 for Legend; summed tower HP 2378 vs 2800 at t200 despite 92.5 vs 69.5 top-ups) and the 29 deaths are economic collapses (opponent income >= 2x ours in 23 of 29), but the 42 lost races are against turtles with our economy (maxIncome 7.7 vs 8.3 in won races), every economy arm failed locally for a recorded structural reason (our half's sites are towers at ladder completion, late mines are far), PV3/PV5 record that the panel cannot measure late economy, and only an arena exception could judge it; the tower-maintenance part (own sites only) is the one new mechanism and is the natural phase-2 idle-time term of the rollout, not the next step. Seat-aware hedging (DEFENCE_FWD on seat 1, an adjacency rule): the tilt is the referee's collision order (the repository fix of 2018-04-28 never reached the live game) and can only be hedged; halving v12's seat gap is worth +0.25-0.4 Gold points, inside M, and the per-seat flag effects (+5-6 pp between seats) are about 2 SE on one 500-map block; worth per-seat reporting in bench_pair and a free re-read of the existing reports, not a step. Enemy-tower-aware flight and idle pump: 114 HP over 180 games (2.7% of the HP lost), one lost race decided (918150190, td 7 = the gap); a near-certain targeted fix to bundle with either proposal (the rollout's enemy-range penalty contains it), not a step. LADDER_CLEAR as a pure distance rule: subsumed by the runner-up's time-based retreat, and the per-game re-costing shows its value is in the deaths (17.9 HP per death), not in the close races (2-3 of 42 flip), so the midgame reader's uniform +4..+6 HP estimate (9-10 flips) overstates it. Giants, archers, RELEASE_NEAR and larger merged releases against queen-safe opponents: the enemy queen is outside her towers' ranges on 0.2-0.9% of turns, giants cost 21 pp against rival, archers were noise, and no local opponent plays Gold's tower-covered queen, so the arena alone could judge them; the lever is the opponent's to deny. Panel and process levers (rival?GIANTS=0, a FieldBot first-wave knob calibrated to Gold's 11.4 HP, shorter boss series, the arena-replay pre-screen, per-seat reporting): they improve how a step is judged, not the bot, and the pre-screen and per-seat report should accompany both proposals rather than replace them.

primary.step: LADDER_CLEAR: after the first-wave window (turn >= WAVE_UNTIL=30 or no enemy knight barracks) and once >= 2 own towers stand, when an enemy knight is within LADDER_CLEAR=500 of the queen but none within THREAT_RANGE=250, replace the ladder walk (nextSite/RoutePlanner and the INCOME_LATE walk) by BUILD TOWER on the nearest own tower not inside an enemy tower's range (walk there, top up on arrival) until no knight is within 500 or the spell exceeds LADDER_CLEAR_MAX (~12 turns); kiting, the defence rule and the touch rule stay as they are.
primary.mechanism: MainBot.play, the ladder branch at lines 148-179 (`target = hold ? -1 : nextSite(...)`, then `route.plan`): a new gate before it, `p.LADDER_CLEAR > 0 && threat == 0 && towers >= 2 && !firstWaveWindow(s, p) && !clearOfKnights(s, qx, qy, p.LADDER_CLEAR) && pauseRun < p.LADDER_CLEAR_MAX` -> `cmd = Command.build(nearest(s, qx, qy, i -> own TOWER && !underEnemyTower(s, i)), "TOWER")` (rule 4's flight form, lines 133-136, with the enemy-range guard the flight lacks); `clearOfKnights` (line 380, today used only by LATE_CLEAR for the INCOME_LATE walk) and `firstWaveWindow` (line 445, WAVE_ANCHOR's window) already exist; a `pauseRun` counter like `kiteRun` (line 287) caps the spell. Two new Params fields (LADDER_CLEAR, LADDER_CLEAR_MAX; LATE_CLEAR at Params line 148 stays what it is). Variant arm: the return tower chosen away from the knights' centroid instead of the nearest. Rule 1 (defence at 250), rule 2 (KITE=2), the touch rule and TRAIN are untouched, so the first-wave behaviour of v12 (WAVE_ANCHOR's tower built while the wave is visible) is preserved by the exemption.
primary.evidence: Lost races (42), turns 50-249: 258 contact episodes, 153 (59%) began while she walked (walk_mine 79 eps/266 kd, walk_tower 38/93, walk_barracks 22/80, route_move 13/17, walk_home 1/0) and cost 456 of 598 kd (76%; 10.86 HP/game; 2.98/episode) against 79 at-tower episodes costing 69 kd (0.87/episode); won races (73): walking 248 eps/420 of 679 kd (5.75/game; 1.69/episode) vs at-tower 0.78/episode (midgame deep2.out). At equal wave size (max K250 in the episode): lost races maxK2 0.41 vs 0.07, maxK3 3.45 vs 1.22, maxK4 7.24 vs 6.00; won races maxK3 1.96 vs 1.41, maxK4 6.80 vs 1.91 (deep3.out). The wave was visible: a knight within 500 on the pre-contact turn in 151 of the 153 lost-race walking episodes; warning turns (K500>0, K250=0) median 2, mean 2.6 (0 turns in 2 eps, 1 in 24); nearest own tower on the pre-contact turn median 136; walking 60/turn she reaches touching distance before contact in 141/153 (92%) carrying 329 of 456 kd; won races 237/248 (96%); deaths 86/95 (91%) carrying 641 of 849 kd (deep3.out). The P2/P4 excess of our kd in lost races (+2.00/+2.08 HP per game vs won) is entirely walking-caught episodes: P2 lost 56 eps/140 kd (3.33/game) vs won 108/131 (1.79), P4 35/136 (3.24) vs 57/80 (1.10). Deaths (29): 849 of 1306 kd in turns 50-249 came in walking-caught episodes (losses reader: deaths are 10-57-turn sieges next to own towers, 879 of 890 HP in the last 30 turns from knights). Opponents who beat us in races keep their queen entirely within 150 of a tower in 76% of our episodes on her (kd 1.09/episode) vs 55% in races we win (3.58) (deep2.out). Code reader: over all turns 1167 of 1743 contact episodes begin while walking to a new site (2.58 kd/episode vs 2.09 at a tower). Cost side: yellow-zone turns per game 23.5 (lost) / 30.8 (won) in 6.9-8.5 spells of median 7-8 turns, on which she walks 58%/47% and tops up 36%/35% (deep3.out). My re-costing (designer/recost.py over midgame/games.json: each walking-caught episode re-priced at the pooled at-tower kd for its max K250: K1 0.00 n=115, K2 0.14 n=112, K3 1.21 n=77, K4 3.9 n=20, K5+ 16.9 n=16): saving 268 HP over the 42 lost races (6.4/game), 200 over the 73 won (2.7), 520 over the 29 deaths (17.9/game; median 9.2; 13 deaths with >= 10 HP). Arena history of the class: v08 (bound kiting) S 0.667 -> +2.46 points, v12 (meet the wave back) S 0.5716 -> +3.28, both queen-position rules the panel undervalued 2.7-3.7x; the panel's known failure mechanism for economy flags is exactly these walks (INCOME_LATE: 63 vs 47 deaths per 1000 mirror games).
primary.lossMode: Queen death first (29/180; sieges and attrition after being caught walking in the midgame, concentrated against >=20-rated opponents: 12 deaths in 58 games), HP race midgame second (the P2 and P4 excess of lost races), and the protection of the 17 won races within 5 HP; not the first wave and not the seat-1 close losses.
primary.expectedGain: Stake ~5.5 HP of knight damage per game over 180 games (988 HP re-costed), the same order as v12's arena first-wave saving (11.4 -> 6.9 HP/game) that produced +3.28 points; but distributed differently: at full saving only 3 of the 42 lost races flip (918145702 -3 with 6.1 HP saveable, 918148351 -2 with 4.8, 918152514 -37 with 38.5), because the 10 losses within 5 HP carry 0-2 walking-caught HP (they are first-wave and seat-1 losses: P1 kd >= 10 in 5 of 10, seat 1 in 8 of 10). The gain must come through deaths: 13 of 29 had >= 10 HP saveable (mean 17.9), the enemy queen stood at <= 20 HP in 10/29 and <= 30 in 19/29 when we died, so 3-6 deaths plausibly become limit games and perhaps half of those wins; plus fewer losses among the 17 won races within 5 HP (2.7 HP/game saved there). Realistic 5-9 games of 180 (+3-5 pp S), +0.4-0.7 head-to-head points at Gold scale 3.04; if the arena multiplies this class as it did v08/v12 (ratios 2.7-3.7), +1-2.5 points, i.e. around M = 2.46 and visible with two placements only at the upper end. The effect is larger where we lose: saving per game 8.1 HP (seat-0 lost races) and 29.8 (seat-0 deaths) vs 5.1 and 12.6 on seat 1; against >=20-rated opponents (11-12 waves per game) the exposure is most frequent. Not a seat-gap fix.

primary.risks: (1) The same family as THREAT_RANGE 350/450 alone (0.471/0.409 vs v05: 'reacting earlier stops her mines and walks') and KITE_RANGE 500 with v07's rule (-12 pp vs field: leaving the ladder to a faster earner). Differences: only the ladder walk is gated (kite, defence, touch unchanged), the response is a top-up at a covered own tower (useful work, not the full threat response), first-wave exemption, towers >= 2, a spell cap; and with the safety flag on, THREAT_RANGE 350/450 was within noise (0.616/0.611 vs 0.621), so the 'stop walks earlier' part cost nothing then. Still, G4 against field is the realistic failure: ~16-18 walking turns per game delayed (58% of 23.5-30.8 yellow-zone turns plus the return walks) means towers 4-6 and the second barracks ~15 turns later; the cap bounds it and the sweep must show the structure counts at t100. (2) The saving is a re-costing, not a measurement: at-tower waves passed the tower's fire first (max K250 2.23 vs 2.69), knights were assumed to head straight at her, 17% of episodes had <= 1 turn of warning; and the flips among the 42 lost races are 2-3 at full saving, so the arena gain depends on deaths converting (unmodelled: the enemy's income is 2-4x ours in 23/29 deaths and the siege continues after the pause). (3) Deaths are also economic collapses (our income <= 2 in 18/29, mines <= 1 in 21/29): pausing mine rebuilds under waves may deepen them in sieges; watch income at t150/t200 in LocalProfile and the DeathTrace. (4) The local midgame waves are well represented (field 17 waves, rival 13), so unlike v08/v12 the panel may not undervalue this rule - do not count on a 3x arena multiplier; a local S of 0.52-0.55 may be all there is, which is +0.3-0.6 points, inside M. (5) The 29% of turns spent idle-pumping stay; the rule does nothing for the first wave, the seat-1 close losses (8 of the 10 closest) or the kiting cost (kite 16.5 HP per lost race). (6) History of similar attempts: WAVE_UNTIL > 30 ('longer windows cost the midgame', field -2.3 to -5.6 pp) shows that anything delaying the ladder after turn 30 is punished by field; LATE_HOLD=100/150 (0.483/0.531 vs v08) shows that stopping walks too early loses; the spell cap and the >= 2 towers condition are the answer to both and must be swept, not assumed.

runnerUp.step: Relax TRAIN_SYNC's hold without giving up the 8-knight wave: in MainBot.train() release knights from the idle barracks when (a) the sync wait is hopeless (SYNC_WAIT_MAX: an idle barracks, gold >= 80 and (160 - gold)/max(income, 1) > N turns, N ~ 20), (b) a kill shot is on (SYNC_KILL_HP: enemy queen HP <= X, gold >= 80), or (c) the game is ending (DUMP_FROM: from turn ~230 any 80 gold trains), keeping the synchronous double release otherwise.
runnerUp.mechanism: MainBot.train(), line 216: `if (p.TRAIN_SYNC == 1 && (idle <= 0 || gold < cost)) { readySince = -1; return ...; }` - insert before it `boolean release = idle > 0 && gold >= 80 && (s.turn >= p.DUMP_FROM || s.hp[1] <= p.SYNC_KILL_HP || (cost - gold) > p.SYNC_WAIT_MAX * Math.max(1, income))`, with income summed from own mines' mineRate as play() does (lines 64-75), and when `release` is true skip the sync return so the loop at lines 223-230 trains the idle knight barracks in id order with the gold at hand (4 knights per 80). RELEASE_NEAR/readySince (lines 217-221) stay. Three new Params fields, all 0 = off (TRAIN_SYNC=1 unchanged by default), so the version-identity tests hold.
runnerUp.evidence: Over 38252 of our turns in 180 games: 8082 turns (21%) with B >= 2, 80 <= gold < 160 and no training = 48% of the 16928 turns with two barracks (B >= 2 reached in 132/180 games); 219 starvation streaks >= 20 consecutive such turns (1.22/game, 6652 turns = 17% of all), 68 of them at income <= 2, the longest 80 turns (918167057, income 1, lost race by 9), 71, 67, 67, 67, 65 (918159459, death), 55 (918167279, death); each double release waits a median 22 turns (mean 24.9, n 263) after the first 80 gold; gold float with two barracks 81 vs the opponents' 60 (losses q5/q6, code reader section G). Trainings per game: ours 7.3 vs opponents 10.9 (won 7.2 vs 10.8, lost races 8.2 vs 10.9, deaths 6.3 vs 11.6); strong Gold opponents (>=20, 58 games) 11.9 TRAIN events at 86 gold every 14 turns vs ours 7.3 at 96 every 20; Legend winners 12.7 events, gap 5 turns (opponents waves.txt). Gold at the end of lost races median 89, >= 80 in 23/42; lost races within 9 HP ending with >= 80 gold and B2: 10 (918158655 -1 with 83, 918165015 -1 with 162 and no training after t208, 918169416 -1 with 132 and none after t231, 918145702 -3 with 102, 918146673 -3 with 145, 918149783 -5/96, 918148960 -8/95, 918158656 -8/119 and no training after t150 at income 1, 918143673 -9/105, 918152187 -9/144); 4 races lost by exactly 1 HP, all on seat 1 where equal HP loses. Kill-shot turns (enemy queen <= 20 HP, gold >= 80, B >= 2, no training) 1281 in 37 games; in losses 918145702 73 turns (lost by 3), 918167279 55 (death with the enemy at 10 HP, 147 gold, 100 turns since the last wave at income 1), 918148596 16 (death, enemy 17 HP, 129 gold), 918150876 9, 918150968 6 (death, enemy 13 HP, 104 gold); the enemy queen reached <= 20 HP and survived in 37 games (23 won races, 10 deaths, 4 lost races) (losses q7). Per-gold efficiency caution: our knights 3.88 HP per 100 gold vs theirs 2.35 over 180 games (4.86 vs 1.75 in won games vs strong, 1.27 vs 2.47 in lost races vs strong), so the 8-knight wave is worth keeping when gold flows (opponents efficiency.txt).
runnerUp.lossMode: HP race last 50 turns (unspent gold at the limit, 23/42 lost races), queen death with the enemy queen low (kill shot: 3 deaths at 10-17 enemy HP with 104-147 gold), and vs strong opponents (their 11.9 waves per game vs our 7.3 at income <= 2 holds of 40-80 turns).
runnerUp.expectedGain: Upper bound 8 of 180 (+4.4 pp): 5 lost races within 3 HP with >= 80 gold left at the end plus 3 close deaths with >= 100 gold and two barracks; realistic 2-4 games (+1-2 pp, +0.15-0.3 head-to-head points) because the released 4 knights must pass T4-T9 towers and their queen stays within 150 of a tower in 76% of our episodes in the races we lose; the late dump recovers about one wave's gold per game (median 89 at the end) and can land only 1-5 HP in the last 15 turns, which is what 4 of the 42 lost races (by 1 HP) and 10 within 5 HP need. An unsized general gain from 20-40% more waves per game at low income (the cadence the strong players run) that the traces cannot price; direction of the hold cap uncertain. Alone it is below the arena's visibility (M 2.46 ~ 2.5 points), so it belongs in the same artifact as the primary or waits for a bundle.

runnerUp.p2Plan: Development sweep on seeds 1 + 397k (k < 500, both seats, in-process): arms DUMP_FROM {225, 235}, SYNC_KILL_HP {15, 25}, SYNC_WAIT_MAX {15, 25, 40} and the three combined (~8 arms + 3 controls, direct vs v12, field, rival, ~10 s per series). Which opponent shows the effect: the mirror (both sides hoard identically, so the candidate's extra releases show as HP; 91% of mirror games are races and 7.5% draws, which the dump should convert), rival (a kiting queen behind towers: tests whether 4-knight releases and kill-shot waves land), field (4 towers at 600: tests tower attrition of small waves); the dev report must show trainings per game and gold at turn 250 (LocalProfile: knight waves trained) and the per-seat split (equal-HP finals lose on seat 1, so the dump's value is seat-1-heavy). Screen on the next free block after the primary's, screen-pv3 k=7: 1007000000 + 397 i (boss the first 500); gates G0-G5; the arms change well over 10% of maps (the dump fires in most limit games), so it is a strategy change, not a targeted fix: G1 lower CI > 0.50 required. A pass: S >= 0.51 vs v12 with the lower CI above 0.50, rival and field within -2 pp, trainings +1/game, end gold < 40. Final evaluation on evaluation-pv3 k=3 (2003000000 + 397 i) only if uploaded alone; otherwise bundle with the primary into one artifact and one evaluation, since the panel undervalued army changes (v06 +0.85 within noise, v10 -0.20 after +8.4 pp vs rival) and the arena would have to judge the cadence part through the mechanism (DeathTrace gold series of the new upload: trainings per game, hold streaks >= 20 turns, gold at the end; v12 baselines 7.3, 1.22/game, 89).
runnerUp.risks: v06 adopted TRAIN_SYNC as a positive (two unsynced barracks 0.40-0.49 vs v05, with sync 0.548): 4-knight waves die on towers, so the hold cap must break only long waits (N >= 15-20 turns at income <= 2) and never the 8-knight wave when gold flows; our per-gold efficiency (3.88 vs 2.35 HP/100 gold) is the thing to protect, and a cadence arm that lowers it loses vs the mirror. RELEASE_NEAR/RELEASE_HOLD (holding the ready wave for the enemy queen's proximity) lost 0.25-0.38 vs v09 and -7 to -20 pp vs R0 - the opposite direction (more holding), so it is not evidence against releasing, but it shows the enemy queen is outside her towers' ranges on only 0.2-0.9% of turns: the kill-shot wave meets towers too. A wave spawned at t230 needs 5 turns to spawn and 9-15 to cross, so DUMP_FROM later than ~230 lands nothing; earlier dumps trade the 8-knight wave for two 4-knight ones. The kill-shot release at <= 20 HP fires in 37 games, 23 of them already won: it changes won games too. The panel undervalued army changes before, and the mirror's identical hoarding may overstate the dump's value (an opponent that spends on time has no gold to recover). Nothing here helps deaths before t225 or the first wave; no seat effect expected beyond the equal-HP finals.

result.whyNotOthers:
Second tower before the wave with a partial first pump (firstwave reader, lever 1): the largest flip pool in the close races (P1 kd >= 10 in 5 of the 10 losses within 5 HP; 8 of 24 one-tower lost races flip at the two-tower mean; within >=20-rated opponents 11/19 won with the 2nd tower before contact vs 11/39 after) and squarely the class the arena rewarded, but it is a variant of WAVE_TOWERS/TOPUP_FROM, rejected twice (S 0.45-0.47, rival -6 to -7 pp, field -3 pp, queen deaths 36 vs 18 per 400 games): the first tower stayed at 200 HP. The new evidence (the t2rel gradient 1.1 -> 11.6 HP, the kill-speed chain) is observational and confounded with the opponent's barracks timing (corr 0.77 with the contact turn), the local first wave is 60% of Gold's so the panel cannot resolve a half-strength variant, and the deaths tripwire is the only local signal. It is the right second candidate after the primary, with a 450-500 HP pump threshold swept and deaths per 1000 as the gate.

Economy interleave (3rd mine ~turn 50 after 3 towers, rebuild to 3-4 mines regardless of income < 3; opponents reader lever 2, history lever 9): the clearest 'strong players do it' gap (3rd mine at median turn 52 vs our 101; income 5.1-5.5 vs 2.6-3.0 at t100-199; unit spend 956 vs 703 gold) and the 29 deaths are economic collapses (opponent income >= 2x ours in 23/29), but four economy arms failed locally with one recorded mechanism - the walks kill the queen (INCOME_LATE: 63 vs 47 deaths per 1000 mirror games; our half's sites are towers at ladder completion) - and the panel cannot reward out-earning (field earns 8 and loses 0.92 to us; the mirror punishes any trade of early safety). The primary is its prerequisite: a mine rebuilt under an approaching wave is the walking-caught episode the data prices at 2.98 HP (walk_mine 79 episodes/266 kd in 42 lost races; rebuilt mines live a median 18 turns). Revisit it after LADDER_CLEAR, under tower cover (MINE_REBUILD_COVER), as a P1 exception judged by income at t150 and deaths in the DeathTrace, with Gold weak players' income 5-6 as the warning that economy alone does not separate strong from weak.

Tower maintenance (stop pumping the capped home tower; top up the lowest own tower; opponents reader lever 1, code reader lever 3): 39-52 wasted turns per game (24.7% of turns alive; strong Gold 20.5, Legend 10.6) and 396 vs 560 HP per tower at t200 in lost races is the largest idle waste, direction near-certain. Not chosen because the Legend winners/losers split is waves and income, not top-ups (turtles tachan and Agade with 116 and 64 top-ups won 5/11 and 4/10), because its gain runs through kill speed that the first-wave reader could only infer (ttk explains 43% of adjacency variance), and because the walks between towers add exactly the exposure the primary removes. It fits as an arm of the primary's sweep (the pause's return target = the lowest own tower) rather than a step on its own.

Rollout-based threat response over cr.core.Rules (code reader lever 1): the largest addressable HP (kite 2679 + in-reach standing/fleeing 755 + defence 581 over 180 games; 2.6 HP/game of in-reach excess alone) and the only lever for the 66% of knight damage taken during kite steps, but a new subsystem (sim adapter, candidates, evaluation, JIT warm-up that CGRunner.warmUp lacks, procCheck on both seats) with a G0 risk the cost model cannot exclude (0.05-0.3 ms per simulated turn is an estimate from loop counts, no benchmark) and no arena precedent; the greedy ladder still has cheap levers with clearer evidence. Defer until the flag-level levers are exhausted.

Seat-aware posture (DEFENCE_FWD=50 on seat 1; seat reader lever 1): the tilt is the referee's collision order (pre-fix commit 918c375 'in favor to red queen', P0 share 0.597 pooled over 64 mirror reports), so it can only be hedged; halving the seat gap is worth +0.25-0.4 Gold points, the per-seat flag effects come from one 500-map block at about 2 SE, and DEFENCE_FWD costs field -3 pp. Worth per-seat reporting in bench_pair.py now and a hedge later, not the next step.

Targeted fixes - enemy-tower-aware flight and idle pump (114 HP over 180 games, 138 of 192 enemy-tower turns at own towers, one lost race 918150190 decided by td 7), seat-aware LATE_HOLD at equal HP (5 of 360 games), ladder-target hysteresis (<= 2.4 turns/game): near-certain but tiny (<= 1-2 games of 180 together); they should ride in the primary's artifact as targeted fixes (the flight predicate at MainBot.java:134 and the idle pump at :175 are the same `nearest own TOWER` choice the primary's return target needs), not spend placements of their own (v02 +0.05, v04 +0.07, v11 +0.92 were all inside M).

LATE_HOLD for the trailing side: not a lever - in the 44 games trailing at t200 our queen lost 7 HP on 598 walking-out turns (0.16/game); the 149 other HP went at her towers, 59 of them in one game (918168604). Giants, archers, GIANT_GUARD, KITE_PULL/STAND_REACH/THREAT_RADIUS variants: all in the do-not-repeat list with no new mechanism or evidence from these readers (STAND_REACH's standing turns are 0.52 vs 0.18 per game, ~1 HP of the first-wave gap, already measured as no gain).

proposal.step: Add LADDER_CLEAR: after the first-wave window (turn >= LADDER_CLEAR_FROM, ~50, and >= 2 own towers), while an enemy knight is within LADDER_CLEAR (~500) of the queen but none within THREAT_RANGE 250, the ladder walk to a new site is paused and she walks to / tops up her nearest own tower instead, for at most LADDER_CLEAR_MAX (~15) consecutive turns per spell; kiting, the defence rule, the touch rule and the first wave are untouched.
proposal.mechanism: MainBot.play rule 5, the ladder branch at line 149 (`int target = hold ? -1 : nextSite(...)`), which today ignores knights entirely (only LATE_HOLD gates it). New gate: `pause = p.LADDER_CLEAR > 0 && s.turn >= p.LADDER_CLEAR_FROM && towers >= 2 && !firstWaveWindow(s, p) && !clearOfKnights(s, qx, qy, p.LADDER_CLEAR) && (p.LADDER_CLEAR_MAX == 0 || pauseRun < p.LADDER_CLEAR_MAX)`; when it holds, take the flight's command of lines 133-136 (BUILD TOWER on `nearest(s, qx, qy, own tower)`, adding the missing `!underEnemyTower` guard there) instead of the nextSite walk, increment `pauseRun`, reset it when `clearOfKnights` is true again. `clearOfKnights` (line 380) already exists for LATE_CLEAR; `firstWaveWindow` (line 445) is WAVE_ANCHOR's window, so the anchor tower is still built with the wave visible. Three new Params fields: LADDER_CLEAR (radius, 0 = off, as v12), LADDER_CLEAR_FROM (turn), LADDER_CLEAR_MAX (spell cap, 0 = none). Optional sweep variant LADDER_CLEAR_MINES=1: pause only when nextSite's target is a mine (the income phase).
proposal.evidence: Midgame reader (DeathTrace of v12's 180 Gold games, turns 50-249, deep2.out/deep3.out): in the 42 lost races 153 of 258 enemy-contact episodes (59 %) began while our queen walked the ladder (walk_mine 79, walk_tower 38, walk_barracks 22, route_move 13) and they cost 456 of 598 knight HP (76 %; 10.86 HP per lost race, 2.98 per episode) against 0.87 per episode for the 79 episodes met at a tower; in the 73 won races 248 of 473 episodes, 420 of 679 kd (5.75/game, 1.69/episode). At equal wave size the walking episode costs more (max K250 = 3: 3.45 vs 1.22 kd lost races, 1.96 vs 1.41 won; K250 = 4: 7.24 vs 6.00, 6.80 vs 1.91). The wave was visible: on the pre-contact turn a knight was within 500 in 151 of 153 walking episodes, with a median 2 warning turns (mean 2.6), the nearest own tower a median 136 away, and a 60/turn walk reaches touching distance before contact in 141 of 153 episodes (92 %) carrying 329 of 456 kd (won races 237/248, 335/420; the 29 deaths 86/95 episodes, 641 of 849 kd). The P2/P4 phase excess of our kd in lost vs won races (+2.00/+2.08 HP per game) equals the walking-episode excess (3.33 vs 1.79 and 3.24 vs 1.10 HP/game). The pause's cost side: yellow-zone turns (knight within 500, none within 250) 23.5 per lost race and 30.8 per won race in turns 50-249, in 6.9-8.5 spells of median 7-8 turns (11-12 spells >= 20 turns per 42/73 games); on them she walks 58 % (lost) / 42 % (won). Losses reader: 42 lost races have margins median -13, 10 within 5 HP, 18 within 10; +2/+4/+6/+10 HP to our final HP flips 4/9/10/17 of them (flip.py, strict lead). Code reader: contact episodes begun walking 1167 of 1743 over all 180 games at 2.58 kd/episode vs 2.09 at a tower.
proposal.lossMode: HP race midgame (P2 t50-99 and P4 t150-199 carry -3.9 HP each of the lost races' -16.3 mean gap; walking-caught episodes are the whole excess) and queen death (849 of 1306 P2-P5 knight HP in the 29 deaths came in walking-caught episodes, 641 with the tower reachable); also protects the 17 of 73 won races within 5 HP.
proposal.expectedGain: Re-costing the walking-caught episodes at the at-tower rate per wave size saves ~192 HP over the 42 lost races (~4.6 HP/game) and ~171 over the 73 won; +4..+6 HP flips 9-10 of 42 lost races = 5-6 of 180 games (~+3 pp S) before deaths; a third of the reachable death-episode kd (641) would be ~7 HP per death game and could turn 2-3 of the 17 siege/attrition deaths into races. Realistic 4-8 games of 180 (+2-4 pp) after the selection bias of the at-tower sample. By the Gold head-to-head conversion (scale 3.04) that is +0.6-1.3 arena points; this class (queen placement relative to knights and own towers) realised 2.7-3.7x its local S on the arena (v08 S 0.667 -> +2.46, v12 S 0.572 -> +3.28), so a step at or above the noise margin M = 2.46 is plausible but not assured.
proposal.effort: Flag on existing rules: 3 Params fields, ~20 lines in MainBot.play (gate + pause counter + the flight target), a unit test on a captured position; ~0.5 day to code, ~1 day for the arena pre-screen, development sweep, screen, evaluation, submit + two procChecks and the records (P2 machine time ~10 min per screen/eval, dominated by the boss process series).
proposal.p2Plan: (0) Pre-screen without games (history reader's lever 4): cgAttribute over replays/arena/v12/gold/upload-01+02/games with -Pbot=current?LADDER_CLEAR=500,LADDER_CLEAR_FROM=50,LADDER_CLEAR_MAX=15 and the arena_diff.py method; count games and turns where the decision changes, split by the 42 lost races / 29 deaths / 109 wins; expect it to fire in most lost races (yellow-zone walks ~14 turns/game) and record the upper bound. (1) Development sweep on seeds 1 + 397k (-PseedBase=1 -PseedStride=397 -Pmaps=500, both seats, -Pthreads=8 -PturnMs=50), each arm vs the v12 mirror, field and rival, plus the three controls (v12 vs the same): arms LADDER_CLEAR 400/500/600 x LADDER_CLEAR_MAX 0/15 at FROM=50, FROM=30 for the best radius, LADDER_CLEAR_MINES=1 (mines-only pause) as the low-cost fallback; ~9 arms x 3 series ~ 5 min. Choose by mirror S with field Delta >= -1 pp and rival Delta >= 0; report per seat (bench JSON aSeat) since seat 1 carries 20 of the 29 arena deaths. (2) Screen on the fresh block screen-pv3 k=6: seeds 1006000000 + 397 i, i < 2000 (-PseedBase=1006000000 -PseedStride=397; boss the first 500 maps with -Pthreads=3 -PturnMs=200): G0 zero candidate failures (repeat at -Pthreads=2 if host slow turns appear), G1 mirror S lower 95 % CI > 0.50 (needs S >= ~0.525 at 2000 maps), G2 boss Delta >= -2 pp (expected 0.000), G4 field Delta >= -2 pp (the binding gate: field's income-8 stream of 4-knight waves maximises yellow-zone turns, so the ladder delay shows there first), G5 rival Delta >= -2 pp (expected positive: its continuous waves and giants catch the walking queen as Gold's do). If more than one arm is screened on block 6, replicate the pick on block 7 (1007000000 + 397 i). (3) Mechanism tripwires alongside S: contact episodes begun walking and their kd per game (DeathTrace-style parse of local replays) down >= 30 % vs control; LegScan's ladder-completion turn delayed <= 10 turns and towers/mines built by t150 within 0.3 of control; mirror deaths per 1000 games not above control; LocalProfile first-wave loss and contact distance unchanged (the window is exempt). (4) Pass = G0-G5 met with the tripwires satisfied; then evaluation-pv3 k=2 (2002000000 + 397 i) once vs v12, submit, procCheck -Popp=v01 -Pgames=100 -PseedBase=5000 and -Popp=boss -PseedBase=6000, then tools/arena.py follow for two Gold placements (P1: rollback only below v12's mean 20.36 by > M). An eval S of 0.53-0.58 with the tripwires moving should be put to the user as an upload recommendation with the class's arena/local ratio stated, even though it is below the 0.60 letter.
proposal.risks: History: every earlier widening of the reaction radius lost locally: THREAT_RANGE 350/450 alone 0.471/0.409 vs v05 ('reacting earlier stops mines and walks'), KITE_RANGE 500 with KITE=1 -12 pp vs field ('leaves the ladder to the faster earner'), THREAT_RADIUS=350 over v11 -10.3 pp vs rival. Those changed the whole threat response (defence tower, flight, touch rule, kiting) from turn 0; LADDER_CLEAR changes only the ladder walk, after the first wave, with a spell cap, and sends her to a tower (a top-up) rather than away, but it is the same trade of ladder tempo for HP, and the field gate (G4, -2 pp) is exactly where v12 already sits at -1.2..-1.5 pp vs v11, so the delay can fail G4; the mines-only variant is the fallback. The saving estimate re-costs walking episodes at the at-tower rate, which is a selected sample (waves that passed tower fire first, max K250 2.23 vs 2.69), and assumes knights head straight at her, so the true saving is smaller than 192 HP. Locally the caught-walking cost is lower than Gold's (the panel's first wave costs 7.3-7.8 HP vs Gold 11.4), so a true +1.5 pp effect could fail G1's lower-CI rule (SE ~1.2 pp at 2000 maps); the arena undervaluation of this class (v08, v12) cuts both ways. Delayed mine rebuilds cost income, but in lost races rebuilt mines live a median 18 turns and 104 of 124 were built 151-400 from the nearest tower, so the forgone income is small; delayed towers/barracks against strong economies are the real cost (longer WAVE_UNTIL windows cost the midgame for the same reason). Fewer walks should lower deaths (the opposite of INCOME_LATE's 63 vs 47 per 1000), but the pause parks her at the tower nearest her, which may be a forward one; the underEnemyTower guard on that target is required. The first wave must stay exempt (FROM >= 30 or firstWaveWindow), or v12's anchor gain is at risk.

proposal.step: Bound the TRAIN_SYNC hold in MainBot.train(): release knights from an idle barracks when (a) the enemy queen is at or below SYNC_KILL_HP (~20) and gold >= 80, (b) from turn DUMP_FROM (~230) whenever 80 gold is banked, and (c) when the wait to 80 x idle barracks at the current income would exceed SYNC_WAIT_MAX turns (~30); otherwise keep the 8-knight synchronous wave.
proposal.mechanism: MainBot.train() line 216: `if (p.TRAIN_SYNC == 1 && (idle <= 0 || gold < cost)) return ...` holds every release while any barracks trains or the gold does not cover all idle barracks (160 with two). New: before that line, `boolean release = idle >= 1 && gold >= Const.CREEP_COST[KNIGHT] && ((p.SYNC_KILL_HP > 0 && s.hp[1] <= p.SYNC_KILL_HP) || (p.DUMP_FROM > 0 && s.turn >= p.DUMP_FROM) || (p.SYNC_WAIT_MAX > 0 && gold < cost && (cost - gold) > p.SYNC_WAIT_MAX * Math.max(1, income)))`; when it holds, skip the sync return and let the existing loop (lines 223-230) train the barracks the gold covers in id order. The income total already computed in play() (line 75) is stored in a field for train(). Three new Params fields (SYNC_KILL_HP, DUMP_FROM, SYNC_WAIT_MAX; 0 = off, as v12). RELEASE_NEAR/RELEASE_HOLD (hold longer for proximity) stay off; this is the opposite direction, a bounded hold.
proposal.evidence: Losses reader (gold series of ours-upload-01/02.txt; q5_out, q6_out, q7_out): over 38252 turns of 180 games, 8082 turns (21 % of all, 48 % of the 16928 turns with two barracks; B >= 2 reached in 132 of 180 games) hold 80-159 gold with an idle barracks and no training; 219 starvation streaks >= 20 turns (1.22/game, 6652 turns = 17 % of all; 68 at income <= 2, 135 at 3-4, 16 at >= 5; longest 80 turns in 918167057 at income 1, a race lost by 9). Code reader: the 80-gold-to-release wait with two barracks is median 22 turns, mean 24.9 (n = 263 double releases vs 1055 single ones); our gold float 81 at B2 vs the opponents' 60. Trainings per game 7.3 vs the opponents' 10.9 (deaths 6.3 vs 11.6; strong >= 20 opponents 11.9 events at 14-turn gaps, 86 gold each, with equal damage per gold vs us: 2.98 vs 2.83 HP per 100 gold, opponents reader). Gold left at the end of the 42 lost races: median 89, >= 80 in 23 of 42 (won races 25 of 73); the 10 races lost within 9 HP that ended with >= 83 gold and two barracks: 918158655 (-1, 83), 918165015 (-1, 162, last training t208), 918169416 (-1, 132), 918145702 (-3, 102), 918146673 (-3, 145, t201), 918149783 (-5, 96), 918148960 (-8, 95), 918158656 (-8, 119, no training after t150 at income 1), 918143673 (-9, 105), 918152187 (-9, 144). Kill-shot turns (enemy queen <= 20 HP, our gold >= 80, B >= 2, no training): 1281 turns in 37 games; in 5 losses: 918145702 73 turns (lost by 3), 918167279 55 (death; enemy at 10 HP, our gold 147, 100 turns since the last wave at income 1), 918148596 16 (death; enemy 17 HP, gold 129), 918150876 9 (lost race), 918150968 6 (death; enemy 13 HP, gold 104); the enemy queen reached <= 20 HP and survived in 37 games (23 won races, 10 deaths, 4 lost races). Midgame reader: when trailing after t200 our gold held 79 mean, one release per ~50 turns at income ~3, our knights within 250 of their queen only 3.3 turns/game.
proposal.lossMode: HP race last 50 turns (gold worthless at turn 250 left unspent in 23 of 42 lost races, 6 of them within 5 HP), queen death with the enemy queen low (3 deaths with the enemy at 10-17 HP and 104-147 gold banked), and vs strong opponents (their 11.9 waves at 14-turn gaps vs our 7.3 at 20).
proposal.expectedGain: Upper bound 8 of 180 games (+4.4 pp): the 5 lost races within 5 HP with >= 83 gold left plus the 3 close deaths with >= 100 gold and two barracks; realistic 2-4 games (+1-2 pp) because the released 4 knights must pass T4-T9 enemy towers and a kiting queen (our knights' kd per contact episode on queen-safe opponents is 1.09, 73 % of episodes with 0). That is +0.3-0.6 Gold points by the head-to-head conversion, below the arena's resolution with two placements (M = 2.46), so alone it is a tooling-measurable but arena-invisible step; its value is as a second flag in the primary's artifact (one upload) or as a gain across all games from ~20-40 % more waves that the traces cannot size.
proposal.effort: Flags on an existing rule: 3 Params fields, ~12 lines in train() plus passing the income total from play(); ~0.5 day to code with a unit test on a captured state, ~1 day of P2 (sweep, screen, eval, procChecks, records).
proposal.p2Plan: (1) Development sweep on 1 + 397k (500 maps, both seats, -Pthreads=8 -PturnMs=50) vs the v12 mirror, field and rival with controls: arms DUMP_FROM=230 alone; SYNC_KILL_HP=20 alone; SYNC_WAIT_MAX=20/30/40 alone; the best of each combined. Report trainings per game, gold at t250, enemy queen HP at the end, our deaths per 1000, kd dealt per training (bench traces) beside S; split by seat. Expected signs: DUMP_FROM and SYNC_KILL_HP >= 0 everywhere (they spend otherwise-dead gold); SYNC_WAIT_MAX is the risky arm and is dropped if field or rival lose >= 1 pp. (2) Screen on the next fresh block after the primary's (screen-pv3 k=7: 1007000000 + 397 i, i < 2000; boss the first 500): G0, G1 mirror lower CI > 0.50 (the mirror is 91 % HP races and both sides hoard identically at B2, so extra releases show directly as HP; expect S 0.51-0.54, so G1 may miss on a true small gain), G2 boss >= -2 pp, G4 field >= -2 pp (4 towers at 600 kill 4-knight releases: the tripwire for SYNC_WAIT_MAX), G5 rival >= -2 pp (its kiting queen under 4 towers tests whether late releases ever land). (3) Pass = G0-G5 with trainings per game up, end gold down and deaths per 1000 not up; then either bundle with the primary for one evaluation on evaluation-pv3 k=2 (2002000000 + 397 i) and one upload under P1, or, if the primary fails, evaluate alone and hand the user the decision with the arena-invisibility caveat stated.
proposal.risks: TRAIN_SYNC was adopted in v06 for a reason: the second barracks at gate 4 scored 0.548 vs v05 only with the sync (gates 3/5 without it 0.51/0.49), and the physics favour concentration: with towers killing at a roughly fixed rate per turn, knight-turns alive scale with the square of the wave size (8 knights ~ 2x the knight-turns of two 4-knight waves), so SYNC_WAIT_MAX with a short N would lose; N must sit above the median hold (22 turns) so that only the income <= 2 holds (68 of 219 streaks) break. RELEASE_NEAR/RELEASE_HOLD (0.25-0.38 vs v09, -7..-20 pp vs R0) shows that touching the release rule can lose a lot, though in the opposite direction. The opponents' equal damage per gold with smaller waves is observational and style-confounded (they also have 1.7-2x our income). The panel undervalued army/economy classes before and the arena never confirmed one (v06 +0.85, v10 -0.20 within noise), so even a local pass predicts little; the mirror cannot show the kill-shot value (both queens kite under six towers; mirror deaths are rare), only rival can. The endgame dump is free of strategic cost but a 4-knight wave spawned at t235 reaches a covered queen for at most 5-10 turns, so its effect lives in the 1-HP races (4 of 42 lost by exactly 1, all on seat 1) and may not register in 2000 maps.

proposal.step: Add a first-wave top-up cap: while fewer than 2 own towers stand and an enemy knight wave is visible (knightWaveComing), top up the touched first tower only while its HP is below WAVE_TOWER_HP (sweep 400/500/600 instead of TOWER_HP=700), so the queen leaves for the second (WAVE_ANCHOR) site 2-3 turns earlier and meets the enemy's first wave with two towers standing, then pumps both to 700 as today.
proposal.mechanism: MainBot.play touch rule, MainBot.java:121 (`s.stType[t]==TOWER && owner 0 && s.towerHp[t] < p.TOWER_HP && topUp`): new Params int WAVE_TOWER_HP (0 = off); the effective threshold becomes (WAVE_TOWER_HP > 0 && towers < 2 && knightWaveComing(s)) ? WAVE_TOWER_HP : TOWER_HP (a second sweep arm uses `towers < 2` alone or firstWaveWindow(s,p) as the trigger). Nothing else moves: the defence rule (:97-110), KITE=2, WAVE_ANCHOR's target choice (nextSite :432-435) and the 700 threshold once two towers stand are v12's. Chain: tower 1 is built at ~t14 and pumped 5 times to 700 (first tower HP at contact 652 vs 672 in the one-tower regime), the walk to site 2 takes 3-4 turns and tower 2 completes at t25.2 (lost races) / 24.9 (won) while the contact comes at 24.5 vs 27.3; 2-3 fewer pumps put tower 2 up before the contact, so (a) the defence rule no longer fires at contact (2 towers within THREAT_RADIUS 500) and the 2.9-turn walk-and-build under knights (1.7 HP/turn, 4.7 HP per lost race vs 1.8 per won) disappears, and (b) two towers (~450 and 200→700) fire on the knights adjacent to her instead of one 196-HP tower, raising the kill rate that governs adjacent turns (Rules.java:355: damage 3 + (range − dist)/200 per tower, one target each). Why it is not the rejected WAVE_TOWERS=2/TOPUP_FROM=2: those set `topUp = !wave` / `towers >= TOPUP_FROM`, i.e. zero top-ups before the second tower, leaving both towers at ~200 HP (range ~260), the first melted out (summed tower HP at t50 1648 → 1464/1436), the line was weaker and deaths doubled (18 → 36 per 400); at 450 HP the first tower keeps range ~380 (vs ~480 at 700) and 60 turns of melt before 200. Global TOWER_HP 400/500 also lost (0.293 vs v04, −7 pp field), so the cap is conditional on the pre-second-tower wave window only.
proposal.evidence: First-wave reader (v12's 115 Gold HP races, summary.csv + traces): lossK20 10.24 (42 lost) vs 3.42 (73 won), bootstrap diff +6.8 HP (CI +3.7..+10.3); adjacent turns (knight ≤ 60) 5.17 vs 2.07; OLS lossK20 = 1.88 × adjTurns, R² 0.89; kiting metrics identical (moves20 10.1 vs 10.3, meanNearTower20 120 vs 118). Towers at contact 1.43 vs 1.75 (MW p=0.017; one tower in 22/42 lost vs 25/73 won), coverQ 1.40 vs 1.70, contact 24.5 vs 27.3 (p=0.021), 2nd tower completes at 25.2 vs 24.9 (p=0.73), 2nd tower at/after contact in 31/42 lost vs 35/73 won. Gradient over the 176 games with a contact (q8-v12.txt): t2rel [−99,−3) n=34 won 21 (0.62) lossK20 3.5; [−3,0) n=47 won 36 (0.77) 3.4; [0,3) n=56 won 32 (0.57) 7.7; [3,99) n=39 won 16 (0.41) 12.9. Against ≥20-rated opponents: 2nd tower before contact won 11/19 (0.58), lossK20 4.3; at/after won 11/39 (0.28), lossK20 12.0 (opponents <20: 46/62 = 0.74 vs 37/56 = 0.66). Kill-speed proxy ttk = waveHP / Σ(3 + hp//200): bands 0-4 lossK20 1.1 (n=37, towers 2.16), 4-6 3.6 (32), 6-8 6.3 (16), 8-12 13.8 (22, towers 1.00); ttk explains 43% of the adjacent-turn variance. One-tower regime (24 lost / 25 won): first tower HP equal (652 vs 672), new tower completes 3.5 vs 2.2 turns after contact (p=0.008), walk turns to its site under knights 2.9 vs 1.7 (p=0.009), adjacent turns 7.9 vs 4.2. Early-barracks opponents (first barracks ≤ 8): 42/180 games, won 21 (0.50), contact 22.5, towers at contact 1.24; corr(contact, opponent firstBarracks) 0.77 — the timing is theirs, the second tower's is ours. Counterfactuals (q5/q8): lost races with the 2nd tower at/after contact → before-contact mean lossK20 2.0: 9/31 flip; one-tower lost races → two-tower mean: 8/24; lossK20 → won mean: 10/42. Code reader: defence walk+build 581 HP over 180 games (4.7 per lost race, 1.8 per won, 5.7 per death). Local reference (docs/data/exp-2026-11-05-first-wave/README.md, 200 maps vs v08): v08 meets the first wave at t24 with 1 tower; WAVE_TOWERS=2/TOPUP_FROM=2 met it at t23 with 2 towers but mean 20-turn loss 7.3/8.2 vs 7.8, tower HP at t50 1464/1436 vs 1648, deaths 36/36 vs 18 per 400; the panel (mirror t24/1 tower, field 21/1, rival 25/1) exercises exactly this regime.
proposal.lossMode: HP race, first wave, against strong opponents: the 24 lost races vs ≥20-rated opponents (within ≥20 lossK20 9.7 lost vs 3.3 won; 39 of our 58 games vs ≥20 had the second tower at/after contact and we won 11 of them). Secondarily the 6 early queen deaths (≤ t106; lossK20 mean 9.4 in death games) and the defence-rule HP.
proposal.expectedGain: Upper bound from the recorded games, rest of the game fixed: 8-9 of 180 flip (+4.5-5 pp) when the at/after lost races take the before-contact lossK20 (9/31) or the one-tower lost races the two-tower mean (8/24). In the task's lens: moving the 39 at/after games vs ≥20 (won 11, 0.28) to the before-contact rate 0.58 would be +11-12 games of 58; halving for confounding by opponent strength (corr(t2rel, rating) 0.21) gives +6 of 58, i.e. S vs ≥20 from 0.39 to ~0.45-0.49. Realistic after costs (first tower at ~450 instead of ~700 at contact, symmetric exposure 6/25 won one-tower races): +3-5 games of 180 (+2-3 pp), concentrated on ≥20 opponents (at/after bucket 39/58 of them vs 56/118 of the <20). Arena conversion: +2-3 pp against a fixed field is only +0.3-0.4 rating points at Gold's logistic scale 3.04 (dP/dR 0.078/pt at p 0.61), but both uploads of this queen-placement/first-wave class realised 2.7-3.7x their local head-to-head prediction (v12: local S 0.5716 → +3.28 placement points; v08: 0.667 → +2.46), and this step acts in the same window on the same opponents as v12, so a step at or above M = 2.46 is plausible but not assured; below ~2.5 points two placements per side cannot see it.
proposal.effort: Flag on an existing rule: one Params int, one conditional in the touch rule, a unit test on a captured one-tower position (plus a small 'second tower turn minus contact' column in LocalProfile/WaveTrace). About 0.5 day code, 1 day sweep + screen + eval, 1-2 hours tests/submit/two procChecks, ~25 min arena follow per placement; 2-3 days end to end.
proposal.p2Plan: Step 0 (minutes, no games): arena_diff-style replay of v12's 180 Gold games with the flag (cgAttribute -Pbot=current?WAVE_TOWER_HP=500) to count the games and turns where the first decision changes (expected: nearly all, at t16-19) and confirm it precedes the contact in the 31 at/after lost races. Development sweep on 1+397k (500 maps, both seats, in-process, -Pthreads=8): WAVE_TOWER_HP ∈ {400, 500, 600} × trigger {knightWaveComing, towers<2 alone} = 6 arms vs ctrl-v12 mirror, field and rival (3 control series); LocalProfile tripwires per arm: first contact turn and own towers at contact (expect 2 in a majority), HP lost in the 20 turns from contact, summed own tower HP at t50 (baseline ~1648; the rejected flags 1464/1436), queen deaths per 400 (baseline 18; rejected 36), defence BUILDs ahead under knights (FW_DEF_AHEAD/FW_DEF_LOSS). Choose the arm with the best S vs mirror and rival whose field Δ ≥ −2 pp and deaths ≤ control. Screen on block screen-pv3 k=6 (seeds 1006000000 + 397·i, i < 2000; boss on the first 500, -Pthreads=3 -PturnMs=200): G0 (0 candidate failures; repeat at -Pthreads=2 on host slow turns), G1 mirror lower 95% CI > 0.50, G2 boss Δ ≥ −2 pp, G4 field Δ ≥ −2 pp, G5 rival Δ ≥ −2 pp; G3 skipped (no `old`), recorded. Final evaluation once on evaluation-pv3 k=2 (2002000000 + 397·i) against v12. What a pass looks like: S 0.52-0.56 vs v12 (the panel's first waves cost 7.3-7.8 HP vs Gold's 10.2 in lost races, so the local effect is damped as for v12), field within −2 pp (its t21 contact is the early-barracks regime where we score 0.50 on the arena), rival ≥ 0, deaths not above control, 20-turn loss down ≥ 1 HP, towers at contact 2 in most games; field shows the effect first, the mirror decides G1. The S ≥ 0.60 recommendation will probably not be met (v12 had 0.5716); the upload is the user's decision. After upload: cgStudy/WaveTrace on the new agent's games must show the share with the 2nd tower before contact above 81/176 = 46% and lossK20 in lost races below 10.2, deaths not above 29/180.
proposal.risks: (1) A third point in a twice-rejected family (WAVE_TOWERS/TOPUP_FROM: 2026-11-05 vs v08 S 0.4675/0.4620, field −3.7/−3.4 pp; 2026-11-07 vs v11 0.4515/0.4470, rival −5.9/−7.3, field −3.0/−2.5). The recorded failure (first tower at 200 melts, line weaker at t50, deaths ×2) is exactly what the 400-600 cap avoids, and the sweep's tripwires detect a repeat; but it may turn out the second tower's timing was standing in for the opponent's timing, as the 2026-11-05 README concluded for Silver. (2) The gradient is partly opponent quality (early barracks = stronger: corr(t2rel, rating) 0.21, corr(contact, rating) −0.22); all flip counts hold the rest of the game fixed; the symmetric exposure is 6/25 won one-tower races. (3) The first tower at ~450 covers ~380 instead of ~480: if the anchor site is far she can be caught between two weak towers; TOWER_HP 400/500 as global thresholds lost badly, so the cap must stay conditional and the 600 arm is the safe fallback. (4) The panel's waves are smaller than Gold's (local one-tower 20-turn loss 5-7 HP vs 10-12 on the arena), so a true gain may show locally as S 0.52-0.55 and fail the 0.60 recommendation; conversely G4 was nearly binding for v12 (−1.49 pp) and could reject a true gain. (5) Arena resolution: M = 2.46 with two placements hides steps under ~2.5 points; a 1-point step needs ~13 placements per side.

proposal.step: Gate the midgame ladder walk by knight proximity (LADDER_CLEAR): once two towers stand and the first-wave window is over, when an enemy knight is within LADDER_CLEAR (sweep 400/500) of the queen and an own tower exists, replace the ladder's walk to a new site by the rule-4 flight to the nearest own tower (BUILD TOWER there, a top-up on arrival) for at most LADDER_CLEAR_MAX consecutive turns per spell, then resume the ladder.
proposal.mechanism: MainBot.play rule 5 (`cmd == null` → nextSite + RoutePlanner.plan, MainBot.java:148-164, and the INCOME_LATE branch :165-175): new Params ints LADDER_CLEAR (radius, 0 = off) and LADDER_CLEAR_MAX (spell cap); gate `towers >= 2 && !firstWaveWindow(s,p) && !clearOfKnights(s, qx, qy, p.LADDER_CLEAR) && spell < LADDER_CLEAR_MAX` → `nearest(s, qx, qy, own TOWER)` BUILD (the flight of rule 4, :133-136), counter reset when clear. clearOfKnights (:380) exists and is used today only by LATE_CLEAR; firstWaveWindow (:445) is v12's. THREAT_RANGE 250, the defence rule, KITE=2 and the touch rule are untouched, so contacts are fought as today; only the decision to start or continue a walk to a new site while a wave is 250-500 away changes. Optional second arm: the own tower farthest from the knights' centroid instead of the nearest. Different mechanism from the primary: a proximity gate on walks in turns 30-249, not a top-up threshold before the second tower.
proposal.evidence: Midgame reader (DeathTrace of v12's 180 Gold games, command classes validated against CgStudy: own-tower BUILD counts match in 315 of 360 game-sides): lost races (42), turns 50-249: 258 contact episodes, 153 (59%) began while she walked (walk_mine 79 episodes/266 kd, walk_tower 38/93, walk_barracks 22/80, route_move 13/17), costing 456 of 598 kd (76%; 10.86 HP per lost race; 2.98 per episode) vs at-tower episodes 79 episodes/69 kd (0.87 per episode) and building-touch 19/48; won races (73): 248 of 473 episodes, 420 of 679 kd (5.75 per game; 1.69 per episode). At equal wave size (max K250): maxK3 3.45 kd walking vs 1.22 at a tower (lost), 1.96 vs 1.41 (won); maxK4 7.24 vs 6.00 and 6.80 vs 1.91; maxK2 0.41 vs 0.07. The wave is visible first: turns with a knight within 500 but none within 250 right before contact median 2 (mean 2.6; 0 in only 2 of 153), nearest own tower on the pre-contact turn median 136, tower reachable at 60/turn before contact in 141/153 (92%) carrying 329 of 456 kd (won 237/248, 335/420 kd; deaths 86/95, 641/849 kd). P2 (t50-99) and P4 (t150-199) excess of our kd vs won races (+2.00/+2.08 HP) equals the walking-caught excess (P2 3.33 vs 1.79, P4 3.24 vs 1.10 HP/game). Cost side: yellow-zone turns 23.5 per lost race (12% of turns 50-249) in 6.9 spells of median 8 turns, 11 spells ≥ 20 turns in 42 games; on them she walks 58% (walk_mine 25%, route 12%, walk_tower 11%, walk_barracks 6%, walk_home 4%) or tops up 36%. Mine treadmill: 157 mine losses after t50 in 42 lost races (3.74/game), 124 rebuilt, 104 of them with the nearest own tower 151-400 away; walk_mine-caught episodes 266 kd = 6.3 HP per lost race. Code reader (all 1743 episodes pooled): begun while walking 1167 at 2.58 kd/episode vs 330 at a tower at 2.09 (self-selected). Lost-race opponents are the queen-safe turtles (their queen within 150 of a tower through 76% of our episodes; our kd per episode 1.09 vs 3.58 in won races; income equal, inc_100 3.0 vs 3.0), so our own HP is the lever against them.
proposal.lossMode: HP race midgame (P2 and P4 each −3.9 HP in lost races; margins: 10 of 42 lost within 5 HP, 18 within 10) and queen death (849 of 1306 P2-P5 kd in the 29 deaths came in walking-caught episodes); vs strong opponents: 24 of the 42 lost races are against ≥20-rated turtles whose queen does not bleed.
proposal.expectedGain: Re-costing the walking-caught episodes at the at-tower rate per wave size saves ~192 HP over the 42 lost races (~4.6 HP/game) and ~171 over 73 won; uniform +4..+6 HP flips 9-10 of 42 lost races, but by the per-game distribution saving half the walking-caught kd flips 2 and all of it 11 (skewed: median 7.5, mean 10.9; 12 of 42 with 0), so the centre is ~5-6 games of 180 (+3 pp) before the delay cost, plus an unquantified share of the 29 deaths (641 of 849 reachable kd). Against ≥20 opponents proportionally ~3-4 of 58 (+5-7 pp of S there). Realistic +2-4 pp after the ladder delay; arena conversion as for the primary (+0.3-0.5 points at a fixed field; the queen-under-knights class realised 2.7x locally predicted for v08), so a visible step is possible only if the death effect adds to the race effect.
proposal.effort: Flag on existing rules (~15-25 lines: two Params, a gate before the ladder branch, a spell counter) plus one local metric ('contact episodes begun while walking' and their kd, from LocalTrace/DeathTrace with the midgame scratch classification, or a cheaper count of BUILD-new turns with K500>0 and K250==0); 0.5-1 day code and metric, 1 day sweep/screen/eval, same artifact steps as the primary.
proposal.p2Plan: Step 0: arena_diff-style replay of the 180 Gold games with LADDER_CLEAR=500 to count the gate's firing turns per game by outcome class (expected ~13 walking yellow-zone turns per lost race; must fire in most of the 42 lost races and 29 deaths). Sweep on 1+397k (500 maps, both seats): LADDER_CLEAR ∈ {400, 500} × LADDER_CLEAR_MAX ∈ {10, 20, 0 = none} = 6 arms (+ the away-from-centroid variant if an arm passes) vs ctrl mirror, field, rival. Metrics beside S: walking-caught episodes and their kd per game, HP per contact episode, towers and mines standing at t100/t150 and ladder-completion turn (the delay cost), deaths per 400, LegScan walking turns. Screen on screen-pv3 k=6 (1006000000 + 397·i; k=7 if the primary used 6), gates G0-G5 as in P2; eval once on evaluation-pv3 k=2 (or 3). Pass: G0; G1 lower CI > 0.50; field Δ ≥ −2 pp — the gate most at risk, since field's 17-18 waves per game make the yellow zone large and a cap of 10-20 turns is expected to be necessary; rival Δ ≥ −2 pp; walking-caught kd per game down by at least a third with towers at t100 within 0.3 of control. The mirror (8-knight waves crossing the ladder, 91% HP races) shows the HP effect; field shows the delay cost; rival (continuous pressure, giants) the death effect.
proposal.risks: History of early-warning flags: THREAT_RANGE 350/450 alone 0.471/0.409 vs v05 ('reacting earlier stops her mines and walks more'); KITE_RANGE 500 with KITE=1 −12 pp vs field ('leaves the ladder to the faster earner'); THREAT_RADIUS 350 over v11 −10.3 pp rival. This design differs (only the ladder walk is gated, the destination is an own tower top-up, exemptions for towers < 2 and the first-wave window, a spell cap), but G4 may still bind and the cap may blunt the gain. The at-tower comparison is self-selected (those waves passed a tower's fire first: max K250 2.23 vs 2.69), the command classes are heuristic (213 of 76,504 turn lines differ from CgStudy) and the reachability check assumes knights head straight at her, so 4.6 HP/game is a stake, not a measured effect. The mine treadmill may only be delayed: the exposed mine walk resumes after the spell (a MINE_REBUILD_COVER companion would be a second mechanism and a second screen). The delay cost (towers/mines later, ladder complete after t121) is unquantified; the code reader rated pre-contact positioning small on the pooled numbers (2.58 vs 2.09 kd/episode), so the lost-race-only stake may overstate it.

proposal.step: Build KITE=3, a Rules-based rollout controller for the queen while an enemy knight is within SIM_RANGE (start 300): every such turn simulate about 27 candidate commands for SIM_H=5 turns with cr.core.Rules (the 24 kite headings re-aimed each turn, stand/top-up on the touched own tower, BUILD on the nearest own tower, the defence rule's site, and the current rule ladder's own output), score = our HP lost minus SIM_KILL x enemy knight HP removed by our towers, with KITE=2's hard constraints kept (end under own tower cover, outside enemy tower range), and replace the rule ladder's command only when the best candidate beats it by >= SIM_MIN_GAIN (1 HP). First deliverable: the sim adapter (seat from the start corner, player swap, a prediction test on the 180 recorded Gold games, a micro-benchmark of Rules.resolve on recorded crowds) plus the controller replacing only kite() and the under-threat stand/flee block; the defence rule and pre-contact decisions follow as phases 2-3.
proposal.mechanism: Replaces MainBot.play rule 2 kite() (C:/Disk_D/Programming/CG/cg-contest-code-royale/.claude/worktrees/bot-analysis-next-step-f64e02/src/main/java/cr/bot/current/MainBot.java lines 242-284: one sites-only Physics.queenStep per heading, knights scored where they stand, +5 gain, cover required) and the under-threat top-up (lines 117-122) and flight (lines 133-137); phase 2 the defence rule (lines 97-110). New code: a rollout class in cr.bot.current with a preallocated pool of GameState copies (GameState.copyFrom, lines 108-141), Rules.resolve per simulated turn (src/main/java/cr/core/Rules.java: processCreeps 233-265 moves enemy knights at CREEP_SPEED 100 in 5 sub-steps toward our queen with collision pushes, dealDamage 312-317 hits within 20+30+5 for KNIGHT_DAMAGE 1, actStructure 347-363 fires each tower at the closest enemy creep for 3 + (range - dist)/200, barracks spawn when barrProgress reaches CREEP_BUILD_TIME 5), the enemy queen WAITs, our TRAIN from train(). Prerequisites named in docs/PLAN.md: a seat field in InputReader (start corner: player 0 at (200,200), 180/180 traces agree) because Physics.load (lines 121-128) resolves collisions in the order P0 creeps, Q0, P1 creeps, Q1 and the build conflict goes by turn parity, so on seat 1 the sim state is built with players swapped. The deadline already reaches play() (Bot.play deadlineNanos; Referee.java line 138 passes turnMs, CGRunner line 47 the 40 ms budget): used as a safety cut only, with a deterministic work budget (candidates x horizon) as the primary control so bench games stay reproducible. CGRunner.warmUp (lines 92-127) gets a knights-adjacent copy that runs the rollout, so Rules is JIT-compiled inside the 300 ms warm-up. Flags: KITE=3, SIM_RANGE, SIM_H, SIM_KILL, SIM_MIN_GAIN.
proposal.evidence: Where the HP goes (code reader, trace_levers section 1, trace_quirks D-E; 180 Gold games): 8615 contact turns of 38252 (47.9/game, 23%); knight damage 4038 of the 4156 HP lost; kite steps 2679 HP (7325 turns, 0.37/turn, 0.97/turn when the nearest knight is <= 120), standing/fleeing in reach 755 HP (291 turns at 2.55-2.63/turn), defence walk+build 581 HP (541 turns at 1.0-1.3/turn). Lost races vs won: kite 16.5 vs 9.4 HP/game, defence 4.7 vs 1.8, in-reach stand/flee 3.5 vs 1.5; deaths 33.8 / 5.7 / 14.8; margins median 13 (10 of 42 within 5); per game, half the kite HP >= the margin in 8 of 42 lost races, stand+defence in 8 of 42, kite whole in 22 of 42. After a kite step a knight is still within 250 next turn in 5754/7292 (79%): the step itself sheds nothing (knights 100 vs queen 60), the fight is decided by tower kill speed and pack tightness. First wave (firstwave reader q7/q8, 115 races): lossK20 = 1.88 x adjacent turns (R2 0.89); adjacent turns 5.17 vs 2.07; damage rate at contact median 6 vs 10; ttk explains 43% of adjacency variance; towers hit one creep per turn, so the fight's position relative to the towers (damage 3 at the edge, up to 5-6 near a 700-HP tower's centre) and the number of covering towers set the kill rate; the static rule has no such term. Collision order matters (seat reader toy port of Physics/Rules: a standing queen takes 19 HP as P0 vs 36 as P1 over 12 turns from 4 knights; fleeing cuts 48 -> 26 and 25 -> 18): kite() cannot see it, Rules reproduces it. Cost model (code reader): 5 collision passes x E(E-1) sqrt pairs, E = creeps + 2 + nSites (<= 24); creeps alive median 12 at t25 (max 16), 2-4 at t50-200 (p90 8-11, max 20) -> 4.4k-7.8k pairs per simulated turn typical, 15k worst, estimated 0.05-0.3 ms (unbenchmarked); 27 x 5 = 135 turns per real turn -> 7-40 ms worst, against a free budget of about 30 ms (50 - 7.7 measured max - 10 margin) -> the work budget or a local sub-state (entities within 600) must be sized by the benchmark. Everything the horizon needs is in the local view except enemy gold and the enemy queen's intent: barracks progress (InputReader lines 81-84), tower HP/range, creep HP; spawns within 5 turns are exact. History (history reader): the two largest arena steps were queen-under-knights changes undervalued locally (v08 KITE=2 S 0.667 -> +2.46; v12 anchor 0.5716 -> +3.28); the one that left cover (v07 KITE=1, S 0.680) gave -0.71.
proposal.lossMode: HP race first wave and midgame (the 47.9 contact turns per game; 54.8 and 28.5 kd/game against >= 20-rated opponents), queen death by siege (9) and attrition (8): in the deaths' last 10 turns 182 of 290 turns were kite moves (13.7 HP per death); vs strong opponents, who stand more (MOVE 0.67) and lose 0.70 HP per contact turn while we kite 85% and lose 0.47 over nearly twice the contact turns.
proposal.expectedGain: Addressable per game: the in-reach excess (2.63 and 2.55 vs 0.97 HP per turn) = 473 HP / 180 = 2.6 HP; the defence walks 3.2 HP (581/180), of which perhaps a third is avoidable; 10-20% of the kite pool = 1.5-3 HP; together 3-5 HP/game, concentrated in lost races (24.7 HP/game in the three pools vs 12.7 in won races). Per-game flips (the code reader's bounds, not a uniform addition): 6-10 of the 42 lost races (= 6-10 of 180 games, +3-5 pp win rate) plus 2-4 of the 17 siege/attrition deaths, so +3-6 pp realistic, +8 pp upper. Local: S 0.55-0.62 against v12 on the mirror is the expectation (v08's kiting rewrite scored 0.667 against v07; v12's 3.5-HP first-wave saving 0.5716 against v11). Arena: the class's arena/h2h ratio was 2.7-3.7 (v08, v12), so a visible step (>= M 2.46) is plausible but not assured; the plain logistic conversion gives only +0.4-0.8 points for +3-6 pp at Gold scale 3.04. The structural payoff is the road: the defence build-or-not (phase 2), the pre-contact retreat and the second-tower timing (phase 3, horizon 10-15 for 3-4 macro candidates), enemy-tower avoidance and the idle-queen tower maintenance become candidates or evaluation terms of one controller instead of a new flag family each, and the same adapter gives the project its first opponent-motion model.
proposal.effort: New subsystem, 3-5 days. Day 1: adapter and tests (seat, player swap, enemy queen WAIT, preallocated states), a prediction test replaying v12's 180 Gold games through InputReader (cgAttribute-style) and comparing the 1-turn and 5-turn predicted HP loss and knight positions with the recorded next turns, and a micro-benchmark of Rules.resolve on recorded crowds (t25 crowds of 12-16 creeps). Days 2-3: controller, warm-up extension, unit tests on captured death windows (918143669 t201-211: 11 top-ups under 7-10 knights at 4-5 HP/turn; 918168604 t197-234; 918150876). Day 4: development sweep. Day 5: screen. The artifact grows little (Rules, Physics, GameState already ship); procCheck on both seats repeats as for every artifact.
proposal.p2Plan: Development sweep on seeds 1 + 397k (500 maps, both seats) against v12, field and rival: arms SIM_H 3/5/7 x SIM_RANGE 250/300/400 x SIM_KILL 0/1 (1 = 25 knight HP, one kill, worth 1 queen HP) with the cover constraint hard, plus one arm with it soft (3-HP penalty) to reproduce v07's failure deliberately; alongside S report HP per contact turn, in-reach stand turns, deaths per 1000 maps, LocalProfile first-wave loss and contact distance, LegScan max play() time and simulated turns per real turn (a queenSteps-like counter), and the number of deadline cuts (must be 0). Pick one arm by S with no G4/G5 regression. Screen on fresh block screen-pv3 k=6 (seeds 1006000000 + 397 i, i < 2000; boss on the first 500 at 3 threads, 200 ms): G0 no slow turn > 50 ms, with the work budget sized so the worst recorded crowd takes <= 15 ms on a performance core (3x margin for the laptop's efficiency cores and CG's single CPU; a 2-thread repeat with identical games settles host noise as before); G1 mirror lower CI > 0.50 on 2000 maps (the HP-race sensor: 91% of mirror games reach turn 250); G2 boss >= -2 pp; G4 field >= -2 pp (17 waves per game, the most contact turns; the opponent where v08's kiting showed +13.7 pp); G5 rival >= -2 pp (the kiting, giant-playing death sensor). The effect shows on the whole panel because all three send knight waves. A pass looks like: G0 clean, S >= 0.55 with HP per contact turn down >= 15% and deaths per 1000 not up, field delta >= 0, max play() <= 20 ms in LegScan. Then the final evaluation on evaluation-pv3 k=2 (2002000000 + 397 i) against v12, procCheck -Popp=v01 (seeds 5000) and -Popp=boss (6000) with no SLOW line, and the user's upload decision (recommendation S >= 0.60; the class's arena record argues for an upload at 0.55-0.60). Pre-screen for free before coding the controller: an arena-replay diff (cgAttribute with the flag over replays/arena/v12/gold/upload-01 and -02) counting the turns and games where the rollout's command differs, split by the 42 lost races, 29 deaths and 109 wins.
proposal.risks: (1) G0 and tail latency: CG runs one CPU with an unknown JIT state, and Rules has never run inside the artifact's warm-up, so a cold rollout at the first contact (turn ~24) could exceed 50 ms; mitigations are the warm-up extension, the deadline cut, LegScan tail times and procCheck on both seats. (2) Model mismatch: the enemy queen WAITs in the sim (she MOVEs on 44-51% of turns; within 5 turns only her top-ups matter), enemy TRAINs are unknown (they spawn >= 5 turns later), and the stdin order of creeps may differ from the referee's internal order used in collision resolution; the prediction test decides, and a biased simulator would be worse than the static rule. (3) Horizon myopia: one 700-HP tower needs about 24 turns to kill a 4-knight pack (one target per turn), so 5 turns see only damage dealt; a large SIM_KILL can make her stand to farm tower damage and bleed, the v07-type artefact the stand-still local opponents reward; keep the cover constraint hard and the kill weight small in phase 1. (4) Panel bias: field never kites and rewards any mobility, rival kites and plays giants in 85% of its games, the mirror over-weights races; the panel predicted +1.0 for v07 and the arena gave -0.71, so after an upload the arena mechanism metrics (share of contact turns at own towers, 90% for v12; HP per contact turn 0.47) must be checked, not only the placement. (5) Reproducibility: a time-budgeted search makes repeated bench runs produce different games; hence the fixed work budget with the deadline as a counted safety cut. (6) The history of per-step tweaks is flat (STAND_REACH 155 neutral, KITE_PULL 200 neutral, KITE_MAX nothing): the rollout's new content is exact knight motion, collision pushes, tower damage rates and the stand-versus-step trade; if the development sweep shows <= 2 HP/game of saving, the subsystem still pays as the platform for phases 2-3, but that is a decision for the user after day 1's prediction test and benchmark, before the controller is written. (7) Effort creep: phase 1 stays in-contact only; pre-contact triggers and the defence rule are later phases.

proposal.step: Add an open-loop wave model, knightEta(s): the turn when the enemy's knights (the ones alive, at 100 per turn, and the ones a visible enemy knight barracks will spawn in 5 - progress turns) reach our queen or the tower she would hold, and gate two existing decisions on it: (a) in the first-wave window, walk to the second tower site only if its build completes >= ETA_MARGIN (2-3) turns before the ETA, otherwise pump the first tower (ETA_PUMP_TO=500 instead of 700) and hold at it; (b) after the window, abort a ladder, mine or barracks walk and return to the nearest own tower that covers her when the ETA is shorter than the turns to finish the walk plus one build plus the return, resuming when no knight is within 500 (clearOfKnights). This is the structural alternative when the rollout subsystem is not affordable: the same prediction, done as arithmetic instead of simulation and search.
proposal.mechanism: New rule (about 80 lines) in MainBot.play before the ladder (rule 5, lines 148-163) and in the touch rule's top-up threshold (line 121, TOWER_HP replaced by ETA_PUMP_TO while towers < 2 and a wave is coming): knightEta over s.cx/cy with Const.CREEP_SPEED[KNIGHT] = 100 and the enemy knight barracks' barrProgress/barrTraining (InputReader lines 81-84 set them from p1; CREEP_BUILD_TIME 5), the walk time from the existing MainBot.walkTurns / Physics.queenStep or RoutePlanner's plan length; flags WAVE_ETA=1, ETA_MARGIN, ETA_PUMP_TO, ETA_RETREAT=1, ETA_SPELL_MAX (a cap per spell like KITE_MAX). It differs from the rejected WAVE_TOWERS/TOPUP_FROM (static tower counts that skipped all top-ups, so both towers sat at 200 HP and the first one melted, summed tower HP at t50 1464 vs 1648, deaths doubled) by the time criterion and by keeping the first tower's HP; it differs from LADDER_CLEAR or KITE_RANGE 500 (distance triggers; v07's 500 lost 12 pp against field by leaving the ladder) by acting only when the wave arrives before the walk can finish, on the 2-3 turns of warning the traces show. No collision simulation and no candidate search; phase 3 of the primary would replace it with simulated candidates, so nothing is wasted if both are built.
proposal.evidence: First wave (firstwave reader q7/q8/q9, 115 races of v12's 180 Gold games): second tower turn minus contact <= -3: lossK20 1.1 HP, 24% lost (n=21); [-3,0): 2.7 HP, 21% (28); [0,3): 6.9 HP, 36% (39); >= 3: 11.6 HP, 63% (27); the contact turn is the opponent's barracks timing (corr 0.77; mean contact 18-20 for a barracks at turns 1-5, 24-26 at 7-8, 27-28 at 13-16), while our second tower completes at turn 25 in both groups (25.2 vs 24.9): a fixed schedule meets an opponent-driven arrival that the input announces (the enemy barracks' progress p1 every turn). One-tower regime (24 lost / 25 won): the new tower completes 3.5 vs 2.2 turns after contact (p=0.008), 2.9 vs 1.7 walk turns under knights; against >= 20-rated opponents the second tower before contact won 11/19 vs 11/39 at or after. Bound the TRAIN_SYNC hold in MainBot.train(): release knights from an idle barracks when (a) the enemy queen is at or below SYNC_KILL_HP (~20) and gold >= 80, (b) from turn DUMP_FROM (~230) whenever 80 gold is banked, and (c) when the wait to 80 x idle barracks at the current income would exceed SYNC_WAIT_MAX turns (~30); otherwise keep the 8-knight synchronous wave.

Add a first-wave top-up cap: while fewer than 2 own towers stand and an enemy knight wave is visible (knightWaveComing), top up the touched first tower only while its HP is below WAVE_TOWER_HP (sweep 400/500/600 instead of TOWER_HP=700), so the queen leaves for the second (WAVE_ANCHOR) site 2-3 turns earlier and meets the enemy's first wave with two towers standing, then pumps both to 700 as today.

Gate the midgame ladder walk by knight proximity (LADDER_CLEAR): once two towers stand and the first-wave window is over, when an enemy knight is within LADDER_CLEAR (sweep 400/500) of the queen and an own tower exists, replace the ladder's walk to a new site by the rule-4 flight to the nearest own tower (BUILD TOWER there, a top-up on arrival) for at most LADDER_CLEAR_MAX consecutive turns per spell, then resume the ladder.

Build KITE=3, a Rules-based rollout controller for the queen while an enemy knight is within SIM_RANGE (start 300): every such turn simulate about 27 candidate commands for SIM_H=5 turns with cr.core.Rules (the 24 kite headings re-aimed each turn, stand/top-up on the touched own tower, BUILD on the nearest own tower, the defence rule's site, and the current rule ladder's own output), score = our HP lost minus SIM_KILL x enemy knight HP removed by our towers, with KITE=2's hard constraints kept (end under own tower cover, outside enemy tower range), and replace the rule ladder's command only when the best candidate beats it by >= SIM_MIN_GAIN (1 HP). First deliverable: the sim adapter (seat from the start corner, player swap, a prediction test on the 180 recorded Gold games, a micro-benchmark of Rules.resolve on recorded crowds) plus the controller replacing only kite() and the under-threat stand/flee block; the defence rule and pre-contact decisions follow as phases 2-3.

Add an open-loop wave model, knightEta(s): the turn when the enemy's knights (the ones alive, at 100 per turn, and the ones a visible enemy knight barracks will spawn in 5 - progress turns) reach our queen or the tower she would hold, and gate two existing decisions on it: (a) in the first-wave window, walk to the second tower site only if its build completes >= ETA_MARGIN (2-3) turns before the ETA, otherwise pump the first tower (ETA_PUMP_TO=500 instead of 700) and hold at it; (b) after the window, abort a ladder, mine or barracks walk and return to the nearest own tower that covers her when the ETA is shorter than the turns to finish the walk plus one build plus the return, resuming when no knight is within 500 (clearOfKnights). This is the structural alternative when the rollout subsystem is not affordable: the same prediction, done as arithmetic instead of simulation and search.

LADDER_CLEAR: after the first-wave window (turn >= WAVE_UNTIL=30 or no enemy knight barracks) and once >= 2 own towers stand, when an enemy knight is within LADDER_CLEAR=500 of the queen but none within THREAT_RANGE=250, replace the ladder walk (nextSite/RoutePlanner and the INCOME_LATE walk) by BUILD TOWER on the nearest own tower not inside an enemy tower's range (walk there, top up on arrival) until no knight is within 500 or the spell exceeds LADDER_CLEAR_MAX (~12 turns); kiting, the defence rule and the touch rule stay as they are.

Relax TRAIN_SYNC's hold without giving up the 8-knight wave: in MainBot.train() release knights from the idle barracks when (a) the sync wait is hopeless (SYNC_WAIT_MAX: an idle barracks, gold >= 80 and (160 - gold)/max(income, 1) > N turns, N ~ 20), (b) a kill shot is on (SYNC_KILL_HP: enemy queen HP <= X, gold >= 80), or (c) the game is ending (DUMP_FROM: from turn ~230 any 80 gold trains), keeping the synchronous double release otherwise.
